I've been playing this game since the 90s, and I still enjoy each playthrough. The characters, mechanically, are not terribly different from one another, but character progression and equipment choices offer enough customization of playstyle to give variety to the usual JRPG grind.
The story is an epic, and although there are key characters, no one character is the star of the show- and no one character is perfect; most express their fears and flaws at some point in the telling of the larger story. Some snippets of dialogue aren't critical to the storytelling, but the fact that different characters being in your party at different times may change the dialogue slightly is a nice bit of flavor that is lacking from some (former and current) blockbuster games.
The iOS release that was ported to Steam isn't my favorite visual style of FFVI, but the potential for modding in the community has me quite interested in following the Steam version. All in all, this work has endured the test of time quite admirably.

SOMA is an intense and thought-provoking existential sci-fi horror game set in an oppressive underwater research facility. Frictional Games once again prove why they're masters of first person horror by presenting us with a disturbing experience that not only tops the Amnesia series but pushes their own uniquely-engaging brand of storytelling forward.
We've seen environments like Pathos II in games before but SOMA somehow manages to feel fresh with every note, broadcast, machine, room, corridor and enemy existing to both unnerve us and deepen the story. The game looks and sounds fantastic and each environment is highly interactive and packed with interesting details. Players who enjoy exploring every inch of the game world will be greatly rewarded and players who simply want to run to the finish will experience a roller-coaster of a ride.
It's unfair to judge SOMA purely as a horror game as the story is perhaps its finest asset. The plot is extremely deep and disconcerting and forces us to consider the concept of 'self' whilst encountering a host of strange machines and creatures. There's absolutely no filler in here and Frictional are keen to ask us to make odd decisions in horrible situations whilst constantly questioning our own choices.
A great sci-fi story, an engaging game world, a fantastic horror experience and a framework for just how far we can go with videogames as a storytelling medium, SOMA is certainly worth your time and money.

Soma is Frictional Games' newest game. It's their first game after Amnesia: The Dark Descent.
The game follows survival horror tropes, and as like Amnesia, you can't fight your enemies. Encounters with enemies are based on a system in which you have to turn off lights, hide in closets etc.
So if you're looking for an experience akin to Dead Space / Bioshock this will not be your thing. If you're looking for experiences similiar to Penumbra, Amnesia or Outlast this will be your thing.
Compared to the previous games mentioned Soma is very slow. The story progresses slowly and the overall the scares are built with time. There is some shock value also, but not nearly to the extent of something like Outlast. (That's a good thing)
The story of this game is something I've never seen in a video game. It's a weird mix of The Matrix and Ex Machina, but it totally works in the context of the game. They clearly went all out.
Overall I would recommend Soma to anyone who is interested in slow horror like Amnesia. It's a good follow up from Frictional Games and deserves your money. It's not a full priced game even, which is great.

IF YOU DON'T LIKE STORY DRIVEN GAMES OR LIKE TO RUN THRU CONTENT WAITING TO BE JUMPSCARED THIS GAME WILL BE PRETTY MEDIOCRE TO YOU.
That's my only execption to the recommendation that I make.
I'll agree with most reviews here:
1) the Story was amazing and kept me interested all the way. The feel when you discover the apocalipse is undescribable... It gets more under the skin when you find out that even the "survivors" are no more.
Two questions never left me be: "What's the real human nature" and "What's the purpose of existence in this world". The second one hit me harder, since I personally think "purpose" is defined by the person itself, It really bothered me how I always chose to turn off/kill the creatures in my way, which showed that my opinion wasn't as strong as the feeling "I would like to be turned off in its/his/her place";
2) The puzzles were very good IMO. Seemed one with the story. Penumbra influences were clear with some pitches of Alien Isolation, well done;
3) the Graphics were very good and envirolments well design. Light effects and the vision were impressive. Highlight for me was the deepsea visual it was AWESOME.
Creatures also were well designed, their wierd anatomy (nothing is scarier than the unkown) and different behaviours made most enconters fresh.
4) the Sound was out of this world. Really. It mashes all the experience together makes it more "organic" (believable). Voice actor performed very convincinly.
That said here is what I think could be improved:
a) Maybe the creatures should impose themselves more like obstacles to player progression. In my experience It didn't feel like they were a part of the ride, they seemed like a "optional" thing. Why? Cause I could run from them or avoid them pretty easily. Prolly if this part were made a bit better (harder) some horror fans (which like jumpscares and run thru content) would be more satisfied with the game.
I think a model to be followed here is Alien Isolation. The Alien is always present and It is an obstacle to player progression a bully.
If in the next game you guys nail the Story, audio and graphic quality with horror elements that impose more to the player you'll have the best horror game of all time.
b) I can understand the choice of not letting the player die too much. Instead you choose to handcap the player progression (vision and movement).
This was another option that IMO made this game less good to rushers: Lack of ingame punishment. If the player doesnt't feel punished by his mistakes or lack of attention, there's no pression. If this kind of player doesn't dig into the story and ambient elements this game will be a calm walk.
Bottom line: some horror fans that don't dive into story elements need another elements to feel challenged by the game, which IMHO would be more imposing creatures AND more punishment with players mistakes.
This were my 2 cents.

A simple action-adventure (with a limited RPG elements) with okay graphics, decent animations/sound, and a story from a child's POV. Controls are usually fine, and the game engine physics allows you to kinda wallrun if you jump towards a wall, which looks pretty funny. You can manually resize the game window, which is pretty handy.
Dungeons are fun enough to run through, but don't expect too many innovations- it sticks to a very basic formula. You go room by room, killing all enemies, breaking all pots, opening all chests, and doing simple puzzles. At the end of a dungeon, you get one item to return to the monster village (which then unlocks more dungeons). You might even notice it reuses rooms a couple times in different dungeons with a little twist (like flipped).
There are several minigames of varying quality. The most annoying is the 3v3 football/soccer one in which you can't control/dribble the ball, only hit it with attacks. If you try to play it like a normal sports game you'll be frustrated since most likely you'll never score a goal yourself. Just do locked-on jump attacks on the ball and it'll automatically hit it towards the enemy goal instead of straight ahead. You can just play defense and your AI ally will eventually get enough goals in.
Enemies aren't too hard, and you're free to switch between the three elements (for enemy weaknesses) and your head gear (for your resistances) in combat to finish them quickly. Bosses are pretty straightforward and in normal difficulty can be brute forced with healing items if you just want to run up and slash.
If you enjoy this basic formula, a childlike/innocent story, and the visuals this game might be for you. Otherwise, there are other action-RPGs that might be more tailored to your tastes.

Picked this up when I saw it on Steam! I did not realize they even planned a port for it. the PSP is starting to age and I am glad I still get to play classics (ish) like this on a more powerful system.
First off, having played this to the bone on the PSP, I can address its content immediately and compare what I've experience in the PC port afterwards.
+Solid action platformer
+Engaging enemy variations (strategy cap must be on!)
+RPG/level elements
+Replayability
+Decently lengthed game (especially for completionists)
+Fun and memorable characters (most are some just add some spice to the setting)
+Great voice acting for the time period of its deveopment (espesially since its in english)
+Made by Falcom, the genius behind the Ys franchise and the early Legend of Heroes games
-Simple camera mechanics sometimes lag behind gameplay
-New Game + requires collecting items again (not necessarily a bad thing, it does add a "replayability" aspect than a God Mode)
-Completing the game 100% will take a lot of effort, some skill and back tracking
-Some progression aspects are vague (rarely)
Overall, this game was one of the rare gems in the PSP treasure trove along the lines of Ys: Napishtim (which Xseed is porting to PC this month), or Ys: Felghana (already on Steam!) in regards to genre. It has a very straightforward story that engages you with plot twists--sometimes unnecessary--that let you keep going. The leveling and gear system here also works well, not to mention customization options with all the different costumes. Gear levels carry over to NG+ given that they need to be reacquired. The characters are memorable and all play a role in the game. One particularly elusive cat, will definitely pique most players interest. The enemies are given so much variety throughout the game that merit a different approach everytime a new foe is encountered. Some can even get a tiny bit frustrating(-ly fun).
For the PC port, I think they only really need to adjust their config menu. Add support to the d-pad and R analog stick, for example. (I prefer using d-pads for platmormers like this because I feel more in control of direction. hehe) Video options also show little difference to me, noted that I'm not too keen on major graphic settings other than fps, res and vsync. I think that this game is aged and simple enough that the settings they give do not entirely make the game too noticably different on medium settings or ultra. The PC port, specifically, feels odd with the PSP type camera system, but perhaps it is more a complex fix than I give it credit for.
The games negatives aren't exactly negatives, per se. Nothing that holds back from enjoying the game entirely, but clearly show how this game was really built for more simpler control inputs. Noting that I play this game, like most of mine, using a gamepad.
If you've played this before, pick it up! If you haven't, PICK IT UP!! Otherwise, pick it up anyway! :D

is an action platformer for PC released on 2004 by Nihon Falcom Corporation, of Ys and Trails in the Sky fame. Following the adventures of Parin, a small girl who moves to a mining town with her grandpa due to her parents being away for work, she finds out that there are no children to play with in the small town. That is until she finds a portal to a different world where monsters, whom only children can see, live.
The game is very reminiscent of old PSX era 3D platformers. You'll jump to platforms, kill baddies, break things to find goodies and all that good stuff. The combat in Gurumin, as expected from seasoned developer Falcom is pretty fun and fast. Parin can attack with her drill, roll, divekick into enemies and soon enough unlock special abilities performed by doing motions on the controller. The RPG branding in this game is pretty misled, the only customization you'll be able to do on Parin is equip her with different (silly) hats to add passive effects and unlocking new moves. Each hat can be upgraded with "Junk" that falls from armored enemies and can be upgraded up to three times. Your drill levels up as you connect Critical Hits (landed by hitting in sync with the music's rhythm) or dig in patches of dirt and levels down when you are damaged, similar to Cave Story. Eventually you'll gain access to elemental parts that can be imbued into your drill and as expected some enemies will be resistant or weak to certain elements.
As far as difficulty goes, Gurumin never offers much of a challenge save for some bosses here and there that require a bit more strategy. The game is pretty straightforward but offers plenty of things as unlockables to add replayability. You are evaluated after every stage based on your performance on time, enemies defeated, jars broken and chests found and these award you medals. Notably, Gold and Platinum Medals are used to unlock special items, so some practice might be needed for those stages. There are also some items that when given to monsters, not only allows you to watch some hilarious exchange of dialogue but also unlocks wallpapers. After beating the game in any difficulty, a new one is unlocked as well as an outfit for Parin. Difficulties range from mind-numbingly easy to sadistically hard.
Graphically, Gurumin looks pretty well despite the dated 2004 graphics. Using a cute cel-shading that reminds one of
and a colorful palette that manages to not be a complete eyesore, the game oozes charm. However, this being one of Falcom's first full 3D games there are places where the quality isn't high, most notably in character animations during cutscenes which (even in current Falcom games) look robotic and unnatural. Musically the game delivers, it's not Falcom Sound Team jdk's finest work but it has a nice slew of catchy tunes, stepping into awesome territory as the game progresses into its final moments. Mastiff has only offered us the English dub for voices which is pretty mediocre to be honest, however as a player of the original japanese version I didn't find this to be much of an issue as the original voice acting was pretty amateurish itself.
The worst part of Gurumin, however lies in the technical aspects. Not much has been changed from the original 2004 release in terms of configuration, so we're offered a tight handful of graphical and controller options. The keyboard control options in particular is pretty restrictive offering only a handful of keys enabled for use, while it is doable to play the game with a keyboard a controller is highly recommended. The game is also hard locked at 30 FPS, same as the original japanese version with currently no workaround to make it work at a higher framerate, only a handful of (apparently not working) antialiasing and texture filtering options and only a small number of screen resolutions. Those used to XSEED's improvements in other Falcom PC games might be disappointed here.
As previously mentioned, the game is reminiscent of early 3D platformers... even the bad parts. The camera has a habit of moving itself into awkward positions, the physics engine works kinda iffy sometimes making you miss some easy jumps, there is no lock-on for enemies, even though you can adjust the camera to focus the enemy it doesn't work as expected sometimes. Controller inputs are also somewhat loose, as I found myself executing a Downward Lunge accidentally even though I never input the full circle motion required for it.
In spite of its shortcomings, Gurumin is still a charming and lovely experience that is just plain fun to play, and a rather lengthy one for a platformer clocking at around 8-12 hours of gameplay, not including the optional dungeon and finding some hidden knick-knacks. If you don't mind the limited configuration options, Gurumin is worthy to be picked up during a sale at least and guaranteed to satisfy any platformer fan.
EDIT: Unlocks appear not to be working. Hold on to your money for a while.

This was a fun little game. Nihilumbra is a 2D platformer that focuses on puzzle solving and spans 5 main areas, each of which consists of several stages. Each area introduces a new colour, which then becomes important for the solutions of puzzles in that area. For example, blue colour makes you slide along as though on ice, making you travel faster and jump further, green makes you bounce, brown makes you stick to walls, and so on.
I found the use of unique effects of each colour for puzzle solving to be a pretty cool mechanic that made puzzles interesting. Some colours even had multiple uses. For example, the red could burn the enemies, but it could also make fireflies glow brighter, hence illuminating darker areas.
The overall execution is very nice. The art and the music are especially stunning. Though the narrator's voice was a bit offputting at times and seemed a tad repetitive. Worse yet, if you died and returned to a checkpoint, the narrator would say the same quote again, even if he already said it earlier. And having to redo the puzzles you've done already just to get to the one you died on was also frustrating.
The game in general is worth playing if you like puzzle games, though the story mode is pretty short (took me about 3 hours to complete). After the story mode, you unlock the void mode, which is significantly harder and might not be for everyone, as you go through the same areas except with much more complex puzzles and more enemies, often pitting you in very vulnerable situations where you're bound to fail or die dozens of times before you succeed. So if you're on the fence and unsure, best to get the game when it's on sale. The story mode is worth it alone.
I would certainly like to see more similar games from the developers, because this one definitely had the right idea.

I bought this on the recent sale, and it is easily worth the full price for any strategy game lover. Where to start? I feel like I have to explain first, and foremost, what this game actually brings to the table. I am a lover of RTS and the turn-based strategy staples. I am also a lover of MOBA type multiplayer. I think it is important to note that the single player and multiplayer are almost two different games. They follow the same mechanics, but the single player feels almost like a career-mode where matches are linked together and unlocking perks for your chosen CEO along the way, while the multiplayer brings the most intense purely competitive gameplay that I have seen in years. Even in the games where I get trounced I am left feeling like I have more grasp on the game than before, and know this is a benefit for future games.
The reason this game is amazing to me is that there isn't a "meta" strategy to just win. This game requires a fluid strategy with the goal being to acquire competing companies by buying a majority stake. The goal is to develop supply chains that produce goods from basic to higher tier products made out of those base resources. One players actions in the first minute may require a fundamental shift in the strategy of another. This is way more than the generic paper-rock-scissors we see in a lot of strategy games, or simply any competitive game.
This brings us to the learning curve. If you have played a strategy game before 2000 then the tutorial is amazingly informative. For those new to the RTS genre (I see this game mostly as such), it will feel unfair to lose repeatedly at first. These losses are the growing process of grasping the mechanics. As you start you will realize you have been handed a toolbox with a dozen tools, and winning only comes when you know the time and place to use each tool. You will lose suddenly and realize that you simply forgot about one aspect, but the oversight is just one more learning opportunity. Players that go into a situation saying I want to always use this specific company faction or believe they have an infallible one-size-fits-all strategy will lose, and quickly at that.
I have seen reviews where the reviewers say that the game is about speed and not strategy. The speed simply comes with playing and understanding the resources needed for expansion. Again for RTS players think of the first time you grasped how to expand bases quickly to reach end game in the likes of Warcraft, C&C, AoE. Once you know how to upgrade quickly then it is time for strategy to kick in. The tutorial games are difficult at first, but only because the learning curve of these levels want you to graduate with the knowledge of the mechanics before letting you loose.
The multiplayer wait times can be on the long side for FFA(4-player) matches, but the game allows you to do the 'Daily Challenge' scenario or a skirmish against the AI while you wait. That game will be autosaved before entering the multiplayer match. 1v1 matches have much shorter wait times. I think 1v1 is easier (may be different for each person), but FFA is where the real fun lies.
If you like single player more than Patron DLC is a must (adds aspects to campaign mode), and I think the Ceres DLC is definitely worth it as well (adds new resources, new power supply, new map type).
TL;DR:
Anyone that wants to be in control of their own game strategy on the fly in quick, highly competitive matches with RTS elements must own this game. A lot of gamers lately want their hand held by a cut-and-paste guide that will ensure they win a high amount of the time. Thankfully this is not that game, this game requires one to like facing challenges.
Edit: I'm now over 115 hours in, and this review was from about 15 hours in. I had only seen the tip of the iceburg. This game continues to amaze and I am still learning more with every game 100 hours later.

Writing a review for a classic title such as this feels rather redundant. I've played through various versions of this title from the original Playstation game, the GBA version, to this port. My favorite of all of them is still the GBA version, but this version has it's merits.
The reason why many find dissatisfaction is in the way the graphics were done in this port. The character designs for the most part are subpar, though I do like Bartz design, and also threaten to reveal certain plot points. There's also major tearing in the background and level designs, where you can actually see the pixels where they "modified" the stages. Various issues with controllers and other computer-related problems have occured while playing the game as well.
However, this is still the same story as before. It's using the updated GBA script with what sounds like the original Playstation music. As someone who has since lost her copy of both the game and the Game boy Advance, this port is what I had been hoping for. It is a nostalgic trip that I come back to again and again.

Pros:
1. The gameplay is fun, good to kill time and quite satisfying

Cons:
1. Very grindy, but not terrible
2. Whenever you try to kill a boss or enemy for exp, items, whatever, a higher level player can just swoop in and take the kill you probably wanted badly
3. Ships are really expensive. Unless you're fine with playing for a while and saving up to buy a ship, you're gonna have to buy it, hence making this game basically a pay to play. And when you do find a good ship, they end up nerfing it and you can't refund
4. Missions that are given to you sometimes involve killing an enemy or boss that is way too hard to kill, and can just one-shot you most of the time

10. Some missions are just grind fests. For example, The Ultimate Poison Part 5 makes you kill 888 ice-moths
Even though there are WAY more cons than pros, I still am reccommending this game. It is fun to play, and is pretty good overall.

I've been staring at this game since early alpha debating whether to buy it and finally bit the bullet.  I should have done this when it was first offered.  If you like the idea of a super fast paced game of domination that is different every time, buy this.  Every thing you do can be countered by your opponent, and likewise you can counter everything your opponent does.  actions per minute helps but isn't necessary; playing smart is infinitely more important.  Every action your opponents take will have direct consequences on your products and prices, can you figure out what the demand is going to be?  will you be caught in a competitive market with your profits steadily dropping?  Will you just dominate through overproduction of your opponents?  Will you lock down technology that lets you skip their profit margins and go directly back into your product?  Will you find a niche that no one is competing in and exploit it?  There are so many paths to victory or defeat in this game and its so simple yet complex at the same time.  If you are still on the fence watch a few lets play videos until you get the gist of it, then figure out how the patent lab, off world market, blackmarket etc. make it infinitely more intricate.  Minutes to learn, lifetime to master.  Excellent game design.

I've had this game since it was in beta, and was the first game I ever streamed on Twitch. Even when its graphics, characters, and music were sketchy as hell, the core gameplay was enticing enough for me to spend HOURS learning how to read the stock market, fake out other players, and understand how I lost.
This isn't Civ. This isn't a turn-based strategy or another RPG (both of which are my more usual fare). It's a game that's like... like chess with the stock market on Mars. There are a limited number of moves/buildings/resources and only one way to win--but infinite strategies to get there.
If you like chess-on-steroids while you're competing against the clock, you'll love this. If you're looking for a narrative or something closer to Civ, go elsewhere--but keep this in your library when you're ready to stretch your brain a bit.

I'm going to say right now, the negative reviews on this game are completely idiotic.
This game is literally what DBD should have been. It's fun, frantic, horrifying, and hilarious all at the same time.
Lets just get right into it with pros and cons
Pros!
-Playing as Jason is FUN AS HELL, as long as you make it that way. You can either kill everyone in 5 seconds or you can actually have fun and toy with people since you're basically unstoppable
-Playing as counseler is tons of fun as well. Aside from what the negative reviewers are saying its VERY possible to survive in this game. Game rewards you for helping your friends, setting up escapes, and stalling jason.
-NO ♥♥♥♥ING RANKS OR OP PERKS, Unlike that game DBD perks in this game aren't game breaking in anyway. They have a positive and a negative effect for them. (Less likely to stumble while running +15% but make more noise by 9%) something like that.
-No cheese in this game. It's pretty hard to cheese jason without actual thought behind what you're going to do after.
-Graphics are actually really well done.
-Animations are nice and polished. (you know since devs used full mocap for everything)
-Shooting jason with a shotgun is insanely satisfying.
-Proximity voice chat!
-Audio in this game is amazing, everything is really tense when its quiet, and hectic as all hell when jason is around chasing you or someone near you.
-Tons of ways to stall jason, traps, beating him, shooting him, using a special something to distract him for a little bit, radios, firecrackers, and the like.
-Tons of ways to kill counselers, on top of the 15 some odd executions you get with your bare hands, each jason has 3 executions with the weapon he has, as WELL as all the enviromental kills
-Keyboard controls i personally think work perfectly and have no issues with them. have not used gamepad.
CONS!
-Not much content, 3 maps, reused textures for those maps, but the  layouts are entirely different so thats something.
-Stuff is level locked. Nothing important, some characeters are locked behind level caps i believe the last thing you unlock is at level 13-15. so not too much.
-Calling tommy jarvis doesn't really help as much as it should
-Price tag. (i am actually perfectly okay with spending 40 dollars on this as it is  TON of fun to play) Other people have a hard time enjoying something if they cant afford it i guess.
-Campaign and Bot matches aren't in the game YET.
-Cant rebind controls (as of now) though if you're okay with the control scheme dont complain about it.
OVERALL
This is great indie game thats tons of fun to play, alone or with friends. If you are okay with a 40$ price tag then you should definitely pick this up. It's only going to get better from here as devs plan to fully support the game with content.
Campaign and bots should be added in sometime in summer from what i last heard.

-Create your very own dream vehicle from models roughly resembling real life cars
-Race around various tracks included in some of the maps
-Finetune your suspension in terms of ride height, spring stiffness, track width and more
-Install dozens of mods, some of them with incredibly high quality
-explore the detailed maps, find all the secret passages
- ... and quite a lot more!
As far as I can tell, the game runs very smoothly until you spawn to many cars (6 on my PC), it looks great even on lower graphical settings and has a FoV-Slider so TotalBiscuit will be happy. Extremely high velocity/force impacts don't look that great, but are still a accurate depiction of what would happen to a similar car (despite some parts clipping through others bended textures/Jbeams etc...) Aside from that crashes in this game are almost worthy of next generation car testing. E.g. brake thermals and cooling liquids and other stuff gets simulated.
Stuff you should know:
Though it's possible to play this game with a keyboard you will have a hard time controlling especially the stronger/older car variants. This is because a keyboard limits you to full throttle, none at all and hard braking. The best option would be a steering wheel,but a contoller also works just fine. The game has force feedback compatibility in general, however this doesn't apply to my ancient  SpeedLink wheel.
There is a experimental replay feature, but it's still a buggy mess. I guess it will be fixed very soon, look out for that.
Which brings me to my next point: The game gets updated regularly (a major content patch comes out every 1/2 months, of high quality, with bugfixes, optimisations and like I said, content). BeamNG also has a very nice and helpful community.
What I don't like as of now:
-The sounds (which have been described as placeholders by the devs) are plain horrible, but they said that they hired a
sound effects guy in the last devblog.
-The particles are not all that detailed and plenty compared to real car crashes
-The game tends to bug out sometimes, nothing major, but it's there and its annoying

[This review only covers single-player campaign.]
This entry in the MoH series is EA's blatant attempt to copy Call of Duty. Unfortunately, the game does a lot of things wrong.
- Lack of information. Where are we fighting? Why do we even fight and shoot everyone in sight? Who are the enemies who are simply labeled as "bad guys"? One mission even puts you in a helicopter with machine gun and Hellfire rockets and your objective is to kill all "bad guys" on the ground who desperately try to fight back with AK-74 rifles.
- The player is part of an overpowered squad which takes down literally hundreds of "bad guys" while listening to praise from squad mates such as "Nice!", "Good kill!", etc. The result is almost as off-puting as
- however, in case of MoH it is probably unintentional.
- The campaign is a bunch of missions glued together with almost no story.
- The game is way too easy, even on the highest difficulty; squad mates are immortal and can deal with anything.
- A.I. is simply idiotic. Majority of enemies don't use cover and just stand in the open. Many of those who are smarter and decide to go for cover decide to constantly switch between standing, crouching and lying.
- Hitboxes don't make sense. 5 bullets in the neck? No problem! 2 bullets in foot? Impossible to survive.
- Player's character is unable to climb or do any action unless told to do so.
- "Press F to receive ammo" (by asking a squad mate) doesn't work 95 % of the time. However, if it works, the squad mates can provide anything - rifle or machine gun bullets, sniper rounds, rockets ...
- The campaign only takes 4-5 hours to beat (on the hardest difficulty).
- The gameplay is smooth and feels good; the same with weapons.
- Graphics & physics. Mountain ranges provide beautiful vistas and destructible parts of environment make the shootouts interesting.
- Contrary to everything mentioned above, 2 missions (out of 10) were well designed and felt pretty great (especially when compared to the rest). Specifically, they were missions 5 (Belly of the Beast) and 9 (Neptune's Net).
Great game, if a bit short.

Overall a good game for the price.
Suggestions;
* A city or town map fight would be good.
* An option to randomize weapon spots so a player can't just camp at the same weapon spawn location.
* Have the bad guys try some flank maneuvers instead of bee lining it to the character which often results in their funneling into an easy slaughter.
* Have the bad guy spawn points move about a bit. Example, drop one or a few and then move to another spot.
* A bit longer reloading time for the minigun..right now it loads faster then a pistol.
* The RPG should do more damage I think.
* A 40mm grenade launcher like the M79 would be wicked to have.
* "Inventory" hotkey that pauses the game so you can pick a weapon, see the ammo, etc..
Good, but very weird in a good way, variety of bad guys.. and some shoot back which definitely increases the challenge..;-)
For those that don't live just for playing online against often rude players.. this game  is a good and cheap alternative.

I followed this game for a long time, and I have tried to give it the chance it deserved, but Ubisoft took something that could have been great and ruined it because they refuse to use dedicated servers and instead use peer to peer networking. This was probably the biggest mistake they could have made with this game. For those who don't know, peer to peer networking means that one player is the host of the match and if he/she has bad connection, everyone suffers. And if the host leaves or gets disconnected, then the game will kick everyone out of the game. Now, I'm not saying peer to peer is a bad way of having online multiplayer, but in a heavily combat focused game like this, it is awful. The game itself is great: good, unique combat that feels good, a pretty engaging story, and fun PvP when it works. I'm not even sure what ubisoft did to let this happen. I played this game's closed beta and open beta and these network problems were still there before release. Ubisoft has the ability to fix this if they would stop being cheap and just use dedicated servers. I literally have not been able to join a single 4v4 game because one host can't handle the weight of 8 different connections so it just disconnects me 5-25 seconds into the match.
TL;DR:
If Ubi fixes the servers I would give this game a 9/10, but since its multiplayer is basically unplayable, it only gets a 4/10 from me since the main focus of the game can't even be used.
GG Ubisoft, you made a good game, but you screwed up the part that is arguably the most important, and you're just elongating your track record for being a company who cares more about money than its consumers, I hope you know that.

For those potential buyers trying to make sense of this game:
If you're still with me, then know this is a
business sim set in a near-future Mars colonization setting.
The premise is that Humans are colonizing Mars (Yay!) but the overwhelmed colonies have privatized their resourcing operations to Earth coprorations (Oh no!).  That's where you come in - You're basically the Mars regional manager for a corporation trying to get a foothold on the planet, before the competition can woo the colonies away from you.
PROS
This is fast-paced day trading coupled with supply chain management.  On Mars.  The sheer amount of stuff you can customize for each run (patents, optimization, contracting/hiring staff, etc.) allows for a myriad of strategies you can try against the different competition and conditions in each colony.  With campaigns, you have to plan and budget ahead of time for the future, because the competition gets starts to get fierce after you win several colonies.
CONS
A little pricy for what the gameplay actually is, which is basically a ledger and a map of resources to manage.  The graphics and sound are only a few rungs higher than what you'd expect on a mobile app.  Would recommend getting it on sale.
SIMILAR GAMES
I can't really think of any.  Factorio is more about the tactics and design of supply chain management and there isn't a market.

Disclaimer: This is gonna be one heck of a ride ladies and gentlemen, buckle up, get some popcorn and enjoy your read.
0. Introduction
Fun game. Very Fun. Great Mechanics unique concept. And i'm not gonna jump on the "omg peer 2 peer" or "omg ubisoft another bad game lol xddddd" bandwaggon, Because i am gonna give my actual opinion on this, and leave some feedback that Ubisoft may or may not take. (yes i know you guys are like: but ubisoft is a bad company they won't improve the game) You never know if this is gonna be the shining beauty of ubisoft, this could be the game that changes their reputation. So let's get rooooight into the review.
1. Mechanics
7/10
Mechanics are unique, they're cool, and the concept is realistic, and done very well.
But there is a problem with them, and i will get into that later.
I really like the blocks, i really like the heavy and light attacks and the different combos that can really seperate a tutorial freshmen, and a multiplayer grinder. As well as how there's a pretty much a counter for every strategy.
But here's the problem. First, no one is perfect, that's obvious. But the thing is, if a player would eventually practice so much that his or hers reaction time was lets say near flawless, there would be almost no counter except for carefully placed unblockable area attacks. Here's my example.
Person A has perfected reacting. Person B is going in to attack. Person B starts off with throwing some strikes at person A; which person A obviously blocks. Person B notices that Person A is a defensive player, and tries to guard break. Person A counter guard breaks with the help of its reaction time.
Person B tries to do a ram, but person A avoids, Person B tries to land an unblockable area attack but person A avoids, person B attempts to throw person A off with a guard break combo, but person A counter guard breaks or avoids. Person B must therefore wiggle person A down with heavy attacks or slowly push person A off a ledge with heavy attacks.
2. Story
8.5/10.
Now my computer is not perfect, but it's above average. It can run 'High' Graphics on most of the games that are above 10 Gigabytes.
Therefor, the cutscenes are stunning, the in-game cutscenes are super impressive considering the little amounts of customization you have at the beginning of each chapter.
So i got a 60+ FPS High Quality Smooth and Slick experience in both types of cutscenes and in-game combat.
The story missions were exciting, challenging, fun realistic, innovative, creative and done wonderfully.
A problem i have is that sometimes when my internet freaks out (It's been a little unstable lately) the story mode seems to glitch and lag a little. Which is weird considering that it's a fully singleplayer experience (unless the samurai chapter has some tricks up it's sleeve)
And i've seen a lot of other reviews saying it's ridiculous how the singleplayer story mode requires an internet connection.
3. Multiplayer
4/10
It has it's good sides, it has it's many bad sides. Now, THE PEER 2 PEER- Nah i am just kidding. I am gonna give actual opinions on the subject.
Now i don't know if this is caused by p2p, but on gamemodes that have Medium and High Traffic, they take a lot of time to find an instance. And when you do find one, it's either full by the time you load in or it fails, but if you do get in it takes too much time for people to join and the instance shuts down.
But in-game it's great. It's fun fighting actual good and experienced players. Sometimes they kick your♥♥♥♥♥ sometimes you kick their♥♥♥♥♥ And it all comes down to how well you know your Hero.
4. Heroes
6.5/10
The Heroes are done okay in my opinion, but their differences and versatile and adaptable playstyles make it so much better. I mean, when you are a warden and completely stomp on a Nobushi or Orochi it feels so good frying their weaboo♥♥♥♥♥
The heroes look stunning, they look unique they are unique in playstyles and customization and their taunts are funny and also unique to some degree.
5. Balancing
2.5/10
Although this is some of my favourite games, the balancing is all sorts of messed up. The reason i give it more than a 2.5 is because this is balancing in general and not just talking about the unbalanced ones.
The vanguards and most of the second and fourth heroes are pretty balanced. Some more unstable in that if you mess up, you're gonna get smashed, and if they mess up you're gonna smash. And others are more fair, balanced and passive.
But the Samurais are too OP, it's been said before but i'll say it again. The only somewhat balanced Samurai is the Kensei.
The Orochi has too many hidden attacks, too many fast attacks, attacks that are too fast in general and its avoid attack is so annoying.
The big fat one deals way too much damage for a light attack and if it gets lucky and hits a heavy on you, the only thing you can do is prey.
The big fat pig will just break you on it's bag, toss you into a wall/off a ledge and beat you down with heavy attacks. Or it will non stop guard break you and beat you down with lights or unblockables.
The Nobushi has TOO much range. TOO good retreats and why did it get a poison? How is that fair? But i believe that the Hype generated for this game will change itself and with the help of Ubisoft we can fix this game.
6. Bugs
6.5/10
There are a lot of problems, especially with weeb pig.
The reason why i give it a low score is because of 1 problem i mentioned in the beginning of this review.
It's blocking, now the blocking is fun, it makes you feel MLG and it's so epic blocking barrage after barrage. But, so many blockables faze right through your blocks, sometimes the slighest move of your mouse will make your stance dramatically change. And if you're out of stamina it's still too easy to block.
Now i would add a suggestion bar, but i feel like if Ubisoft reads this carefully enough they will see what they need to improve on.

A fun, super-charming 3D action game.  You get a bunch of different headgear to serve as equipment, with some shared and some unique benefits, like the gas mask protects from poison gas, goggles from water damage, etc.  Headgear can be leveled up to improve their effects and add new ones like damage reduction and damage multipliers. You only have a drill as a weapon, with three exchangeable elemental parts but they all play the mostly the same aside from some enemies being weak to different elements.  There's a bunch of special moves you unlock through buying parts for your drill and they're all easy enough to perform.
The gameplay is separated into short dungeon crawls, with no area being any longer than twenty minutes or so.  Each area has two regular stages, then a boss, then two more "secret" stages that can be unlocked by solving some type of riddle.  There's enough stages to give the game a solid length and it ends before becoming tedious.
Being a 3D action/platformer, the camera control can be a bit finicky, especially since the game doesn't an option to map the right analog stick on the controller as camera control, instead defaulting to the shoulder bumpers.  You get used to it after a while though, and it's never too big of a problem.  The first platforming section with water is probably the worst in the game for various reasons, so don't fear if you flub it up a bunch.  There's not a ton of precise platforming here.  Otherwise, the game controls well.  Parin moves fast and attacks fast.  If you've played previous Falcom games, you already know they know how to do fast-paced action really well.  The music and sound effects are good, too, as you'd expect from a Falcom game.
As for the story/voice acting stuff, it's bleh and generic for the most part, but the lead character has a good dub and the game has a ton of little charming touches that overshadow the problems.  NPC dialogue is pretty fun and you can examine a bunch of stuff in-game and Parin will comment on it.  The game's artstlye has aged really well, so even though it's technically unimpressive, the game never really looks bad due to a strong stylistic foundation.
For those that like to replay/master rank games, there's a ton here, like multiple unlockable difficulties and extra headgear/costumes to find and even a secret playable character.  It you don't care about that kind of thing, it can be safely ignored without hurting your experience.
As for the port, it's a bit of a mixed bag at this point.  I'd played it 1080p, and there was a constant white line along the top of the screen, only really noticeable during the letterboxed cinematics but it's there.  There's also appears to be issues with new game+ stuff unlocking incorrectly, as I had one of the extras upon starting up a new game+, but it seemed to have disappeared forever after quitting the game and reloading.  I imagine these types of bugs will be fixed in the near future.
In short, if you're looking for a fast-paced, light-hearted 3D action game, Gurumin is what you're looking for, especially considering how few likeminded games like this there are available on PC.

Pros:
+Fun, easy to learn controls
+Easy to navigate
+Easy to jump into for short periods of time
Cons:
-Loot system punishes weaker and newer players
-Higher level players are incentivized to wipe out low level areas
-Starts to feel like a cash grab after a short time
-Ships are way too expensive for how often good ones are nerfed
-Ships are non-refundable even if their stats are drastically changed
At first I really liked this game, it seemed like something I could really get into for just a few minutes at a time and enjoy, and the people in the game are actually generally helpful for a F2P MMO.  My problem lies in the systems that the developers use to force very high level players into very low level areas for timed or daily quests, and they also seem to base loot rights on who does the most damage to a target rather than who hits something first.  This creates a situation where you as a lower level player will spend a long time trying to kill a difficult ship with a bonus loot on it, only to have a severely overlevelled player swoop in, hit it with a giant explosion once, and reap the rewards to which you no longer have any right.  This could easily be remedied with allowing whoever hits something first have loot drop as well as whoever damages it the most.
This is on top of their aggrivating habit of releasing an incredibly expensive and overpowered ship (which can be bought with either real money, or a several month time investment to save enough of the purchasable currency through exploration and timed missions), waiting for most of the playerbase to purchase the ship, then completely nerfing it to be worse than the next overly expensive ship they plan to release, making the game feel like a constant cash grab if you wish to compete.
If not for the mistakes in the looting, nerfing, and cash store systems, I would recommend this game.  The gameplay itself is simple and fun, but the frustration involved in dealing with the flaws of this game prevent me from doing so.

This game is actually really cool. If you aren't super into rpg's, don't be discouraged to buy this game. A game that this plays very similar to would be (to a very small extent) Kingdom Hearts. But comparing this game to another doesn't do it justice. Some might complain that this is just a flatout port of the psp game. They would be right. But here's the thing. There was nothing wrong with the psp game to begin with, so what do you really need to change? Imagine this like a PS2 launch game that wasn't. It gives me the same vibe I got playing Ratchet and Clank or the aforementioned Kingdom Hearts. If you grew up with the PS2 (which sounds crazy to guys in their mid 20's), then I totally think you'll feel the same. Now this game is not neccesarily polished. There are some (kind of hilarious) graphical hiccups such as what looks like parkouring ever corner you see when not grabbing on a ledge. But this game has some wicked cool things about it. For example, you have a seperate currency system for upgrading equipment that you get from battling monsters. The game rewards you for searching around for money by giving you medals depending on how many jars and chests you get. You can even spend those medals on items that will help you out later on. There's also a pretty cool combat system. Although the controls can be a bit wonkey with my Xbox 360 controller, for the most part you can get the job done pretty well. The fact that your drill levels up instead of you kind of makes this game feel less and less like a traditional RPG (which I normally don't like). The voice acting is good. That is except the main character. You can obviously tell she's new and some points makes you want to cringe with her acting. She's not terrible though, just below average. The music is good but kind of repetitive. It didn't get on my nerves though, but if you showed me a song from the game and didn't say it was from the game I'd probably just think it was from some random rpg. Overall, I say get this game if you are a fan of non-traditional rpgs and games like Kingdom Hearts. Either way though, I'm not complaining. I got it for free because I met the requirements for the greenlight campaign.

I fondly remember the days of playing this game in my parents house as a 9-year old, awestruck by just how good video games can be. I played it for hours upon its release and it ignited a love for RPGs that lasts to this day. I still go back every once in a while to replay the game, and I'm happy to see that it's been ported to Steam so I don't have to break out the old Nintendo DS or -- gasp! -- my grandfatherly SNES that still sits in my closet next to a shoebox on my most cherished titles from the '90s.
Most reviewers gripe about the graphics "update", and while I generally do prefer the original sprites (sprites tend to age better than any polygonal graphics), I don't find the graphical change to be much worse. It's different, sure, but really not worse in any objective way. I can understand how the greybeards would be miffed at a change to their beloved classic games, but it really didn't bother me. And as a nearly day-one played of the original title in 1994, I'm about as old school as they come.
and I'm happy to say that's not much of a problem here. This one, while it's not fantastic, seems to work fine. You're going to lack some high resolution options here, but given how badly they were implemented in Final Fantasy VII with its disastrously upscaled backgrounds, I'd say that's not too much of a problem. This isn't an HD remaster, it's just a port of the original game, which was designed for tube TVs rather than PC screens. As such, this is a perfect game to play windowed while you've got some other stuff going on in the background.
While the graphics have aged incredibly well, the story and writing, however, have not. When this game released it helped to push the bar of good character writing and narrative. Unfortunately that bar has long been pressed onward and well past where Final Fantasy VI left it. While the characters are still incredibly charming and thoughtfully written, and the plot has some decent surprises in store for you, the writing in general lacks a lot of the depth that we can find in modern day games.
That's no reason not to play Final Fantasy VI, though. The combat system is still fun, with a grand cast of party members each featuring their own special abilities carrying combat through the majority of the game. Using such a colorful cast of characters is a joy, and the game really takes pains to ensure that they're all unique and introduces them in a manner in which none of them are just a face in the crowd. You genuinely care about them all and want to see them succeed. You'll find yourself cheering when one of them lands a critical or pulls you out of a tough situation. The game isn't overly challenging unless you've got no idea what you're doing, though.
The Esper system is good, but lacks a little bit compared to the job system and the later Materia system, which is probably my favorite in the series outside of Final Fantasy Tactics' jobs and abilities system.
Seriously, Squeenix, can we get a PC port for Final Fantasy Tactics? Please?
It'd be a crime not to mention Nobuo Uematsu's unbelievably amazing score, which is among the best in the Final Fantasy series and certainly among the best scores in all of video game history. It's spellbinding, utterly engrossing. To this day I can't hear a track from it that doesn't take me back to sitting on my parents' carpet, staring up at the 20" tube TV, playing the best game I had ever played up to that point of my life; one that would stick with me more than 20 years later and inspire me to write a review on this newfangled Steam contraption. And that's why I love this game so much. It's a charming, emotionally impactful roller coaster ride to a simpler time. Play it and maybe it'll be the same for you.

I'm going to say right now, the negative reviews on this game are completely idiotic.
This game is literally what DBD should have been. It's fun, frantic, horrifying, and hilarious all at the same time.
Lets just get right into it with pros and cons
Pros!
-Playing as Jason is FUN AS HELL, as long as you make it that way. You can either kill everyone in 5 seconds or you can actually have fun and toy with people since you're basically unstoppable
-Playing as counseler is tons of fun as well. Aside from what the negative reviewers are saying its VERY possible to survive in this game. Game rewards you for helping your friends, setting up escapes, and stalling jason.
-NO ♥♥♥♥ING RANKS OR OP PERKS, Unlike that game DBD perks in this game aren't game breaking in anyway. They have a positive and a negative effect for them. (Less likely to stumble while running +15% but make more noise by 9%) something like that.
-No cheese in this game. It's pretty hard to cheese jason without actual thought behind what you're going to do after.
-Graphics are actually really well done.
-Animations are nice and polished. (you know since devs used full mocap for everything)
-Shooting jason with a shotgun is insanely satisfying.
-Proximity voice chat!
-Audio in this game is amazing, everything is really tense when its quiet, and hectic as all hell when jason is around chasing you or someone near you.
-Tons of ways to stall jason, traps, beating him, shooting him, using a special something to distract him for a little bit, radios, firecrackers, and the like.
-Tons of ways to kill counselers, on top of the 15 some odd executions you get with your bare hands, each jason has 3 executions with the weapon he has, as WELL as all the enviromental kills
-Keyboard controls i personally think work perfectly and have no issues with them. have not used gamepad.
CONS!
-Not much content, 3 maps, reused textures for those maps, but the  layouts are entirely different so thats something.
-Stuff is level locked. Nothing important, some characeters are locked behind level caps i believe the last thing you unlock is at level 13-15. so not too much.
-Calling tommy jarvis doesn't really help as much as it should
-Price tag. (i am actually perfectly okay with spending 40 dollars on this as it is  TON of fun to play) Other people have a hard time enjoying something if they cant afford it i guess.
-Campaign and Bot matches aren't in the game YET.
-Cant rebind controls (as of now) though if you're okay with the control scheme dont complain about it.
OVERALL
This is great indie game thats tons of fun to play, alone or with friends. If you are okay with a 40$ price tag then you should definitely pick this up. It's only going to get better from here as devs plan to fully support the game with content.
Campaign and bots should be added in sometime in summer from what i last heard.

I really wanted to recommend this game; it has so much going for it, but in the end, I was just angry at it.
It's absolutely beautiful. It's almost worth buying just for that. The story is fun, the mechanics are great and very novel. During the first part when you're collecting the colors (game mechanics), the game is super fun, even though it's kinda easy.
However, in "Void mode," (which is the real game, honestly), the puzzles are just stupidly hard. And I don't mean they're difficult to figure out (that's the fun part of any puzzle game, right?). What I mean is once you do figure out what to do (and that part is challenging and fun because they don't let you take the obvious route), it's almost impossible to time correctly. The game stops being about figuring out puzzles and starts being about minuscule timing tasks, i.e., try to make an enemy chase you off a ledge and have it step on a button while you rush through the opened area.
I'm sorry Nihilumbra. I wanted to like you so much more than I did.
tl;dr: Beautiful, fun story, stupidly hard timing/jumping tasks.

The dev really tried to make a great game, and almost did so.
There are alot of options for weapons, a good amount of enemies, some bosses, and CONSTANT updates, which make the game good, but the main issue is two things:
1) There are many "Filler Items" in the game. For example, there are a vast selection of guns, but some do a small amount of damage, while the rest do the exact same (A Sniper rifle, magnum, LMG, and Assault Rifle do the exact same amount of damage, they all just have different clips and distances they can shoot). There are alot of enemies, but many of them, once more, do the same amount of damages and are basically the same monster reskined to look different. And the Food and Water system is honestly out of place and just feels like something the dev added in to be able to say "And look! Survival!"
2) Enemies are honestly overpowered, while you are horribly underpowered. Every single enemy (Including the boss) Runs slightly slower than you and NEVER stops running, meaning that you cannot stop to reload at any point during a wave, and you cannot run while reloading. Some weapons, such as the magnum, are totally useless further on in waves because it does the exact same amount of damage as a sniper (The sniper would be useless as well, but it can shoot longer ranges than all weapons, which barely gives it enough slack to make it ok), and becuase you have to wait 2 seconds in between each shot. There are 3 enemies that do a large amount of damage: Rock giants, Aliens with blasters, and the mini bosses.
They all run, once more, slightly slower than you, so you can only sort of outrun the giant. The aliens will stop and shoot at you, and their shots are IMPOSSIBLE to avoid, and they do a good amount of damage. Same with the mini boss who shoots a lazer at you, high damage, runs ACTUALLY FASTER than you, and unavoidable attack. What is even worse about this is that the boss glitches through all placed objects (Minus buildings), so if you try to hide behind a tree, it just passes through it and hits you anyways.

There is so much about this game may people don't know, and I could talk for days about the abilities, tactics and details of this game but I'll try to cover the high level aspects of this game. If you want more details contact our community in the discord link below.
Allegiance was originally developed by Microsoft in the late 1990s and was originally released on March 16, 2000 as a pay to play premium game on Microsoft zone. Eventually to help boost sales they released a limited version free to play. Microsoft's failure to run the game and assist new players lead to low sales and poor customer service. They officially shut down the servers in 2002 and released the game under a shared license. After that the community supported the game to keep it alive by running their own servers and keeping the code up to date and working on balancing and supporting new players into the game.
In June of 2017, Microsoft released the code to the public and opened the license to public domain and the community who loved this game took the code, fixed problems with it and released it free of charge to everyone on steam so they could share this game with the world. Magazines have noted this game as the "Best game you never played" awards and the community couldn't agree more!
Microsoft Allegiance combines real-time strategy elements into a space combat simulator. The main objective of Microsoft Allegiance is to attack and destroy your enemies bases, while protecting your own. You have to consider all aspects important such as defense of your miners so your team can make money, defending your bases, attacking enemy miners to disrupt their resources, attacking and defending against enemy pilots, and you must work with your teammates to achieve this objective. Without it, you're doomed to fail.
While old to the eye, the game is incredible to play. No other game has ever been this detailed in strategies and tactics. There are many different factions all with their own special abilities and weaponry. The "fog of war" that everyone talks about is entirely based on scanning and signature of your own ships abilities. Some factions can easily scan targets while others provide superior cloaking and are hard to detect. You must also consider that the ship has better scanners in front, than behind so you can sneak up on enemies with poor scanning from behind. You can also lower your signature by disarming weapons and running with limited ammo. Your mass entirely bases your ability to turn and attack enemies.
Once you master the ability to fly the ships and you understand their capabilities, the game is far from mastered because now you can also be the commander of all the ships on your team. The Real time strategy elements now play a factor. You have limited money to purchase ships and upgrade technology for your team, and being the eye in the sky, you have the ability to see what's going on everywhere. Employ your friends to assist you with commanding miners and keeping them going, while you focus on the overall strategy, or employ your best squadron leaders and have them lead attacks while you keep your leaders informed with details of whats going on around them.
The community is amazing. You will never find a group of people who love the game more than the people you find in the discord channel. There's people willing to provide help, and training to anyone who wants it. All you have to do is ask and you will get people willing to help you. They love the game, and they know they need people to enjoy the game they love and the old saying "The more the merrier" couldn't apply more here. The community developers will answer questions and are actively working with the game. If you want to help out, the community will accept anyone with talents to help with building the community as well.
If you have problems, join the official discord channel for help and assistance from experienced players who have been playing this game for over 15 years.

For Honor is a Player-Versus-Player game like no other currently on the market. Picking from one of 12 playable hero classes from each of the three factions - the Knights (DEUS VULT), the
Vikings or the Weaboos (or as they like to be called, 'Samurai') you march into battle against between 1 and 4 other players (or AI if pure PVP isn't your deal) in a variety of different maps and gameplay modes to duke it out in bloody and brutal combat until you and/or your team come out the victors.
There's more to it than just smacking each other about for giggles though, as every win awards you War Assets, which you can then use to contribute to your faction's control of the different territories on the world map - giving you access to a different selection of maps and regions for the next round of play.
Every hero controls different, even amongst similar play-styles - with the general rule of thumb being that the Knights can take the most punishment, the Vikings hit the hardest and the Samurai are swiftest, but even this has it's variations (as the Sugoki, the Samurai's hard-hitter, deals the highest damage of any unit in the game, whilst the Knight's Peacekeeper is one of the swiftest.) Learning the basics of any hero is easy; mastering them is hard.
For Honor is not a game that button-mashers will enjoy; timing is key to keeping your combos going and turning a simple block into a staggering Parry. But patience pays off, and the feel of besting multiple opponents at once as they do their best to take you down is a rush beyond compare.
Thus far, the game's Story Mode is it's weakest point, offering a mere 16 missions which will take, at worst, around 2-3 hours to work your way through. However it does give you a bit of background into why you're brutally decapitating people left right and center, whilst also giving you a chance to try out most of the heroes on offer against AI enemies of increasing ability and unlocking some neat customisation options for your heroes.
The biggest point against For Honor as a whole right now is it's matchmaking stability. Rather than using dedicated servers, For Honor operates on a peer-to-peer system; meaning the stability of each match relies on the stability of everyone's connection. It's not the end of the world if a single person disconnects; they'll be replaced by a bot which will likewise be replaced by another player as soon as one's available; but it can lead to whole matches going up the crapper more often than not which is, to put it lightly, bleeping infuriating.
Despite that it's still a shedload of fun and, IMO, worth the money.

I would love to recommend this game. The gameplay is great. Singleplayer isn't bad. Bot AI isn't bad. Overall it's a really fun and enjoyable game. The classes have nice variety, with different strengths, and playstyles. No class feels overpowered by itself because power comes from skill. Maybe that will change as people get more used to the game.
HOWEVER.
Matchmaking takes forever, then disconnects.
It can kick you for "low fps" the moment you drop a frame, even if you've been running smoothly for hours.
I can not play multiplayer reliably because I am constantly getting kicked for inactivity. While fighting.
I have been kicked for inactivity while in the process of executing someone.
I've been kicked for inactivity while dead, at the end of a match, with no respawn available.
There is no inactivity warning. There is no option to reconnect.
I often get "Network error" and get disconnected. I'm told that this might have something to do with two people playing from the same connection. So be aware of this if you want to play with your roommate, wife, girlfriend, boyfriend, husband, brother, sister, son, daughter, or awkward cousin who is crashing at your place until he gets back on his feet.
In short:
If you want a skill based singleplayer game, Buy this. It's really good.
If you only want to play custom games with a group of friends and no rewards, this is great, would definitely recommend.
If you want to play multiplayer (EVEN VS AI), consider waiting. Maybe the connection issues will be fixed, but right now multiplayer is pretty unplayable for me, and potential buyers should be aware that it could happen to them too.
---
Edit:
They have fixed the issue where I get disconnected for inactivity. It was related to using a steam controller.
Now I get told that I cannot join a session because it is full, then kicked back to the map screen.
Or the host disconnects and I get kicked from the game.
These issues are less common than the original issue, but still common enough to be a bit annoying.
So, still buy this game if you want to play with friends. It's a good game. But connection issues still make multiplayer a bit frustrating, and the more strangers you plan on playing with the more frustrating it's likely to be.
---
Edit2: Multiplayer has a lot of issues, but I'm coming to believe that (now that they've at least fixed it so I can play more than 1/10 games) the gameplay is worth it. Changing this to recommended because the gameplay is worth the horrible connection issues.

A cute Ys-style game from Falcom, originally released for PC in 2004 and ported to the PSP in 2007. The game's environments and BGM are quite relaxing, as you wander about the town, helping characters solve their problems. The voice dub is competent, if goofy in a way, and the characters are very well-drawn and animated. The art is very well done. Almost all of the various headgear and costumes you acquire along the way fit Parin rather nicely.
There is a lot of attention to detail in this game. Stand Parin the protagonist next to a character dancing to his boombox and she will join right in. Characters go about their lives in town and might wander in and out of different buildings if you are looking for them. Parin in particular is full of personality, from the way she acts and how she responds to other characters.
Gameplay-wise, combat is smooth, and the invincibility frames you get are very generous. It's not nearly as difficult as Ys, but some opponents are notably tougher than the rest though, otherwise this is a very child-friendly game. There are plenty of secrets to find and things to unlock. Truly mastering a stage would mean getting S triple + rank, so there is plenty to do.
Criticisms incude: keyboard key-binding options are not the best and camera control with a controller is non-existent. The option for Japanese audio would have been nice, but Mastiff (the localization company) is looking into both of these at time of writing. The higher difficulty levels also need to be unlocked first.
Games with unadulterated charm are rare these days, so give it a whirl if you like the genre.

Gurumin is an action platformer developed by Falcom in 2003.   The project was helmed by the same group who made Zwei but is about a girl who uses a drill to defeat enemies and dig through structures instead of using a partner to shoot magic and relies on eating to boost stats.   This title was also made when Nihon Falcom was sorta in a rut and didn't find financial success to run on until Sora no Kiseki Second Chapter.  This really shows now adays as Gurumin looks no better than a N64 game with improved textures to dabble with.
The game's still fun, albeit very very simple.   The music is kinda boring, the enemies are slow and easy, the map design is kinda rudamentary.  All and all this seems like a simple game whipped up by a studio and dev team to just clear some technical checkpoints.  This is a Banjo Kazooie/Mario 64/Ape Escape/Crash Bandicoot clone that while fun is just lacking in so many areas.
It's charming, cheap, and worth a try.   Give it a whirl if you like the team behind it, but I wouldn't really say get it if you're looking to revist the era where action platformers dominated the market because this is not the next Jet Force Gemini.

Even though I'm not sure that this is my favorite episode in the series, I just have to admit that it may be the most complete and well made of all. This will certainly bring a bit of nostalgia to players, especially those who miss that time when both Squaresoft and Enix were creating the best RPG that you could find on the market.

I recommend this game to anyone who is in search of a crash simulator, a driving simulator, a game with realistic In-Depth car customisation or just a way to pass some time if you dont want to bother loading into any other game.
So far I have played almost 80 hours of this game, which is a fairly high amount for me and actually more than I have played GTA V. I have installed quite a few mods and lokked deep into the vehicle customization.
Just a few things you can do in the game:
-Simulate crashes with (on my PC) up to six vehicles (which can have a rudimentary AI)
-Just drive around and relax
-Create your very own dream vehicle from models roughly resembling real life cars
-Race around various tracks included in some of the maps
-Finetune your suspension in terms of ride height, spring stiffness, track width and more
-Install dozens of mods, some of them with incredibly high quality
-explore the detailed maps, find all the secret passages
- ... and quite a lot more!
As far as I can tell, the game runs very smoothly until you spawn to many cars (6 on my PC), it looks great even on lower graphical settings and has a FoV-Slider so TotalBiscuit will be happy. Extremely high velocity/force impacts don't look that great, but are still a accurate depiction of what would happen to a similar car (despite some parts clipping through others bended textures/Jbeams etc...) Aside from that crashes in this game are almost worthy of next generation car testing. E.g. brake thermals and cooling liquids and other stuff gets simulated.
Stuff you should know:
Though it's possible to play this game with a keyboard you will have a hard time controlling especially the stronger/older car variants. This is because a keyboard limits you to full throttle, none at all and hard braking. The best option would be a steering wheel,but a contoller also works just fine. The game has force feedback compatibility in general, however this doesn't apply to my ancient  SpeedLink wheel.
There is a experimental replay feature, but it's still a buggy mess. I guess it will be fixed very soon, look out for that.
Which brings me to my next point: The game gets updated regularly (a major content patch comes out every 1/2 months, of high quality, with bugfixes, optimisations and like I said, content). BeamNG also has a very nice and helpful community.
What I don't like as of now:
-The sounds (which have been described as placeholders by the devs) are plain horrible, but they said that they hired a
sound effects guy in the last devblog.
-The particles are not all that detailed and plenty compared to real car crashes
-The game tends to bug out sometimes, nothing major, but it's there and its annoying

It's a top down MMO space shooter with a bit of depth to it. 150 level cap and lots of resource gathering for upgrades. Flux is this game's currency used to buy ships and other nice non-essential things. You can either buy flux with real money or you will have to grind missions/daily logins for it in-game.
Pros:
*Plenty of different ships, some have unique weapons pre-installed on them
*Plenty of weapons, over 100 of them and they are all quite fun to play around with
*Artifacts are this game's form of loot to help improve your ship's stats in general, they are randomly generated too
*PvP matches although it needs some improvements to keep things more balanced
*Open world PvP where you could of course take on higher/lower level players
*Boss battles that are quite tough, especially if you haven't got a good setup or a strategy for taking them on
*Storyline quests, gives you something to work toward as it takes you through all the systems
*Timed missions, these are randomly generated quests that give you some decent rewards
*Daily login and missions give you some cool rewards for minimal effort
Cons:
*Playerbase isn't very large and not sure whether it will increase by much
*Lag spikes and desync seem to happen a bit of the time, especially when picking up lots of loot
*Boring for players that constantly want something new and fresh every time they play it as it's very grindy
*Crew feature which is used to upgrade your artifacts needs serious improvement (Takes too long to train them up)
*Co-op survival while fun, needs to be improved so that exp loss on death isn't something that puts people off of it
*Grindy, as mentioned before. If you want new ships, upgrades or levels, you will need to grind quite a bit for them
*Devs, apparently they are not interested in changing or adding much to the game (From what people say)
*Bugs, quite a lot of them and I'm not talking about the ones in-game that you shoot at
*Upgrading, requires too much resources after you've made previous upgrades to things on your ship. Prevents you from investing and experimenting with other weapons which ruins the weapon variety
Overall, this game has a lot of potential to be something amazing. It has loads of variety in weapons, ships, artifacts and strategies to go with them but it gets boring fast if you don't like grinding out levels and missions. Personally, I enjoy it very much and can see myself being part of this game for a good while. I do hope that the devs put in some more effort to make this game the best it possibly can be as well as add in some more co-op related stuff but for now, the game is good for what it is.
I would recommend playing. 7/10, 9/10 for the F2P section
