I have found this game to be very intricate and engaging, and have enjoyed it immensely.  I feel that most people who are disappointed with this are expecting another Civ4, set in space.  Common complaints are lack of story, short games, lack of content diversity for replaying.  However if you have the right idea about what this game is, it is amazing.  This is a fast paced competitive strategic battlefield, played with production, stock markets, and espionage, rather than armies and warfare.  Played in real time, if you sit back and try to make a happy little colony you won't last long.
The very solid yet short tutorial gives you a decent understanding of a game that is easy to start, yet very tricky to master.  I have not yet ventured into competitive multiplayer.... The "campaign" mode is really just an extension of learning, and the skirmish or multiplayer modes are the real meat.  Every game starts much the same, and rapidly spirals off in a different direction; directly influenced by your choices and those of your opponents, with a small amount of randomised external forces.
What I really appreciate about this game is the total lack of paper-scissors-rock "counters" that exist in most strategy games.  Everything is viable, and even if your current strategy is shut down, you can pivot to something else and still be heavily competitive from behind.  The only wrong move is inaction, however the smallest things you do will be felt elsewhere.  I wasn't fully sure what I was getting into with this game, and tbh the first couple of hours against easy AI felt shallow, however I rapidly discovered that this game is satisfyingly deep and pretty much perfect, and that the AI 'easy' level was called that for a reason.....
Additionally, the strength of a game based on numbers and definite cause and effect such as this is that the AI can be intelligent, unfeeling, ruthless, efficient, and incredibly challenging.
In summary; this game is darn near perfect FOR WHAT IT IS.  If you are wanting empire building, long protracted games, campaign as a main feature, then this game will not be another Civilization.  If you want short fast-paced matches in which you can test your instincts and decision making skills against opponents, while able to use a whole variety of strategy combinations, then this game will keep you happy for a long long time.

This was my fiist time playing this game so I don't have nostalgia influencing my review.  I have been a casual FF fan for a while and always considered FF7 the best of the series.  I was wrong, this game is by far the best Final Fantasy and has become one of my all time favorite games.  The characters are great, you develope a connection with them and end up caring about most of your party members (sorry Umaro and Gogo).  The story is solid. An ancient war, magic disappearing from the planet, an industrial revolution rising from the ashes of a once scorched earth, an evil empire draining magic for their own empowerment, a love triangle, rediscovering self worth, the list goes on.  I can see how this game influenced FF7 in many ways, only FF6 did it better.
Many reviews criticize the graphics becuase this is a port of the iOS/Android game.  Who cares?  It looked great to me on my 1080p monitor.  Sure the sprites are a bit cleaner now but I don't feel like that distracts from the game at all.  It still has a wonderful retro vibe to it.  I had a Sega Genesis as a kid, not a SNES, so I never go to experience this game in its full glory.  But, as someone who doesn't like to emulate/pirate, this was the best way for me to expierence this wonderful game without spending a ton on a GBA cartridge.   If you're on the fence, I wholeheartedly recommend getting this game.  I spent a fantastic 35 hours with Terra, Locke, Celes and the gang and cannot stop thinking about it.  It's sticking with me.  Here's hoping FF15 will be half as good.

Not a bad port, but not the greatest, it has is upsides and downsides. This FF6 version is ported from the iOS/Android mobile edition, based on the Game Boy Advance edition for Final Fantasy VI, so expect a different translation from that what we knew in the Super Nintendo release. Many bugs and glitches were fixed so if you were expecting to use them at your favor, then don't count on it.
This Version PROS:
- Enhanced Graphics.
- New Translation more accurate to the history and less trigger happy that Nintendo early 1990's police.
- A bit less of censorship (Cafes are now Pubs & Bars).
- The Original Great FF6 history.
- More Espers (summons).
- More Dungeons.
- Cards, Badges and Emoticons.
This Version CONS:
- Based from the Game Boy Advance edition, the Celes beating scene was censored/removed (can be restored with a patch, look in the community hub).
- Certain Monsters and Summons were censored by covering their shameful body display (Siren, Lakshmi & Goddess, can be restored with community patches).
- Loading/Lags the game does not retain the SNES fluidity, after battles, exiting main menus, entering new dungeons or towns can cause a small loading freeze for about 1 to 2seconds.
- Lack of Video filters, only bilinear available and always ON, can be deactivated trough mods, (Seriously SquareEnix why can't you could add Open Source filters like xBRz, Scanlines?, etc.).
- No upper resolutions above 1360*768.
What Could make this port better?.
- Fixing the above CONS mentioned.
Still is a good game, be sure that the game is still enjoyable. Personally I would have loved to have a faithful edition closer to the Japanese edition with zero censorship.

For Honor is a good game, in need of some patching. While the game was just released recently, I have high hopes for its future. As long as the developers take care updating the game frequently and fixing the MANY inconsistencies that are currently present, I can see this game continuing to be a fun experience for quite a while.
Why it's garbage:
-P2P sucks noodles.
-Either no, or terribad matchmaking.
-Microtransactions to get more in game currency.
-Some blatantly unbalanced mechanics, like infinitely guard breaking with no cooldown or using a hero specific skill with no cooldown.
-Some builds are terribly broken.
-Some heroes can instantly switch guards and attack fast for full damage, while others attack slow for the same damage.
-The wonky guard break counter system is inconsistent.
-Forgettable, laughably bad story that no one asked for.
-Ubisoft (Uplay runs when you launch the game)
Why it's radical:
-Fun gameplay, it's fun hitting your enemy with swords and axes and you can feel the hits.
-The 3 direction targeting system is easy to use, but hard to master.
-The "steel" you get with the microtransactions can instead be earned in game.
-There are modes where all weapon stat buffs are off, no items, fox only.
-Getting a new item that looks cool is awesome/the cosmetics are pretty sick.
-People get super, and I mean SUPER salty when thrown off a ledge/it feels great ledge cheesing some guy who you obviously can't beat.
-The whole faction war thing is neat, the multiplayer maps you can play change depending on where there is fighting.
-Nice animations, the run animations especially look very nice, and you can really feel the weight behind the weapons.
-Ubisoft (if they treat this game like they do Rainbow Six Siege, you can expect lots of updates/balancing/bugfixing/ and online stability fixes.)
So yes, I do recommened this game. The reason there are so many negative reviews right now is because it's peer to peer instead of having dedicated servers. Not perfect. Not a traditional classical shooter. Not a great DLC model.
What it is, however, is a ton of fun. Controls are solid, gadgets are fun to throw around, guns have a decent feel to them (though still worse than quite a few indie games I've played).
The big draw to Siege is how the destructible environments and objectives change the game from a straight shooting contest to a game of tactics and positioning. Stealth, landmines, misdirection and underhanded tactics are straight up ENCOURAGED, and in most cases mandatory. Each new operator changes the way a round plays, giving the game pretty good depth and replayability for a straight multiplayer shooter.

My first impression:
Worth the price of admission, just to roleplay as one of my ancestors and learn some of their history. Plus it's a Mount & Blade game!
My second impression:
Warband is better, for a few reasons. Warband has better troop diversity among the factions and more interesting upgrade trees for troops. In Fire and Sword, I think they did a good job making combat different from Warband with the addition of guns since they do sooo much damage. You're forcedd to modify your battlefield tactics to take advantage of them. However, with guns, armor and melee feel less important. This means all the different factions' units feel like identical reskins of each other. Everyone seems to have sharpshooters, cavalry, and pikemen. Plus, you can just hire a relatively inexpensive mercenary army of sharpshooters, cavalry, and pikemen instead of raising your own troops. It's still interesting, but different.

In the moments after fulfilling an objective and you are under pressure from multiple enemies, there is nothing more satisfying than finding your range, and nailing headshot after headshot. As someone who enjoyed the first game but wasn't a huge fan, I'm glad I picked this up, and upon finishing I will definitely be buying Sniper Elite 3.

If you are a hardcore fan of Shadow Warrior 2013, I would skip Shadow Warrior 2 until it's cheap like $9.99. If you are a fan of first person shooters then get the game because it's a lot of fun and has a Serious Sam/Borderlands type of gameplay to it. I went blindly when buying SW 2 and saw little of gameplay trailers. I thought the co-op addition of the game was an added feature and wouldn't be the main focus of gameplay, I was totally wrong. The main focus is co-op because it has huge levels, a variety of weapons and a lot of them, and ammo dumps throughout each map. I didn't like the addition of the statues that replenish all ammo, health, chi, and rage. Those statues took the challenge away from surviving enemies, but I could get around them by not going near them, sometimes I did by accident. New weapons can be found throughout the game by defeating large enemies or opening loot chests. Instead of the missions and story being linear, it's "choose your missions until you hit the end of the 'Part 1' of thre story to go to 'Part 2'. The Hub is boring and Larry looks like he belongs in Borderlands, not Shadow Warrior. I really wanted this game to complement SW 2013 because that game has a great story, comedy, and action packed gameplay, but this is a totally different game.
The developers played it safe with the story. Having Kamiko take place of Hoji from SW 2013 and she is annoying. She doesn't add much to the story, her character model is lower quality from the oher characters  (which is weird), and she doesn't have the bantering connection with Lo Wang that Hoji had.
Be prepared to be ping ponging back and forth during the game with "Find the door-the door is locked-go across the map to get the key-get the key-go back the way you came to unlock the door". I think the developers did this for co-op reasons, leveling up for skills and abilities, and killing hordes of enemies. Overall, the gameplay is fun just like SW 2013, some of the jokes are funny, and the weapons are fun to use. I know I gave a lot of cons to this game. These are my gripes about what annoyed and bored me about the game. Check out the reviews or comments of the people who played SW 2013 and then this game, they give great pros and cons. Also check the reviews of people who just played SW 2 and not SW 2013. This will help you decide if you want to get the game along with my review.

Let me tell you why you should buy this game. Just listen here for a second.
Can I say, that this game is awesome? Because it is. It's genuinely hard to complete in one sitting, all thanks to well placed environmental and NPC "screamers". Ah, that word - I shouldn't have used it. "Screamers" are what bad horror games prefer to use. There is no psychology behind that fear that you get after coming across a screamer. It's a one time thing, and all it does - is make sure your reflexes and self-preservation instincts still work. You scream not of fear, but of suddenness. Well, you won't scream if you are Kristen Stewart.
Amnesia? It doesn't have screamers. Well, not too many. Instead, it makes sure you get the feeling of dread just by walking through levels. The atmosphere of desolation and doom, the sounds that you make while walking across the creaky rotten floor, the creatures that make you feel disgust just by looking at them, not to mention the sounds they make... All of it is mixed together into a beautifully tragic and horrifying horror game, with a twisted story and a character to remember. Amnesia became a classic nowadays. There are better games, of course. I won't name them. But Amnesia is one thing you shouldn't miss out. Even if you're afraid of the year gap between now and when it's been created.

Beforehand, I thought this would be primarily a horror game with a nice story (like Amnesia). I was actually a little bit dissappointed at first as the first monster you encounter isn't really that scary. While the game does become more frightening as you go along (and is at some points so scary that you will want to cry), it is the story and the setting that defines the game
Hands down, this is probably one of the best stories I have ever seen in a video game. Profound, original, awesome. Some of the settings are insanely cool, especially towards the end of the game. That goosebump feeling I am always looking for in games was with me the entire later half of this game. It was just so weird and awesome. Things you never get to do in most games because it's just too big of a hassle to design were in this game. Short spoiler: imagine walking the seafloor of a 5 mile deep underwater crevass, being followed by something big that doesn't like bright lights....
For reference, I love story-driven games like Half-Life 2 + episodes, The Longest Journey, Dreamfall, Syberia etc. If you do too, you will love this. Oh, and if you liked Amnesia: The Dark Descent, you will LOOOOVE this!

I am going to make this short and (not so) sweet.
This game is broken, and has been broken ever since I purchased it early 2017. I have played quite a few games, and no game has come close to how many bugs are in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege. This has to be the most bug infested game I have ever played. From outright falling through the map, to thrown grenades rubber banding back to you and getting you killed, to poor networking and hit registration, to rubber banding and so, so much more...
The developers seem to be working hard to fix these issues, but unfortunately their lack of competence is only creating more issues and bugs each time they "fix" one of them.
Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege has an incredible amount of potential, unfortunately it isn't a game created by a competent team, and is a frustrating game filled with countless bugs and unfortunate events leaving you feeling as if you've purchased a game which is incomplete, and in its Alpha stage.

I didn't think I was going to like this game after reading some of the reviews. The single player campaign was surprisingly good. The only blemish is the enemy spawning. There are a few sections where the enemies will spawn indefinitely unless you advance your position. It ruins the willing suspension of disbelief for those sections of the game, although it should be noted that the enemy spawning didn't make the game unfair. It's just that enemy respawning indefinitely is an outdated convention. I would have given the single player campaign a 9/10 if not for that single blemish. Still, I had a lot of fun playing the game. The weapons were some of the best I've ever used in a FPS war game and the action was always engaging. The story was typical, but how many of us play FPS's for their story? The campaign was short; six hours tops, but it was never boring. The graphics were excellent and the explosion effects were second to none. I don't know why this game was reviewed so poorly. I didn't play in multiplayer, so consider this review only if you are interested in the single player campaign. 8.5/10

If there is one thing I can say about this game its that it caters to a very specific audience, and it caters to that audience very well. If you've ever played an RTS or other overhead style of build and conquer game and thought to yourself, "Wouldn't it be cool if there was a game like this where everyone played own of the little pieces rather than having one person control them all?" Then you might really enjoy this game, because thats what its all about.
LiF is a teamwork game where individual MUST work together to build something substantial. This is not a good single player game, its not designed for that, you will lose your mind if you try to play this game single player, or even try to go it alone on a multi-player server. 99% of the capabilities of this game come from interacting with others to create something. This game is also relatively slow pace, as you look through the comments sections you can see that most people giving a thumbs up have 1000+ hours in this game. The result is that people work hard and long to develop things in this such have strong sense of pride when its done. The amount of work and effort that goes into actually achieving things in this game makes griefing much more difficult than in other similar games, and the necessity of teamwork makes it much more compatible with Roleplay for those who want it.
In my experience this is a great game, but you have to know what your getting when you buy it. If you want action and to be the hero of a grand and epic story, this is probably not the game for you. If you want to experience a truly immersive take on medieval life and contribute to making something greater then just yourself, this game is for you.

I played Allegiance back in beta in 2000 and loved it. It died on the vine due to a number of bad marketing decisions by Microsoft and eventually they shut the servers off.
The Allegiance community managed to keep it alive (somehow) and now they've finally gotten permission from Microsoft to put it on Steam.
So that means a 17 year old game is being re-released.
Graphics, control schemes, etc, all reflect the age of the game. Making it work properly is going to take some tweaking and you WILL need to remap your controls.
It's a game with a steep learning curve and a really involved community which means that jumping into a big game and expecting to be the commander or even just doing poorly can make some people mad at you.
The folks who managed to get this on steam recognize that some portions of their community (as much as they want more players) are not doing things that are going to attract them.
I recommend hopping into small games (less than 10 players) that are labled Training Grounds or otherwise newbie friendly.  If you want to play with the Commander role, you can make your own game and uncheck the bullet to the left of the second team, and then tool around playing with the tech tree to your hearts content.
Don't expect modern amenities and spend some time learning the tech trees and this can be a GREAT game. The meta, the teamwork, the pretty deep tech trees, the 10(!!!) different factions, and the satisfaction of blowing up an enemies base in a bomber or capital ship with the entire enemy team frantically trying to stop you make this work sinking some time to, especially since it is completely free (no FTP microtransactions here!)
You can play with a mouse and keyboard but I do recommend at least a basic joystick.

I've had a love for space sims ever since I was a child. I wanted to be an astronaut. I begged my parents for a $60 joystick that I played to death. I've got hours on flight sims and driving sims just because I enjoy it. And this is why it pains me to say that this game, while it handles well, it completely misses the mark. 
Allegiance seems to have found that perfect balance where it takes all of the worst parts of RTS and combines them with the worst parts of MOBA. What I find odd is that the creator posted this proudly.
"Allegiance is also a fully formed RTS with tech trees, exploration, base building, and resource gathering. But there’s a twist: most of your ships are flown by real human beings! "
Is this... fun? Micromanagement is enough of a pain when your units don't have brains, yet for some reason it's good when they do? You know what's really great? When I tell my fighter to go to sector X but instead I find them in sector Y, doing lord knows what, and my miner is now dead. On top of that, now the fighter can tell your units where to go. Hold on! I thought that I was the commander?! Why are my units telling my other units where to go? On top of that, remember that your units are now real people, which means not only will they ignore you, move your units for you, but they'll also yell at you and be all kinds of cancer. They often tell you not to play commander unless you've played for a while. Do what now? Why would you put being the commander as a selling point for your game if you don't want people actually being a commander? This problem is compounded even further (if you can believe it) by the addition of a 'mutiny' system in which the commander may be replaced if enough people vote for it. And sure, that might seem fair, you don't want an idiot steering the ship, but shouldn't there at the very least be a single-player option? Where I can futz around as much as I like without hurting any multiplayer games? 
Then the creator straight up lies to you. They say, "Unique fog of war system". I expect a unique fog of war system. There is nothing unique about the fog of war system. Why is that even listed the way that it is. This is a fairly bog-standard fog of war system just like any other Starcraft game. I asked a mod for comment on this and the mod said that the system was unique for its time. Unique for its time? Is this how you can get away with lying? By saying that something was unique when it was created, but not at the point of being put on steam? This is a black mark against the developers in my eyes. 
I trust most of you have played other shooters, yeah? So riddle me this - when someone leaves your team, is it not painful to play 1-2 people down? You get camped which causes more people to quit which makes the problem even worse. Which is why many games have introduce ~~~ autobalance! When a game becomes too unbalanced, someone from the other team will be moved to your team! Tada! Why does this game not have that? 
Let me describe something that might pain those of your that like competing for top dog. I played a small 1v1 game and after losing, I noticed at the top left the game says "Win not counted". Okay, cool. So the game won't count your games if they're too small which is probably fair so you can't 1v1 someone to the top of the leaderboard. I played a 4v5 game later, won that one, 'Win not counted'. Ummm.. Okay. I guess maybe the game is balanced for 10v10 or something. I played a 13v13 game, 'Win not counted'. Excuse me? EXCUSE ME? How large does the game have to be for the win to count? A mod of the game was in the room and they said that the win was counted, the game just always says that. Well it sounds like something you could have fixed in the 20 years of development! 
How many other things in the game can I not trust? Can I even trust the developer? 
This might be a bit of a personal complaint but the game tries to sell you on diversity of gameplay. There is no diversity of gameplay. This is like saying every league of legends game can be unique depending on the players. True in theory, but not in practice. You're still going to have a meta and those that do not follow the meta get treated poorly. In the 2 more serious games I played, people kept complaining that the commander wouldn't do X. This creates a heavy burden on new players. "Easy to learn but once you learn you better do everything right because remember there's a mutiny button that can be used to replace you".
Also, can we talk about how garbage the default keymappings are? They're really garbage. It seems to me that the keymappings were made with the intent to play by keyboard but anyone that has played a PC shooter since... I guess whatever came after this knows that the default keymappings should be made with the mouse in mind. 
I get that the game is free and the game is 20 years old. So I suppose that this game is purely for the nostalgia crowd. I Just don't see any excuses for why the game should play this poorly 20 years later. You're telling me over 20 years no one thought to update the default keybindings? And I guess this is the key problem. The authors seem to rely on "It's 20 years old". That's not a viable defense. If anything, it's the exact opposite of a defense. If I see a dude that has worked at a company for 20 years and he's still in the mailroom, is that a testament to his worth? If an abused wife stayed in a relationship for 20 years instead of seeking the help they desperately need, would we praise that wife or have pity for her? 
Again, I want to stress that flying ships is legitimately fun and does require some skill to play. But it has too many drawbacks in its released state for me to consider it viably. I'm sorry, but this is going to have to be a no from me.

Glad I found this game. It's a lot of fun. Well worth $2.49 for sure.
Granted, it's not designed to be a heavy bridge building simulator, it's just a simple arcade style game you might want to file under "Comedy", because I've had lots of laughs with it so far.
You don't actually build bridges with it, but you are doing stunts where a bridge is under construction. You have to build the perfect RAMP, or ingenuis pathway, to get to the other side and capture the checkered flag.
I also like the instant replay, the ability to save a replay, the ability to convert the replay into a video, and the ability to convert the video into a GIF. Totally setup to share the laughter with your friends for sure.
Not everything is entirely simple in this game. It does have a few challenges where you must use a little strategy without going over your construction budget. There are times when you must run a stage TWICE, once to grab a star along one possible route, and again to grab a bolt along another possible route. A few routes may seem impossible, but nothing is impossible in this game. There's always more than one way to get to where you want to go.
As far as stunts go, you're basically doing forward and reverse flips, BUT it's the way you DO THOSE FLIPS is what really counts in some situations. You might have to use other particular objects found at each site to give you some boost (hint, hint).
Theres really no right or wrong way to play this game. You can be serious with it, or goof off with it, or experiment with odd ramp designs in odd places that other people might not think about considering. With that being said, here's another clue... Just because it doesn't look like you should put a ramp there, it doesn't mean you can't. Just try it and see what happens. LOL

Okay, before you read this review you should know that this is a game I have been waiting a very long time for and the excitement grew to a very large calibur. With that being said, let's begin.
The Good ~
Graphics - Entering a server for this game, waiting a few moments for the textures and objects to pop in, and then looking around will leave you stunned. The game's textures a very extraordinary, the meshes are amazing, and the lighting is superb. You look around and find these amazingly destroyed structures with light shafts shining through and shadows that work properly unlike any other game. The graphics in this game rival that of single player games, and this is a pseudo-mmo with up to 64 players at once, it is something to be unexpected in this genre.
Variety - Scavenging through mounds of rubble and opening countless drawers opens the gates for mountains of variety. Whether it be food, water, guns, or melee weapons you will never be let down. From simple knives to gashing katanas, from F-Off Insect Repellent to Crunchy Benz corn chips. This game offers more than most in terms of vast variety. There is a huge number of enemies that the game offers. Ranging from giant brutes to little imp-like nether crawlers, even adding some flying scrapper-like things to make you fear the skies in certain areas.
Organization - While some games, especially games with such large numbers of players, suffer from poorly designed menus and terrible interfaces, it's hard for me to say that with this game. Everything in the menus is properly spaced and the design isn't too intrusive. It allows for immersion among the highest degree as you don't feel impeded on by having so many things in the foreground at once.
The Bad ~
Exploration - Okay, I am going to lead off with this because it seems to be the most controversial, When the game first was released for early access, you had just one part of a city, since then they have essentially doubled the size of the map, adding this infested, marsh-like location. This was great at first but then I realized how dismembered the landscape is, there are pieces of ground floating above where it should be, adding about a three foot gap of terrible, see-through land, the waterways become a hassle to navigate around because they take up so much of the area, the buildings are mostly closed off, and the area is terribly optimized lowering frame rate by 10-15 frames in some locations. This can all be seen passed though because the game looks so great in the areas that are polished and if you have patience then you can move around the number of blocked off paths. In the newer version of the game, they added locked storage containers, ammo boxes, the like. I am going to assume that they have higher grade items but I wouldn't know because it wouldn't even let me open them regardless of the fact that I bought ten keys from the store, also when I got killed on sight I seem to have lost my keys so that also was a bummer because I paid real money for those, but that was sort of to be expected. The problem with these locked units is that they have replaced so many of the normal storage containers. I went up four different sky scrapers, entered countless buildings, and searched a number of run down defenses to find one crowbar and a shotgun barrel, oh but there were twenty locked units so it's okay.
Gameplay - Now, the gameplay itself is rather simple. You have first person view and you are able to toggle between standing, crouching, and prone which is a staple of the First-Person Shooter genre. The problems stem from the game being unpolished. I can't count how many times I went to walk up a fire escape to find my character glitching through the railings and falling four to five stories to his death, or clipping against an object that would be so simple to walk over, yet I am not even allowed to jump over it and am forced to go around said object when I am being chased by countless enemies. There are problems with sprint not working when you press the shift key and crouch not sticking as well. The gameplay just needs to be touched up in order to make the experience worth-while.
-~-~-~-~
In conclusion, I can't say I recommend this game. I wanted to Love it so bad but the number of bugs and terrible designed updates just ruined the game for me and many others. In the state that it is in, avoid it like the plague. I really hope that these devs turn around and fix the mess that they created.

I've got to weigh in on this, namely  because I don't write reviews often, but also because this is a port of my favorite game from my childhood. This is a direct port of the mobile version that was released in 2014 for mobile devices. That's not necessarily a bad thing, unless you take issue with there being slight variations on the battle menu as well as some altered character art.
Is the character art good or bad? It doesn't take too much effort to figure that out for yourself. It isn't anything to write home about, but for me, it doesn't take me out of nor does it ruin the experience. The modding community has corrected that issue and you'll be happy to know that you can alter those appearances through modding and still earn achievements.
That said, the game will crash (still, as of August 2016) if you remove certain controllers during play, but that's the only issue I've encountered. This is a great game and you probably know what you're getting yourself into if you purchase it. Make a decision for yourself, but don't expect some radical change in the way Square Enix does business -- you won't find that here.

Oh god, I cannot remember how many times I have forgot how to spell/say the name of this game. Nihilumbra. Nihilumbra is a very original indie platformer that is actually very deep. The narration explains the character, Born, and his thoughts. Of course, assuming that they are a he. It's fairly standard 2D platforming here, except that it introduces the concept of drawing colours across the landscapes. You will use colours to solve the many puzzles in this, admittedly short game's, levels and defeating the many enemies the void throws at you. I won't spoil the lovely narration in the game however, that you can experience for yourself. However, after finishing the main story you unlock void mode. Which is boring as hell. Honestly, the game isn't really suited to dashing about and disposing with various void enemies in different and pretty frustrating ways. I honestly couldn't be bothered with it.
+ Great Narrative
+ Moving Story
+ Fun Platforming
+ Colour Mechanics
- Void Mode
- Short Playtime
A very interesting game, with beautiful artwork and a fun colour mechanic but... void mode is just painfully boring. It would have been much better to extend the main story mode of the game. Overall, a great indie title and particularly because it's fairly cheap.

I recently got this game through the promotion, so it was a free gift. I wanted to try this game out because I was tired of playing super serious games, and many reviews for the PSP version likened it to Zelda games. I'm interested in those, so I had a good outlook on this before it came out.
First and foremost, this game is NOT friendly to keyboard users. The controls are very flighty, and you can't keybind with the normal WASD setup. You are given a tutorial at the start of the game that explains that you can use the right click to move (which is incredibly odd). The problem here is that the character likes to take wide turns. Jumping, something that many games includes, is fairly nice in this; except for that god awful sound effect. SPROING, SPROING, SPROING. Don't hold the space bar down, use X to jump. The camera controls don't work in some places, leading to a poor view at times. In the starter town, these controls are pretty annoying and almost off-putting.
Audio quality is varying. I understand that this game is meant for younger audiences, so I will approach it as such. As said above, the jumping mechanic includes a very annoying sound effect. VERY annoying. I'm not far into the game, but I'm almost positive that jumping will be required, so I'll be subject to the torturous sound when I need to progress with jumping. I could go on and on about how bad the sound effect is, but I'll leave it there. Music is charming and enjoyable, but it's incredibly loud. I've got the volume set to its absolute lowest, and it's still very loud. I've had to lower my computer's max volume just to get it to a reasonable level. As for voice acting, I apologize to any of her fans, but the voice actress for Parin just sounds so bad. She's unenthusiastic, and her dialogue sounds like she's just reading the script and nothing more. The grandfather at the start sounds so lively and cheery, and then Parin talks and sounds boring. I've read elsewhere that the PSP version has optional Japanese audio, but the Steam release does not. Either way, the voice acting is pretty weak. As I was wandering around the starter town, I suddenly hear a LOUD not-dog barking. Really irritating sound, AND loud. I didn't expect to get spooked by a cartoony game.
Characters are pretty cut and dry in terms of tropes. Parin, the heroine, is the peppy young female who is always cheery. Her grandfather, Hyperbollic, is the flighty and forgetful old mayor who's fun to talk to. Then there's Cyllinder. HOW DID THIS GET APPROVED? He's practically a pedophile with how he talks to Parin. It's incredibly creepy. The first monster you meet, Pino, is the generic cutesy "mascot" kind of character in the sense that she shows up out of nowhere, gets into trouble with a simple animal, and is rescued by a girl who is the only one who can see her. The monsters, prior to obtaining the drill, are all goofy critters that you'd expect from a child-friendy series. Other than the pedophile, the characters are all alright.
Gameplay...First off, I skip cinematics. The dialogue mixed with the ridiculous volume and bad voice acting are enough to get annoyed with. Thankfully that can be turned off so I don't hear them. Luckily, there's boards that explain what to do. In the first dungeon, you learn how to attack, push objects, and dodge. You also learn a move where you can stay airborne for as long as you jump and attack enemies. That's pretty enjoyable. One thing that bothered me at the start was the meter up top with the moving stars, but that was explained as the method for getting critical hits. Now things die too easily since I'm good at rhythm games. Still, it's a nice mechanic, and probably the one thing I really like so far. After the first dungeon, you meet another character named Popon, who uses a sword rather than a drill. I couldn't stand her voice, so I didn't play as her for more than a minute (I didn't close the game to turn off voices at this point). The most hilariously bad aspect is that you can't equip the goggles you're given at the start of the game. This may be because I run around in one of the alternate costumes, but still.
Disregarding all of the glaring flaws, the core game is enjoyable even if the controls are flighty. In my opinion, playing the game muted is best, but that's just me. The story isn't anything fantastic, and the characters aren't all that unique, but it's pretty fun for a time waster. I'd GREATLY suggest getting the PSP version instead, since this game was obviously made for controllers instead of keyboards. I'm only selecting "Yes" for recommending since there's no "Maybe" option.
Also, that wardrobe lets you wear a skimpy leopard costume. On a little girl. Thanks, Japan!

Final Fantasy VI was one of my favorite RPG games on the SNES and still ranks as one of the best games I’ve ever played.  The game uses an ensemble cast and has one of the most engrossing story lines of any game I have ever played.
Unfortunately my first hour or two of the game as absolutely terrible.  I tried playing with a keyboard at first just to see what the game was like on the PC and it was almost unplayable.  The key bindings were in random places all over the keyboard and in desperation to try to figure out which keys performed which actions I accidentally pressed a key that caused me to lose complete control of my party during battle and I could not find the key I pressed to turn it off.  Had I not played the SNES version and seen how the game was intended to be played I would have ended my playthrough within the first hour and joined the string of negative reviews that barely had any time invested in this game.
I took a brief break and after calming down and decided I was going to write down the keybindings (or reassign them) so I could at least gain control of my party again.  Within a few seconds I then realized “why not try using a controller?” so I tried playing it again with the Steam Controller.   To my surprise it worked well with the Steam controller although it did take an hour or so to get completely comfortable with using the controller.  After I overcame that hurdle the experience was great.
The graphics had received an overhaul and while I loved how the backgrounds looked during combat I was not entirely sold on the new character sprites as they struck me as being a bit too childish for some of the models (and I am not a fan of Locke’s beer gut that they added).
As I found myself nearing the end of the game I was strongly considering whether or not I could give this game a positive review.  This probably ranks as the best game of all time for me and while I had enjoyed most of my playthrough I kept comparing it to the SNES version and was wondering how I could, with a clear conscience, recommend this game after the debacle that was my first hour of learning the controls when I should be recommending to someone that they play the SNES version instead.  I learned shortly afterwards that apparently this version of the game had two additional areas added as this was an indirect port of the GBA version of the game (I had no idea there had been a GBA release of the game).  These additional end game areas were barely enough to shift a negative review to a positive one although this was extremely close.
There isn’t too much in the way of replayability in this game but a full playthrough of the main game will likely take you around 30-35 hours (around 40-50 hours if you want to tackle the additional areas).
In summary this can be a great experience if you have a controller for your pc to play the game with.  If you don’t and are unwilling to get one then stay away from this version of the game.

Neat critical hit combat system involving the rhythm bar at the top of the screen, hit enemies in time with the music and deal extra damage. When you have a mechanic like this it's imperative to have a great soundtrack, and this game's got it. Great fun so far. Play with a controller for the best experience.

The good part:
The aspects i like the most of this game is the big variety of enemies, weapons and ships, it has great amounts of content, for example, there is one boss in most maps,  Tefat, Rotator, Dominator, Cleaner,  Motherbrain, and even tiny minibosses in some maps, the weapons feel refreshing and are very diverse, even the weapon itself can take different paths when you start upgrading the weapon individual technologies. also ships have unique weapons themselves.
The ambient of the game itself is here not very complex, music is decent enough and everything seems to fit good enough.
Taking into account the above, i think it has a good formula to be addictive
The bad part:
Despite having a fair amount of content and a relativelly good gameplay, it lacks on a lot of aspects too, such as:
-Missions get boring and repetitive eventually, i remember having a mission were i had to kill 900 enemies in an specific system, later i had to kill 300 bigger enemies and than around 100 in an even harder system, thats up to 1300! REALLY?, THATS INSANE!, considering the fact that a third of those 1300 enemies were a lot harder than the initial 900.
missions can be separated in 3 categories, Killing, Landing, Collecting, collecting is not different than killing, because you kill -> you collect, and landing is in either a planet or a station.
-Clan system being too simple. there is something called "Planet wars" wich rewards you and your clan with "Troons", wich  give small boosts to your ship. yet its so boring, your only task in planet wars is to jump from system to system, and land on planets that are not captured by any other clan... Troons feel like a weak reward for repeating this over and over.

-Dead pvp system. Nothing much to say about this, it probably needs more players, but it kinda feels pointless sinse the rewards are just... basically the same, as a reward, they give you some resources that are relative to your performance in the match, also this system is used in many games. note that you can go in hostile alternative maps, that give you better artifacts or loot, wich seems to be worth sinse most of those maps are empy...
-Extremely grind based, seriusly, steel is the main resource used for upgrading equipment or buying weapons, yet is so frustrating to get. The grind is insane in this game and if you're not familiar with griding for hours to lvl up a thing, you probably shouldnt touch this game.
-Some payd elements feel odd and are rather overpriced or simply not worth.
There is this tractor beam, wich is not even a permanent purchase, but a rent, you pay an amount of flux that is equal to 5 dollars, just to speed up your looting during a week. and its something as basic as a beam that drags loot to your ship.
There is also this ship that costs 11.900 Flux... wich according to some players, its not even close to be worth, sinse there are better ship for a third of that price.
You got to pay 100 to even change your name or nick, wich honestly is a bit annoying, not a big deal though.
The conclusion of this review is:
The game is not for everybody, it puts some requirements for you to enjoy this game, the grind could be the main problem in my opinion. despite being very addictive at the beginning, the concept of this game is interesting, but some aspects are simply too plain or poorly executed.
¿Would i recommend this game?:
To an average probably wouldnt, In the short term you'll get hookd wthout a doubt. but in the long term you'll realize that, the game is not worth enough or will become a bit tiring.
POST DATA: if this game happends to correct in the long term the issues i stated in here, without a doubt i will update this review and maybe give it a thumbs up.

I know that this amount of text is intimidating but hear me out. Now that I am at almost 730 hours played at the time of this review's publication I thought it was time for me to review my favorite game. This is not going to be a typical review where they say something along the lines of "swam in the air, 79 out of 10 would be break laws of physics again," although that has happened to me and it was hilarious. This is going to be an in depth and honest review of Arma 3. But now though here is some context.
When Arma 3 first came out in 2013 I was so excited because I had been watching Arma 2 for so long, and I was really hyped on the Arma 3 trailers, not that I actually had a good enough computer to play either one of them of course, so I waited until I finally did. I waited for 3 1/2 years watching YouTube videos and wishing that I could have Arma 3, It was sheer torment, all the cool things that people did just made the situation worse: every valiant last stand against zombies that saved the city, every stealth mission that crippled the enemy, every scuba mission that destroyed an enemy vessel while in port, every close air support gun run that saved a convoy that was under threat just made me want Arma 3 more. So when I finally had a computer that was good enough to play games on it one of the first games that I got was Arma 3.
Arma 3 was nothing like I had expected it to be, it was better. An entire virtual sandbox for me to do anything I wanted, go anywhere I wanted, play any way I wanted. It was not like a "sophisticated Battlefield" or a "Call of Duty on steroids" like I was expecting it to be, it was better. Those descriptions don't even remotely do the game justice. The modding support is astounding to say the least, like I said earlier, zombies. The maps are gorgeous, the weapons are wonderfully modeled, and you have a fully customizable character from the face, to the clothes, to the voice. Arma 3 is more than meets the eye, sure it’s beautiful, but it also has a great deal of depth behind that gorgeous high polygon count tree, and highly reflective water, and I love it to death for it.
Many people say that Arma 3 has a steep learning curve and I disagree. You pick up new things very quickly in Arma, or at least I do. Arma 3 just has so much to learn that many people think that it is a very difficult game to play when it is not. Almost everytime I play Arma 3 I learn something new about the game or how to play it more effectively. It does not matter whether this is some knowledge about how to use Zeus more effectively, if it is some new tactic for clearing houses, or even if it is a technique on how to get more stable frame rate. Even with my amount of play time, and the amount of videos I have watched on Arma 3, I am still learning new things constantly. I believe that fact alone sets Arma 3 apart from other games.
Arma 3 is in some ways the next logical step for somebody who is into the first person shooter genre, you probably don't know what they say about the game but here it is anyway "children play Call of Duty, boys play Battlefield, men play Arma," and I feel like this is true, the Arma series just feels mature to me, and much more refined than Call of Duty or Battlefield as well. They are not games where you can easily be a "super duper MACV recon SOG SEAL Delta force Green beret CIA operator, go gunz blazin, and kill all dem dudes over dere," although that sometimes works much to my own surprise and amusement. Arma 3 requires at least some modicum of strategy, or my personal favorite, a great big helping of luck to win, or even be good at in some cases.
Arma 3 has a large amount of multiplayer content that somebody can enjoy, you can play on a life server and rise through the ranks to become whatever you want to be, whether you want to be are a brutal crime lord, or the mayor of the town. The king of the hill servers bring a nice challenge to Arma 3 where you can fight in and against, in a perfect world, a well organized group of players who are trying very diligently to accomplish their objectives in Arma 3's virtual world. If you somehow don't like the sound of this then just play it for the LOLz.
The singleplayer content of Arma 3 is quite good, I am very much enjoying the new "Stepping Stone campaign," where NATO forces are trying to seize the picturesque island of Malden in an attempt to attain and maintain aerial dominance over the critically important Strait of Gibraltar. Furthermore the "Apex Protocol campaign" is very well made in my opinion with several missions that make you feel like you really are a super duper MACV recon SOG SEAL Delta force Green beret CIA operator, another great thing about the Apex Protocol campaign is that it gives you the option of playing it with friends.
Arma 3 is a somewhat underappreciated treasure in the gaming world with endless content and unlimited scenarios to explore and it deserves more publicity than it is getting. I hope that this review was helpful to you and informative as well. Furthermore I hope that it didn’t bore you to death too much. Anyways you have a great day now.

First things first: For Honor is not a perfect game, but it also doesn't deserve the terrible rating it's getting on steam because of technical difficulties. Honestly this is the problem with these reviews being recommend or not recommend, because games like this look like♥♥♥♥♥♥just based on their overall rating. If you're here and you feel kind of iffy about buying a game that as of today has a poor approval rating of roughly 60%, I urge you to remember that people who face a combination of technical issues and a very challenging competitive game are far more likely to come on here and give a♥♥♥♥♥♥review than the people enjoying it are to come over here  and tell you why you should buy it.
Let me just adress the technical difficulties. They definitely exist, though I haven't seen much of them personally. I don't know exactly what is causing specific people to get it constantly or if they're just exaggerating, because it is very frustrating when it happens. But I can tell you that with a good internet connection and open NAT it is at least anecdotally possible to  play with little to no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t tech stuff. The most frustrating tech part for me has been that the matchmaker sometimes tries to put me into a full game and I get kicked back to the map menu. I have been dropped from a couple of matches, but not a significant percentage by any means.
All in all; if you have a good internet connection and you have or are willing to open ports to make your NAT open, then I do not think you should let the talk about technical difficulties stop you. If you're not confident in your connection, maybe wait until there is a sale or the tech difficulties are fixed, or both.
As for the gameplay, I think it's great. The game is all about reactions, mindgames and matchup knowledge. The skill ceiling is crazy high and I am personally definitely stuck on the floor for now. I could try to explain how the system works or why it's good, but if you're wondering about that I would rather say you should take some time and watch different top streamers on twitch.
One thing that frustrates a lot of people is the possibility for enviromental kills. The idea that you may be winning a duel and then you just suddenly get thrown off a ledge and it's over. And well... it's in the game, and can be quite frustrating when it happens. Usually people dont try to do it too much if you play 1v1 or 2v2, but sometimes they do and in the other modes expect people to play as dirty as they can. The best thing I can tell you if you hate the idea of it is to learn how to counter guard breaks, it should save you a lot of grief.
You will see a lot of people talk about OP classes, either because they are consistently crushed by it themselves or often because they've heard streamers talk about it. Honestly, the difference in power is negligable unless you play at the highest level. As in all games some characters are better at some levels of play and against some playstyles. If someone talks about how OP the berserker is, chances are they dont have good enough reactions to block and parry them, or they're trying to go aggressive and get counter attacked by a faster class. Then there's also the lack of knowledge of what a character does, how the matchups work, the game mechanics and so on and so on. The game is not perfectly balanced, no competetive game where you have unique characters will be, but it is not unbalanced or filled with OP chars like a lot of people would have you believe just because they can't face the idea that they might need to put actual effort in to learn the game.

SOMA is a rich narrative woven around a solid set of core game mechanics and wrapped in a cohesive, hard science fiction shell. I haven't been so immersed in an video game experience on an emotional level in a very long time. The writing in this game is sharp, on the level of the Portal series though with a different tone, and the philosophical conundrums it presents run much deeper than those games... and most games for that matter. Or most science fiction in general. It's a great, captivating narrative-driven experience is what it is, and I enjoyed it thoroughly. If that's what you're looking for then you've found it. Great job, Frictional Games!
On the subject of gameplay, I'm not particularly a fan of the horror genre however I found that there was an ideal balance between the horror elements and the puzzle elements in this game to prevent the horror elements from being too nerve wracking. I found the balance and the core gameplay mechanics to be better than, say, Alien: Isolation which is the closest recent game I can think of to this (and the pacing was also better). I really enjoyed the interaction system as well--it is simple yet very versatile and helps greatly with the immersion (it really makes for some tense moments!)
Graphically, the environments in this game are generally amazing despite being on what would seem to be an indie budget. The engine definitely shines at the bottom of the ocean and not so much on land; thankfully most of the game takes place in the former.
The audio is nothing short of excellent as well. From the voice acting to the ambient sounds to monsters wailing, the game wouldn't be anywhere near as good as it is without solid audio production.
Play this with a good set of headphones!

Let me get this straight, you want me to tell you a review about this game? Whoever you are, you might as well go to the curators, because if you've come for a review on this game, you've come to the wrong place. However, if you have come for an outstanding chocolate chip cookie recipe, you've come to the right place.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Ingredients
1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter
3/4 cup packed dark brown sugar
3/4 cup sugar
2 large eggs
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
1 (12-ounce) bag semisweet chocolate chips, or chunks
2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
3/4 teaspoon baking soda
1 teaspoon fine salt
Directions
1. Evenly position 2 racks in the middle of the oven and preheat to 375 degrees F. (on convection setting if you have it.) Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone sheets. (If you only have 1 baking sheet, let it cool completely between batches.)
2. Put the butter in a microwave safe bowl, cover and microwave on medium power until melted. (Alternatively melt in a small saucepan.) Cool slightly. Whisk the sugars, eggs, butter and vanilla in a large bowl until smooth.
3. Whisk the flour, baking soda and salt in another bowl. Stir the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients with a wooden spoon; take care not to over mix. Stir in the chocolate chips or chunks.
4. Scoop heaping tablespoons of the dough onto the prepared pans. Wet hands slightly and roll the dough into balls. Space the cookies about 2-inches apart on the pans. Bake, until golden, but still soft in the center, 12 to 16 minutes, depending on how chewy or crunchy you like your cookies. Transfer hot cookies with a spatula to a rack to cool. Serve.
5. Store cookies in a tightly sealed container for up to 5 days.
For a Rocky Road Bar:
1. Lightly butter a 9 by 13-inch baking pan. Make the batter as per cookie recipe and fold in 1 cup chopped walnuts along with the chocolate chips. Spread batter in prepared pan. Bake until the edges are light brown and the batter sets, about 45 minutes. Cool slightly and cover surface with 4 cups marshmallows and 1 cup chocolate chips. Broil at least 8 inches from the heat until marshmallows turn golden brown, about 2 minutes. (Keep an eye on the marshmallows, and turn the pan frequently--they go from golden to char in a wink.) Cool, cut and serve.

Wow. This game was a giant rollercoaster for me. I started this game with high hopes, because Amnesia: TDD was a great game. This game was just as great, if not better, but for different reasons.
Pros:
+Amazing story, because it deals with intelligent and thought provoking subject matter, while not feeling belittling or being too complex. All the elements grow nicely together, characters interact in a way that one might expect under these circumstances, and the ending is quite bittersweet.
+Looks pretty good. Some textures are kinda blurry when up close, there are some lag issues here and there, and when continuing a game textures take some time to load in, but overall this game looks nice, and the visuals help the atmosphere a lot.
+Sound design is amazeballs. SOMA takes a great step forward when compared to the sound in Amnesia. Everything sounds and feels the way one would expect when underwater. It's somewhat hollow, and feels more bass-y. When not submerged, sound is quite nice, and the way the sound and visuals work together when the mosnters appear left me pretty shaken.
+Monster design and variety is pretty good. There were a few too many in some areas, but I don't think the game suffered too much due to this. Every monster has a way to get past it, that only takes a few moments to figure out.
+Scares are good. Whether it be something ambient like the lights flickering, or having a monster chase you, you'll jump at least once. Even after dying to a monster and knowing how to deal with it, having any of them stomp up to you is pretty nerve wracking, and might make you cringe while waiting to be hit.
+ Moral choices out the wazoo. Seriously, a lot of choices you make in this game will leave you feeling as though you did the wrong thing, and it may have been better to take an alternate route. There's a lot of "which is the lesser of two evils" presented throughout the story, and sometimes you don't even realize you can do something else until after the fact.
Cons:
- Optimization issues. Not game breaking, but can be annoying at times.
- Monsters may be too frequent for your taste, really depends on how you feel.
- Character interaction is mostly spot on, but some reactions and interactions are questionable. Not enough to bring you out of the story, but it may stand out to a few of you.
- Feels very linear, but also really open. SOMA has this strange shift between areas being too open and taking a lot of needless time to get through, but other areas are far too linear and it feels like more could have been done with them. Overall I enjoyed the level design, but this may definitely irk some people.
TL:DR-
I would HIHGLY recommend this game. It has its flaws, but I don't think they're big enough to not recommend it. Frictional Games is good at horror, and they have proven to me that they can write a quite engaging and thought provoking story. If you want a good spooky game that isn't super cliche and has a well written story, pick this up immediately.

So I decided to write this because they're are plenty of misguided reviews regarding this game and I think it's unfair to not try and counter some.
One review particularly, which was the first review on this page at the time of writing, got my attention by completely misunderstanding what this game was and what it was about. On actually correcting the wrong things in the review (ironically, everything) they removed my comment. Anyway I won't name the person here out of respect but there name rhymes with PrudlerTheHorse...
I will also use their review as a template.

You will not find next gen graphics here, there are no 4k textures. It's a hacking "simulator" therefore it doesn't need fancy graphics, hackers use command consoles and code to initiate commands not fancy buttons and iPhone apps. This is a bare bones approach. It still has added UI for the people who don't just want a console, with helpful information and visuals, so for a hacking simulator, it's actually very visual.
If you get this game and complain about it just being a console and a few graphical information modules, then you are stupid. You get exactly what you see. You wouldn't complain on a game like papers please, that it didn't have the best graphics in the world.
This game is hard, it's supposed to be. The learning curve is not steep in terms of mechanics but the puzzle lies within analyzing data on servers to find the next step in the path. It's about being intuitive, it's about being savvy with resources (bounced servers/proxies, money, trace percentage), it's about actually reading stuff and not getting spoon fed.
The tutorial gives you everything you need, it gives you a few hotkeys to bring up help/goals etc. and then guides you through a basic scenario. If you constantly fail at the tutorial then blame yourself not the game. I have had no problems with the tutorial so it's a user problem, not a game problem. Again, it's like complaining dark souls is too hard because they don't force feed you instructions on the tutorial.
In terms of a hacking simulator, the mechanics are there. Actual console commands are used as well as the functionality of a console (pressing arrow keys to recall previous commands). You can also use tab to autocomplete commands. The typing is not long winded and anyone who has used a computer for more than a few days should have no trouble typing.
Secondly, it's a hacking game. Hacking = typing, expect to do a lot of it. Game analogy number 3: go complain stardew valley has too much farming.
There are a few good non-recommended reviews however and a lot of good points against this game. The gameplay is very punishing, I don't believe it's that punishing (at least as far as I've got) though. However, the point that the game is far too linear, in terms of only having one or two ways of actually getting the information and the endgame from each scenario. If the game was a bit more lenient in terms of the amount of trace you get each time and therefore allocation of exploration, it would lead to a much better open experience.
As I hear the newest game is exactly that, open world hacking. Not too sure on the games that proceed this, as I want to play through this first but I just wanted to point out some issues people have with the game as it's been bringing down the rating unjustifiably.

For a bit of background my ideal game would be a full PvP, full loot medieval mmo. Similar to the MUD's of old!
This is a tricky one. On one hand I love the concept of the game and it does seem to run quite smoothly however it is extremely long winded which in itself isn't necessarily a bad thing but a new player should be aware of it.
Crafting isn't overly intuitive and requries frequent looking at the wiki. Combat was straight forward enough, similar to Mount and Blade or War of Roses (although not as good). The biggest let down for me is the claimed areas which are fully protected against looting or damage, some servers have a judegement period but this just seems like a cheap cop out. This has always been the way though has it not? Crafters and PvE'rs wanting safe zones but the PvP'rs after at least the chance to wage war. This also prevents terraforming in the zone as well which is frustrating when people claim the zones next to an essential resource. I understand that this is done to prevent griefing when players are offline but it would be better if you could hire NPC's to guard your land or had player areas that would respawn after a certain time unless they were taken out my seige weapons and claimed by another group.
Overall I wish Steam allowed for a maybe reccomendation. The keep building is fun and coming across other player settlements is great and it really is pretty free with what you can build and where. I think it has a solid base game here and will grow into something good albiet not what I am after. For people who like building their own bases, limited PvP and a free roam area it is a good bit (assuming you have plenty of time).For me though the search for a full loot mmo continues.

Hamlet or the Last Game without MMORPG Features, Shaders and Product Placement is the original point-and-click adventure game based on twisted William Shakespeare's Hamlet. Solve logic puzzles and fight with monsters to uncover secrets, punish all the villains and rescue the princess.
Hamlet is a very short room-by-room puzzle adventure, more of an art showcase than a full video game. Still, the absurd humour splashed on the classic stage play may find its way to the appropriate audience.
Key Features
In the best traditions of classic adventure games,The first indie game in the world based on Shakespeare's Hamlet,25 levels,Boss battles,Logic puzzles,No inventory
To carry out this epic quest, our Hero must solve a series of puzzles, arranged in a format that would fit web-based games: you are presented with a single scene, and you need to manipulate objects to be able to leave the room. Some of the puzzles are straightforward, some need good reflexes, and some are really devilish in design by looking extremely difficult, yet having a painfully simple solution.
All in All

+ Action packed, fast paced and exciting singleplayer campaign.

+ Good controls for PC, which is not always the case for a lot of games released these days.

- Story, while reasonable, could improve greatly and lift the score for this game.
- Multiplayer is literally full of young kids. No realism or authenticity here, the guns are awkward to use, the maps unimaginative and it is plagued by the typical problems with multiplayer, like spawn camping. As a whole, it's a boring multiplayer experience.
Overall Score: 7/10
Medal of Honor is a fun singleplayer game and that's probably all you need to know to buy it. Sure, it doesn't last long, but those 7-8 hours are good. Multiplayer does suck, so if you're purchasing for that reason alone, I'd say avoid.

-REVIEWER, REVIEW.
I got this game for free - however, from what I rember from when I last played the game (not the steam release) the game was pretty darn fun. Now that I'm looking at it, there's 2 things so far that have slightly annoyed me - the controls. To put it bluntly, at the moment, when playing with a 360 controller, it kind of feels like your wrestling with it, on default controlls. However, that is my opinion, but remapping some of the controllers makes it a lot easier to play through - especialy helping, for me, with not pressing attack, when I meant to jump - and doing so, having to restart a platforming section. Aside from that, the next and final issue I've found is that the subtitles look out of place, as in, they look almost fuzzy. To put it bluntly the game looks good, but then the subs look wrong - almost out of place.
EDIT: ONE MORE ISSUE;
The cutscenes. The cutscenes are jarring, in comparison to the rest of the game. In my opinion, they could recieve an update, however if you're not running this in 1920x1080, I can't comment on how they'd look. Despite this, the game is still over all pretty good. Though, it is only some - the consistensy on how the cutscenes/animations look isn't exactly there
EDIT:
;
The lips don't sync up. Yep. That's it. It's kind of like you're watching a realy badly dubbed anime. You know,  it's translated, it's animated nicely, but you can't quite keep yourself looking at it. You can't quite get a true grasp of how the game looks, preforms and operates, it's jarring. It's a small, but extremley noticable things - to the point, one character wasn't talking, but their lips were moving (insert a joke about the Meghan Trainor song here)
Aside from that, the graphics look pretty good - a cutesy cell shaded graphics style, the voices fit, the music is excelent, comedic timing is pretty good - and a few of teh jokes directed at characters made me chuckle a fair bit, an
combat system - over all, it's pretty good. I'd give it a 7/10. Not the best game, but considering it's old, and a port, it's not too shabby. The problems could be improved, and the in game dialogue regarding controller inputs could be changed based upon what it detects as per the game pad  (y being refered to in game as z, being the most noticable one). If you want to see as to whether or not this game is for you - just look at a lets player, mute the person playing if you want, but judge it from how it looks.
UPDATE 3;
I've put in another hour or so of gameplay. The game's style changes, it appears as though it was only the opening animation to the "monster viliage" area of the game, which was so different compared to the rest. That being said, the voices dosn't get any better through out the game, furthermore, I've actualy noticed that bits of people are  translucent, like you can see the mane characters gloves and you can see her mouth, or other characters through them, almost as though the body parts are made of tissue paper. At the moment, I'd strongly reccomend this game, however if you don't like action rpgs, then this game will not be for you. You might get kicks out of the comedic aspect, but the gameplay - you probably won't like the combo - rythm system that the game takes, for it's fighting portions of the game.
NOTES; I'm currently playing the game on an AMD FX8350 and an R9 270x, running the built in amd catylst vsync.

Edit from the grave (9/4/2017): If any of you are reading reviews to see whether or not to play this game: take some of these reviews with a grain of salt. I wasn't actually planning on making edits to this review, but some of the past complaints of "high level players stealing boss kills" are particularly amusing, since XP scaling dictates that the only bosses new players have access to aren't even worth sneezing at by high level players.
Not only are they amusing, but I find a couple of these specific "not recommended" reviews ironic, since I distinctly remember another veteran player and I having to intervene on at least two of these separate occasions when dozens of new Steam players were complaining about being kept from the first boss by players that attempted farm them solo. (Oddly enough, they didn't consider it "kill stealing" when they were the ones receiving the loot.) Of course, once we interrupted them to give a kill to the little guys, they threw up their metaphorical hands, shook their fists at us meddling kids, and decided to settle the score with an all-powerful thumbs down.
Why they had such a knee-jerk reaction is beyond me. Perhaps they don't like people being kind to new players. Perhaps they don't like cooperation. Perhaps they didn't like our suggestion that they could create their own private game instance, in which they could farm whatever they want, whenever they want, without any distractions. But I'm thinking - and this is just a hunch here - that laziness won, and if they couldn't play the game exactly how they wanted, then nobody should play the game.
All of that being said: I feel a bit sad that a grindy, somewhat laggy, but ultimately *fun* game is having potential players driven away by reviews of a couple sour players.
---------------------------------------------------------------------
In a game that rewards players with bonus XP for grouping up, the only time you see the words "kill stealing", is when  why are some of these reviewers complaining about having their boss kills (plural) stolen? And what's in it for high level players that will get +1XP from a boss kill?

I was intimidated upon hearing about the premise of this game... It sounds like one of those games that are only fun to people with very specialized knowledge and tastes. But actually the developers have succeeded in making a very approachable and fast game about economy, business and finance, with clear tutorials and interface, and with a focus on multiplayer but still having a fun singleplayer experience.
Every building needs special materials and produces something else, but all materials can be bought or sold at the market, with dynamic prices based on supply and demand. Imagine if in warcraft 2, you could sell your extra lumber to other players. There's no military combat here, but economic attacks, defense and espionage are integral to the game.
You may be interested in the premise or not, but don't skip the game fearing that it will be too complicated. The mechanics are simple at the core, and may teach you an abstract thing or two about how business works in the real world.

I forgot how much I loved this game, I have always considered it one of my favorites if not -the- favorite game of mine in the FF franchise. I'll be honest, when I was thinking about replaying it my mind went "Meh, it's kinda dated." I looked at some screenshots and that didn't help, eventually I did pick it back up then and I was almost instantly hooked and getting nostalgic butterflies in my stomach! Don't make my mistake, despite it's age the story still holds up, and the art due to being 2D is still beautiful, it doesn't age quite as poorly as blocky 3D graphics (*cough* FF7 *cough*).
As a game, it's a must play, no matter your preconception please do yourself a favor and at least try it for a few hours, if the FF style of games appeal to you at all, you will almost certainly love this installment.
Now for the quality of the port:
A lot of the changes in this version will be completely opinion based, and refer to your taste.. First of these are the art, one of the biggest selling points of the steam version is the improved graphics, some people don't like it, personally I love it and it's the main reason I picked this game up on steam, not really much to say about it other than this is higher resolution versions of the old art we know and love, obviously being in higher resolution it will look a bit different, but no drastic changes has been made.
Second is the writing, the conversation has been smoothed out a lot and feels more fluent and modernized in comparison to the slightly awkward but more direct translation of the PS or SNES version. For old time fans it's always painful when this sort of thing is messed with, we loved that translation and grew up with it. But there is no question that the Steam translation is better and more fluent in an objective sense, it comes down to each individual what they would rather have. Ideally for me i'd want what's closest to the original japanese script, but since I don't know fluent japanese it's kinda hard to tell which one that is, and as someone who DO know a -bit- of Japanese I can also say that as a language it's not really possible to do a direct translation since the structure of the language is completely different, in the end it's just going to boil down to personal taste.
The menus feel a bit like they were made to play on a phone, it's a bit annoying that the cheapened out in this regard and seems to have taken this straight from their mobile version, but in the end the menu's are still cleaner and more visible than the original ones so I would still have to count it as a pro, I am especially happy about the way your spell menu looks in battle. Speaking of battle UI, I personally found it very distracting and annoying that the menu's would rise with the ATB gauge, THIS CAN BE CHANGED IN SETTINGS, please keep that in mind - it looks a lot better turned off and with a classic ATB gauge.
Overall I think this version is getting a lot of uneccessary hate, it's a decent port even though it could have been better in some regards. The only problem I had with it is that the keyboard controls can clash with name entry, for an example if you like me change your directional keys to wasd, when you click right to go to the confirm button during a character naming sequence you add a D to it, so now you are stuck with Terrad, and I had changed my confirm button to my space bar which instead added a space to the name. Annoying, but avoidable if you just change your keys, I decided to just stick with the arrow buttons and got confirm on TAB which is completely fine. Luckily in a turn based game reaction speed isn't really that important so none ideal controls is not the end of the world.
In the end, I recommend picking this version if you are a new player, and even as a returning one considering it purely for the art upgrade like me, it's worth the 14€ I payed.
