After spending an unhealthy amount of time in this game I think I can give you a good review. It is addictive, frustrating and refreshing all at the same time, but is not without some flaws.
The game overall
For Honor is basically a fighting game. Although people are dubbing it a hack and slash, if you are looking for that, look away for this is anything but. There are combos, dodges, throws, blocks and guard breaks to break those blocks. There's stances and various other trickery such as feints to throw your opponent off their rhythm. These are all given their own flavour over 12 classes spread over 3 factions.
The game does have a story mode, which can be completed on your lonesome or with a friend, but it's not more than a lenghty tutorial to paint the backdrop as to why everyone is dicing and slicing each other. There are also numerous tutorials to help you get to grips with the combat system as there's quite a steep learning curve.
The online portion of the game consists of various modes and is where the meat of the game lives. Duel and brawls are where gear stats are ignored and it's down to your skill in a 1v1 or 2v2. Then there's the modes where gear stats and special abilities can be used. Deathmatches, which see 4 of you fighting to eliminate the other team and prevent revives or to gain points by doing this untill one side reaches 1000, then it's down to whoever wipes the other team first. Then the Dominion mode, which is the same idea but centered around capping points.
All of these can be played vs AI cooperativley or vs Players. All of them are stupidly fun.
Characters level up individually and there's a wealth of unlockables and loot to change the way your character looks and plays. You can play with a keyboard and mouse just fine but I would recommend a controller due to the fighting style of the game.
Matchmaking and Online
Ubisoft has started to address some of the issues with online play but it is what you'd expect from a Ubisoft game. Sometimes there are strange bugs and errors in connecting and as it runs via peer to peer sometimes the connection drops out entirely or has to 'resynch'. Matchmaking is a little slower than I'd like but it's not awful, sometimes its good to step away for a moment. You can get some odd pairings or end up with 3 bots on a team vs a full player team. I am hoping they'll address this, but who knows. I've not had any issues with cheating, that I've noticed, but I am sure it happens.
Matches don't drag out forever for the most part and you can leave with no penalty for you will be replaced with a bot. I should mention the AI is good in this game and will use all options available, including responding to and making quick chat or taunts.
I don't exactly make it sound like a fun experience but the gameplay itself, in my opinion, makes up for any short comings the online mode has.
DLC and Cash Shop
Again, it's ubisoft so there is a cash shop. It is however a better model than you may have seen previously. Most of the items in the cash shop are for convienience because you don't want to wait untill you are level 19 like the rest of us, gosh darnit! or because you want to look cool.
Both of these things are a little redundant because everything becomes unlocked with actual gameplay and if you practice or put the time in having things like 'feats' unlocked aren't of huge consequence. All of the cosmetic stuff is buyable with ingame currency and most of your characters look is determined by unlockables and gear rarity anyway.
This is where it gets a little worse on the cash shop front. You can buy currency, which I think is perhaps a bit over priced. You can also use this currency to not only buy crates for higher gear but also buy a 'Champion Status' which allows you to level up faster and sometimes get better loot drops at the end of a match. If people in your group/team are also 'Champions' you get an additional XP boost.
It is again, more of a convienience thing, the only way this is impactful is you can level characters up faster and have more of an idea of play style. The gear drops aren't really substantial enough to cause an issue as even if you do secure a rare drop as loot, it most likely won't fit your play style and you still have to upgrade it. These stats on the gear are ignored in duels too, but it is worth being aware this cash shop mechanic is in place.
One thing also worth noting is that all DLC for this year is free for everyone and will include 6 new characters, with season pass players getting a week headstart. It's certainly better than a flat out pay to win model.
UI, Optimisation and Graphics
The UI is drenched in that ubisoft formula. There is a lot to look at, it's not detrimental to the game play but it is something to be aware of. The art style is obviously following that ubisoft formula but it's not cliche or cheesy (apart from a few emote animations that are meant to be obnoxious, sun beams, cherry blossoms and edgelord darkness anyone?). The graphics themselves are clean, think skyrim with ubisoft and occasional chromatic aberration. But most importantly, it runs smoothly, I've encountered very little stutter at high settings, with a lower end skylake set up, I run at a solid 80 fps.
Overall
If you are the sort of person looking to button mash or will get angry at 3v1, rather than learning how to deal with stuff, you might get a bit tired of this game so maybe wait to buy it.
However, if you are a fan of fighting style games, enjoy thinking strategically about PvP, like learning movesets and honing your timing, this is a fantastic game. The mix of genres alongside the combat system is unforgiving, refreshing and addictive. If you're bored of FPS or MMO PvP this is a great remedy and I would highly recommend giving it a go.

Okay. I'm going to give this an honest review, even though I've been a fanboy for this game since it was announced.
GAMEPLAY
First off, it's a fun game to play. Wading through opponents, cutting through your enemies, and killing them in grand fashion never gets old. The "Art of Battle" system works beautifully, and no two characters fight the same. A lot of people are already griping about "OP toons this, spamming that." However, in my honest opinion, there is a way to fight each individual character. You don't want to allow a spear user to maintain their gap. You don't want a twin axe wielding berzerker closing said gap. Every character has their strengths, and obvious weaknesses. The "Art of Battle" system is very involved, and it seems the gaming community is either loving it, or scowling at it. (The people that just want to play an x-y-b button masher seems to be the ones that don't enjoy it.)
Using the environment to your advantage is also a great system. Slamming people into walls stuns them, throwing them off cliffs or high areas kills them isntantly, (although people seem to resort to this more often than actually fighting). You can also slam people into walls that have hazards such as fire or spikes, making the Batman Begins saying that much more true. "Always mind your surroundings."
The Faction War is very involved, and I applaud them for making it truly a cross platform map. The game modes need a tad bit of work. The Team DM modes seem useless, because everyone only enjoys one of them, which is Elimination. Dueling mode keeps honorable 1v1 fights in the spotlight, especially for those that hate being ganked by a horde of enemies. Dominion works beautifully, and is a joy to play.
The only real gripe I have about gameplay is one thing. Cross faction play.
It's more a personal thing. If you swear allegiance to a faction, you shouldn't be able to pick a toon from another faction.  Just a personal opinion. If this were the case, damn near everyone would be Samurai due to the Orochi and Nobushi spammers.
GAMEPLAY SCORE - 9.5/10
SOUND
Swords clashing, battle drums, cruching bones, and the sound of screams when you tear someone apart or throw them off a cliff is magical. It really gets you into the mood.
SOUND SCORE - 9/10
GRAPHICS
No complaints. It's a rich and gorgeous looking game, with plenty of eye candy. You take damage, and can plainly see the wounds that were inflicted. On Ultra, you can even see your own blood spread as your bleed out, and the spray from another opponent decorates your weapons and shields.
Only complaint here is the lighting. No real glimmer on shining armor when in the sun. Did the Knights paint all their armor matte gray?
GRAPHICS SCORE - 8.5/10
ONLINE
Oh... this is where we start seeing the game's less that stellar workings. P2P connections are a bane to matches. Lag is ever present, games are rife with disconnects, and are not puniched in any way... and how does the game counter this? By adding a skill-less bot to the match and giving the enemy team a distinct advantage.
Uplay. That's all I need to say about that. Horrible platform.
Also, micro-transactions day one? I seem to see a lot of people with ALL classes, ALL executions, and ALL special effects unlocked already, (which costs roughly 30,000 steel to unlock all for ONE toon.) I understand today's gamers want everything from the beginning, and don't want to earn their stuff... but this is ridiculous. I have half the stuff for my Warlord, and I've been playing since day one. See my time played? That's how long it took. Then some 12 year old with his daddy's wallet can get all the stuff for 40 bucks.
ONLINE SCORE 2/10
Overall, this game is complete joy to play. However, it's connection issues and Uplay are a bane upon it. Introduce dedicated servers, and maybe a punishment for people that leave their teams high and dry.. and this game will be flawless.
OVERALL SCORE - 8/10

One of my all-time favorite games. Nihilumbra is a side-scrolling puzzle game, where you control the lone protoganist, Born, guiding him through five varied realms. Born is alone, too- aside from the enemies in the game, which are few and far between, every landscape you travel through seems abandoned, deserted. It adds an apocalyptic feel to an already stark and melancholy game.
Born starts out with very few tricks up his sleeve- he can jump and move inexorably to the right, and the enemies he encounters are deadly. As you progress, though, you pick up new skills that allow you to alter the landscape around you- colors you can paint on the world to allow you to slide, bounce, stick, and more.
There's really two parts to this game- the story mode, which is relatively straight-forward but still retains a challenge, and the mode you unlock after beating the story, which is devilishly hard. The controls seemed fluid to me, though they take some getting used to- one hand moves Born, while the mouse uses the various colors to guide him along. The game rarely rushes you, and when it does, it's considerate enough to provide enough checkpoints to prevent too much repetition.
This seems to be Beautifun's Freshman game for the PC, and I am definitely looking forward to where they'll go from here.

Tactical team shooter of up to 5 players with many different multiplayer and co-op / vs. AI game modes. Plant the bomb, defuse the bomb, protect hostage while other team try to eliminate you, terrorist attack where you and your team clear map from AI enemies. As well as some PVE missions to hone your combat skills.
There's a healthy selection of characters both in defense team and attack team. Men and women from different countries with different skills and weapons, attachments and utility gear to use in missions. Some have higher armor, others are more agile, pick the one that is more suitable for the mission.
You can customize characters not only with different weapons and weapon attachments like scopes, laser sight, barrel attachments but also uniforms and helmets, different camo options, weapon accessory charms that dangle on the weapon while you move around.
Game has a lot of different, detailed maps with some destructible environments, a lot of ways to the objective. Be it rushing head on through the front door or grapple onto roof for a sneaky breach through window or ceiling window.
There are micro-transactions in the game but I haven't noticed any P2W elements in this. All the weapons are unlocked and you just change visual appearance of your character. Skins and shop items can either be bought with in game credits or money, but not all of them. For example loot packs you buy only with in game credits, and few uniforms and weapons are bough with real money only. You don't need any additional items, unless you like customizing your character.
I recommend buying standard edition if you want normal game experience, and only buy starter edition if you want to check the game out and not spend a lot, because there are few limitations that will make the credit grind for items a lot more tiresome.
Also for those who have R6 on uPlay, but want to have it on Steam as well. You can buy starter edition on Steam, thus when you install and run it, game will sync your info with uPlay game. Stuff you had unlocked will be available, but all attachments unequipped, and Situation progress reset. You will retain your level, credits and currency, items, unlocks, characters, etc.
Personally I play it only in Terrorist Hunt mode vs. AI as I'm terrible in PVP.
Game runs great with recent updates, 60 fps on very high. The HD textures might give you a few FPS spikes if you don't have 6GB VRAM. Always match settings to your hardware for best results. Have fun! ;)

Of Guards and Thieves:
TL;DR This game is one of the best time wasting action based "I want to play something fun and skip the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t and get right to the action" point+click shooter games I have in my library. It's a stealth/strategy/top-down shooter and it's loads of fun.
Of Guards and Thieves basic rules:
- When joining a server and when any game ends and returns to the server, immediately begin spamming "start" or "go" so the Admin knows they're permitted to begin the game. You are more important than them, after all.
- Always end every game with "gg" regardless of how you thought the game went.
- If you are a Guard, hide in bushes whenever you can, it doesn't irritate other players at all.
- If you are a Thief, hide behind doors with the Cobra class whenever you can, it doesn't irritate other players at all.
- Juggernaut and Guardian classes are your best friends, they aren't OP and are the most fairly balanced classes in game.

PROS:
- Small, mostly tight-knit community. There are multiple familiar names I see in-game that gives the game a sense of community. Always fun to play with people you enjoy playing with.
- Good strategy game with a "jump feet first into the action" mentality, if that's your playstyle.
- Can be played either casually or with intent to scar other players for life.
- No huge advantage to purchasing the full game. (YES, you have more classes/gamemodes but the game is entirely playable with the demo version, and the classes (aside from Juggernaut and Medic) really don't provide much of an advantage. ~70% of players don't have the full version.
- Enough variety in gamemodes to experience a wide range of fun.
CONS:
- Small, tight knit community. Sometimes there are barely enough players to get more than one or two good full servers running.
- Some gamemodes (Zombie Rush, Demolition especially) are near impossible without some basic teamwork. Having idiots on your team can ruin a game, but each game is 5min so not for long.
- Some gamemodes are kind of gimmicky and not very fun for all gamers. (Soccer/Faceless come to mind)
- Early Access, I never have had the game crash but occasionally if someone joins a server as the game is starting the server can crash. Not too often does this happen though.

:::First thing's first, the bad:::
This is a port of an IOS game, and you can tell.  It's jarring for the first five min or so.
The team making the IOS game stayed as true to the original art style as possible, and that's not going to be a good thing for some people.  The characters arms are all freakishly long, for example, and there's sections in the game where in the original there were some graphical design mistakes, and for whatever reason these mistakes are still here and since it's been cleaned up they are more noticeable
You'll notice some slowdown occasionally, which is odd considering how small a game this is.
:::Now, the good stuff:::
It's freaking FF6!!!! It's one of the best in the series.
Once you actually get used to the menu system it's more functional than the original game's menu system.
MUCH appreciated balance tweaks, the biggest I've noticed so far being Cyan's sword arts.  In every other release so far you were not able to issue commands to your party while his sword arts charged, and the baddies would swing on you, which made him by far and wide the absolute worst character in the game.  Now you can issue commands to your party while he charges his moves.
Bug fixes :D
Example: Evade and accuracy aren't bugged out. (In the original raising evade did nothing, lowering accuracy also did nothing)
Translation.  It stays true enough to the Woosley version that you won't be sad it's gone, but it just reads better.
Stays so true to the original art style, if you're a fan of the original you will likely literally not realize you're not looking at the original visuals.  While things look jarring at first, give it about ten min and you'll feel like you're playing the original.
Very amusing.

tl;dr This shortens load times and sometimes improves framerate on games with asset streaming. You'd better have the ram though, nothing short of 16GB will do you any favors with this.
If you've ever heard of a RAM Drive, you know what to expect from this; A super fast temporary storage solution with speeds that outclass even SSDs, cuts down on load times, and may even improve frame rate on games that use data streaming to load assets. It's not "Hurr durr paying to download more RAM." And you know that unless you use a virtual machine, 8 GB of that fancy 16GB of RAM you have won't be
put to use otherwise (At least until Ubisoft releases their next unoptimized PC port, HEYOOOO).
There are free solutions out there but I bought this just for the convenience of automating the process of creating and deleting symbolic links, which I
how to do, but would prefer not to every time I wanna load a game onto a ramdisk. Lazy people like me who know what I'm talking about will agree that it's worth $30 to do that if you're really serious about using a RAMDisk. And besides, the time you spend creating symbolic links would be the time you take up in exchange for shorter loading times, making the entire concept moot without this unless you copy an entire non steam game over to a ramdisk manually.
The few games I have tried this with so far have seen satisfactory boosts in loading times; One game I used with it, Warframe, seemed to also have the random framedrops I was getting (That also happen after alt tabbing) shortened or eliminated entirely. On top of this, the initial loading screen in the hotline miami games were shortened from 5 seconds to like half a second. You definitely want to use this program with free roaming games however, as those have the largest assets to load.
And here's where the actual problem comes into play, not with Dimmdrive itself but with the very idea of using a RAMdisk. Seeing as your operating system determines how much RAM you can use (Thanks, Microsoft; Except what I actually mean is ♥♥♥♥ you) storage space would be a problem, as with 16GB of ram, I.E.
, you hardly have enough space to store large assets while leaving room for non-partitioned RAM to do it's thing. Luckily, Dimmdrive circumvents this with a "Less Ram" option which lets you load specific files of a game through a RAMdrive, but to know what to move over you'd have to get
to see what assets are being loaded the most.
Anyway, this program does what it sets out to do and does it better than most Ramdisk programs, and for that I have to give it a recommendation if you really hate loading times or think you can improve the framerate of a game with it. Unfortunately as far as I know there's no list of "Games that use data streaming" so you know which ones would benefit (If I had to throw a random example at the wall though I'd say unreal engine 3 games as even as you load into the map you can probably see the textures still loading; This would theoretically eliminate that) but if you know what you're getting into when you buy this product and are really serious about it then go for it.

Quick Summary:  BeamNG.drive was a surprise find for me.  It's an ambitious game that replicates realism and simulation on levels that other well known sim racers can't currently compete with.  It isn't without faults, of course, and there are areas where the immersion is broken.  However, I think a lot of this will eventually be addressed before the game actually releases.  There's a lot of fun to be had here, driving/racing enthusiasts should definitely give it a try.
In-Depth:  The game is best described, in my opinion, as a sandbox driving game.  I hesitate to directly compare this to sim racing titles as BeamNG.drive feels more ambitious than that--it has racing, sure, but its scope is much larger.  Before I start going into the game further, my experience is based on playing the game using the following set up:
Thrustmaster TX Servo w/ 458 wheel
Thrustmaster T3PA Pro Pedals w/ conical brake mod
Thrustmaster TH8A Shifter
RSeat Chassis
Predator X34 monitor
The game detected my equipment fine, but did not automatically set everything up correctly by default.  With that said, I absolutely love how you can assign absolutely everything in the game to any button on your wheel or if you have a button box.  It also allows multiple mappings, so you can have keyboard commands simultaneously.  The overall UI is clean and easy to understand--it has a couple quirks, but overall very nice for such an early game.
I have a pretty strong PC, and the game runs relatively well.  I'd expect for it to be even better optimized as it moves closer to actual launch, but its current state runs quite well.  I did have to run it in fullscreen or the game would barely run.  So if you are used to setting yours up as bordless windowed or anything like that, you may have to fiddle with some things to get it working properly.
The game looks incredible.  Most racing sims really focus on the cars visuals, which makes sense, but track side visuals usually pale in comparison.  BeamNG.drive is much more even--the cars, interiors, and environments are all equally beautiful, which I'm a big fan of.  There are plenty of graphical settings, however, I mostly had everything turned all the way up to max playing at 3440x1440 and it was great.  I'm kind of blown away with how nice and even the game looks for being still early in development.
On to the actual gameplay.  The game here is a bit split for me--at times (most of them), it felt like the most realistic driving experience I've ever had, but there were some times where the feeling was a bit off.  The few off times did seem to occur on paved surfaces, but it could also be the fault of my forcefeedback not accurately relaying to me what was happening with the car.  This is an area I think could use some improvement, the forcefeedback is present, but feels underdeveloped compared to the rest of the experience. (Assetto Corsa is my benchmark for forcefeedback)
Now a bit more on why I would not directly compare this to sim racing games.  This game is so much more ambitious than that.  I would call this a driving simulator, not a racing sim.  There's a lot of variety here, and while it does have some racing, I was more impressed with its environments off-road.  I hope this doesn't sound like a knock on the game--I think it could be a great sim racing game if they focused on that, but this game is so much more.
To the above point, there is a scenario mode which highlights all of the variety.  These scenarios are incredibly different from one another and provide a taste of what sort of possibilities there are for this game.  I won't go into them all, as there are quite a lot, but here's a couple:
Car Delivery - Here you are driving a flatbed and have a sports car on the back.  You're tasked with delivering the sports car to its new owner.  You are timed and are required to deliver it without damaging it too much.
Police Chase - Someone has robbed a bank and is making a getaway, you're tasked with stopping them.
Van Jumps - There are some crazy jumps in this game, but the set you'll need to tackle with a van are some of the most difficult.
This game has plenty more to offer including rally style driving, offroading, etc. There is also a mode that just lets you load up in a map and create your own fun.  You can spawn in multiple cars and objects, which allows you to set up some incredibly fun stuff.
Now onto the game's main feature, it's soft body physics/damage.  This is by far in a way the most impressive thing I've seen in a video game in the past few years.  It's without equal to my knowledge, and adds a layer of not only realism, but also fun to this game.  It seems everything can be damaged, starting with the obvious body panels, all the way to individual axles, driveshafts, and engine internals.
In closing, this game is very ambitious, beautiful, realistic, and fun.  There's a large variety of environements and driving surfaces.  This is a sandbox driving game at the moment and is amazing at what it does.  If you enjoy the chaos, destruction, and stunts of something like Burnout, or the make your own fun of any sandbox titles, you should definitely give this game a try.

If you love cars and all the physic's that go with them, then this game is for you. If' you're looking for the next racing game however, keep looking. BeamNG is the most realistic physic's simulatior I've ever played, is it perfect? Absolutly not. But it's very very good, among the best of the few games it compares to. It is so easy to turn on some music, or listen to book on tape and get lost for hours on end just driving around in your sandbox, racing, crashing, towing, testing or just exploring. Perhaps most importantly the dev's actually care about this game...One of the drawbacks to buying / playing early access game's is that it is often a gamble. A lot time's the devs become tired with their product and halt devolpment all together, leaving you with a hole in your wallet and a half finished product that'll never be more than that. That however, is not the case here. I owned this game for almost a year now, and throughout that year I have witnessed consistent improvements, patch's and added content. I cannot praise this game enough, I don't have the time to invest thousands of hours playing games like some people do. But I beleive this is my second most played game on steam...Only surpassed by Skyrim, and for the record BeamNG is closing fast on my Skyrim hours. The game has a decent arsenal of vehicles, ranging from your run of the mill work truck (which can modified to suit your taste) to Race cars, to Semi tractor trailers. And the fact, that this game is Steam Workshop compatible mean's that even more vehicle's and track's are just a click away!
I'm trying to think of some potential ''con's'' to weigh in with all the ''pro's'' that go with this game. Personally I would like to see even more customization implimented into the game, such as the ability to tune gear ratio's in the transmission and fine tune things like aero dynamics. It would also be nice to be able to add specific upgrade's to your vehicle's engine. As it stand's right now, most vehicle's have Stage 1 Stage 2 and Stage 3 engine tune's and/or intake's that give you three stage's of horsepower/torque. But that's really just cherry picking on my behalf. Let's see what else, For those of you who enjoy playing with others...This is not your game. To my knowledge it currently does not have any form of multiplayer. No internet race's, I heard one time that it has split screen playability, but it's not something I've ever tried to use. I've heard some complaint's that this game only run's good on bad♥♥♥♥♥desktops, which is not completely true, however their's some truth in that statement. My current desktop was top the of line...Eight years ago, which my graphic's turned down a bit I can run most of BeamNG just fine. Howver, until I get a new computer I cannot play on certian level's...Like Moab, it's just to much for my old machine. On the side of sound, it's currently fairly weak. All vehicle's sound the same, a turbo I4 sounds excatly the same as a modified big block V8 in this game, so there isn't a huge veriety in that area, but hopefully that'll be improved upon in future patch's...Personally I just play with the sound off and listen to Reddit horror stories on Youtube while playing.
With that said, It's time to tally up the Pro's and Con's.
(Pros)
AMAZING Physics.
Reliable Devs who invest in their product to make consistent improvements
Potential to get lost for hours playing.
Immense depth in level's, lot's of exploration to be done.
Decent veriety of vehicle's ranging from Pickups to Race cars to Semi's.
Supports Steam Workshop, meaning downloadedable vehicle's and tracks are just a click away.
(Cons)
Taxing to run at high resolution.
Needs a little more depth in vehicle tuning.
Lame sound effects.
In it's current state I give this game a solid (9/10)
It was worth every penny I spent on it.

enjoy this chicken stir fry recpie
- Serves 4
- 10 mins to prepare and 10 mins to cook
- 325 calories / serving
- Healthy
INGREDIENTS:
- 1 orange, zested and juiced
- 2tbsp soy sauce
- 2tbsp sesame oil
- 250g (8oz) tender stem broccoli
- 5cm (2in) piece root ginger
- 1tbsp sunflower oil
- 1 garlic clove, finely sliced
- 1 red pepper, deseeded and thinly sliced
- 150g Straight To Wok Noodles
- 400g (13oz) chicken fillet, cut into thin slices
METHOD
Step 1 - Mix together the orange zest and juice, soy sauce and sesame oil and set aside.
Step 2 - Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain well and set aside.
Step 3 - Finely shred the ginger. Then heat a large frying pan or wok, add the sunflower oil, heat it until sizzling, and fry the ginger till it's crisp.
Step 4 - When it's done, remove with a slotted spoon. Add the chicken and garlic, and stir-fry until just browned. Remove the meat using a slotted spoon and set aside.
Step 5 - Add the red pepper and broccoli and stir-fry for around 2-3 minutes until it's just tender. Add the soy sauce mixture, bring it to the boil then return the chicken to the pan

Amnesia made us afraid of water.
SOMA put us under the sea.
Thanks Frictional.
-SPOILERS-
First things first, this was an amazing game. A round of applause for the crew at Frictional. They made this game worth waiting for and it was everything I hoped and so much more.
I approached this game as if it were Amnesia, I tried to play this as if it were Amnesia. We might be lacking a sanity meter and inventory but that does not take away from the game. Do not let yourself think this is AAMFP either. You can't play this game like Amnesia, the enemies are different, more intelligent, and do not despawn. There is so much to say about this game it's even hard for myself to put it into words.
Simon is a treasure. That's put simply. As much as it hurts me to admit it, Simon is now my newest favorite Frictional protag. He is the only being who can come off as an actual human compared to the rest of the cast. So out of place and confused, much like the player themself playing for the first time. Simon thinks about the things others do not want to. Where does he belong? He cannot go back to being that man who lived a simple life in Toronto a rough hundred years ago. By the time we reach our destination, Simon wants to feel that belonging, that heaven, the ARK. Somewhere he can rest easy and be who he is. Sadly only a copy of him can feel that.
I did not expect such a diverse cast of enemies, all of which have unique features and abilities that makes them all different. It's difficult to even choose which enemy was the best. All were placed in enviroments they could best showcase their talents. Now I expected no mercy from these enemies such as the ones from Penumbra and Amnesia who would attack until we safely hid/killed them/died. I was quite shocked upon blacking out the first time from the robot at Upsilon. This blacking out feature added a few method to the game when moving around the enemies.
Now as for downsides, I loved the game but I feel like we could have benefited more from interaction with the WAU and Simon's girlfriend. The WAU was everywhere we went but I wanted more interaction with it, that might just be because I was playing the game for the campaign and not the backstory. As for Simon's girlfriend, she was viewed in game twice and I thought the would play a bigger part in the campaign or have some lurking presence. However that does not take away from the atmosphere the game already gives off.
Frictonal redeemed themselves from AAMFP (even though they might not have developed it), SOMA revived their trademark scares with a whole new way. This game deserves so much more attention and less hesitation from gamers who played previous games. Frictional spent the last five years on this and it was very well worth the wait.
Thank you, Frictional. You guys made another memorable game which will stay with me for years to come much like Prenumbra and Amnesia have done before. You guys know not only how to scare me but to break my heart and make me think about life itself. Very much like Simon himself. This game will make you think much like how they want you to. Are you really alone in this world?

Oh my, what a trainwreck Duke Nukem Forever was.
All the developers had to do was very simple. They should have made an old school/90s FPS with intense battles, interesting weapons, and incentives to explore the levels, then add some Duke flavour to it. It should have been an instant success in an era of "modern" shooters in which you can just carry two guns and the levels are super linear. Legend has it that the original Duke 3D was already completed with very strong gameplay elements, and they decided to add further interactivity to the levels and the personality of Duke later on.
Sadly, the developers seemed to focus only on latter part of the Duke formula, and forgot to make an actual good game out of all this. What we got was a watered-down version of a once classic game with regenerating health, weightless combat and recycled ideas from other shooters of the time. The game is also padded with unnecessarily long turret and driving sections, which might vary up the gameplay, but this is really not what Duke is about.
Don't get me wrong, DNF has its moments and it even has some memorable puzzles and levels. Sometimes, when you're fighting the aliens and Duke says one of his signature one-liners after dealing with a pig cop, it brings back memories, you know? But this is not Duke, it is rather a weak CoD/Halo game with a Duke Nukem coating on top.
What a pity really. The most disappointing thing is that the trailer for the 2001 version (heck, even for the 1998 version) of the game showed so much potential compared to the final version we got in the end.
If you're a fan of Duke, I would just get DNF on a heavily discounted price.

Played five rounds and requested a refund. I have zero emotional attachment to the Friday the 13th franchise, so I can be impartial: The game design is terrible and here are a few reasons why:
If Jason singles you out, you're dead. You can't outrun or juke him. He can teleport. And if he grabs you once, you're dead.
Imagine playing a board game with friends, almost winning, and then Jason grabbing your game pieces, tossing them on the floor, and shouting "Haha, I win!". That's F13.
Compared to Dead by Daylight, it appears like there's so much more you can do here other than repairing generators. Escape by boat! Call the police! Drive a car! But technically you're still doing the same thing over and over: a simple fetch quest. Going into visually identical buildings, opening dozens of drawers, and hoping you'll find a needed item. It's as engaging as trying to find your misplaced car keys around your home while being late for work.
There's an animation input delay for most interactions. Closing a window and climbing through is done with the same button. Running around the map will give away your position, so you're encouraged to go as slowly as possible (boring). You can't creatively hide either.
Going back to Jason's teleportation, here's how annoying it is: You look backwards, Jason is running after you. He random disappears into thin air, no animation. You spin the camera forwards and now he's in front of you, choking you, and chopping your head off. Better luck next time.
What pushed me decide to refund? First round: Team killed within 20 seconds. Second and third round? Griefing. Fourth: Mic spam and Jason teleport death. The fifth round was sort-of kind-of almost fun, but only because I was allowed to live for more than five minutes and found a player that did not want to murder me. But then he got team killed. Then Jason got me.
If people are already griefing and team killing this much on day 1, to me that means the main gameplay is simply not engaging enough to hold people's attention and they are getting bored. Or the community sucks. Either way, I have not experienced this much toxic behavior on any release day ever.
All in all, I wouldn't recommend buying this game. Especially not for $40.

Review for mac users:
Offworld Trading Company (OTC) barely runs on my Macbook Pro Retina, despite my rigs' specs being well above the recommended. It runs so poorly that by the later tutorials (that's right, tutorials!), it turns into a slideshow, at low settings and 1440 resolution. We're talking isometric graphics here! The developers have ackowledged performance issues on Macs in the past, but the latest patch from June 2016 has not sorted that out, so I would strongly advise Mac owners to wait before purchasing this game until they see some clear indication these issues have been addressed.
On the plus side, the little I have seen from the tutorials I have played looks indeed very interesting, with traditional resource-grabbing mechanics being nicely updated by the new trading setting (no direct confrontation besides sabotage and a bit of piracy), a nice variety of factions, and serviceable graphics. Obviously, I would need to be able to play at much more length before being able to talk about long-term playability...

After the initial high of playing with a new game wore off, I found OTC to be a little dry. It's a well-made game with a wonderful soundtrack and all, but I fail to see what sets one 10-20 minute match apart from the next. Once you understand the basics of play, there is little left to discover. Certainly the game is difficult enough to keep you very busy for those 15 to 20 minutes, but I have not felt that coming back to this game was going to be a learning expereince or that winning a match was going to be an achievement. Compare this to, say, Dark Souls or Guns of Icarus where your success is based on mastery of mechanics and growing knowledge of a complex and intricate system. I don't see that in OTC--it's just "buy low, sell high" in essense, which isn't terribly interesting.
In a nutshell: It's fun, it's pretty, it sounds nice, and it's engaging to play, but there's not really a reason to play it besides an overabundance of free time. If you play games because you enjoy system mastery or continuously teasing out new knowledge of mechanics, give this a miss. If you're looking for an immersive experience, then definitely give it a try.

Is Kotor 2 a good game?
Many reviewers here have already answered that question (read: YES you bloody meatbags) so I will move onto the follow-up question:
Is it better than Kotor 1?
Yes.
If looked at from a broad perspective Kotor 2 is everything you would get from Kotor 1. Same RPG style. Same Combat system. Same adding more lore than needed. Same running around the bloody galaxy across a set number of planets in order to find a set number of plot devices. Since it's more of the same but more buggy (RCM disregarded) so you'd think that Kotor 1  would be the superior. However, what makes K2 in my eyes a much better game (and perhaps my favorite RPG) is two things:
1) The story
Don't get me wrong, Bioware has an excellent teams of writers and they've made some fantastic stories but the stories are always very simplistic. You are either the King of All Things Good or the World's Most Respected ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fighting against someone so evil (or more evil than you, if you choose to be the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥) it would take a loon to say [obviously evil guy] isn't.  In other words, Kotor follows the Original Star Wars (and nearly every Hero story out there) to the letter. You answer the call to a quest. You mature and grow in strength. You go and defeat the obvious baddie as one of the two archtypes above and save the galaxy. Boom. Roll Credits. Kotor is a hero story with all your Star Wars tropes.
Kotor 2 however takes said tropes and subverts them, throws them into fire, beats them to a pulp, and dumps them off into the nearest sun. What is a jedi without the force? Are the jedi really as good and deaaring as they are made out to be be? Or are they a bunch of jackasses? What is really difference between Jedi and Sith other than one likes red and the other a variety of colors? Or are both ideologies silly and just trying to stamp rules on a force (bum dum tsh) that they can barely understand? These questions and more are asked and played in Kotor 2 and they tie in with the overarching plot.
Even with the Binary Moral Choice system there is depth. It actually ties in with your character and companions other instead of being something to change the last 30 minutes of the game. You have incentive to what you do. You are a Jedi Exile returning to a galaxy that has (almost) entirely forgotten you. Are you angry at your former masters and wish to gather power to reap vengence upon every last one of them? Or have you accepted (what you consider) your wrongdoings and wish to redeem yourself and forget your past? This small context of backstory adds metric tons worth of depth to your character and growth.
TL;DR Kotor 2 manages to create a complex and fullfilling narrative that ties in both gameplay and story.
2) It has Heart
No really I'm serious. This is also a bit difficult to explain.
At first I though this "heart" was just nostalgia ,but I realized that Kotor 1 never had this "umph", and Kotor 1 was leagues ahead in nostalgia.
Kotor 2 is a game that really makes me care about the world, the characters, and the tale it is trying to tell. This is where Kotor 1 failed for me.
Your companions have depth and personality beyond there aligned stereotypes. I can give a couple paragraphs about each of them without needing to describe their appearence. The personal interactions you have with each member of your crew gives volumes more impact and detail and emotion.
The main quests of each planet made me feel like I was actually having impact on the galaxy. I felt change. After each planet I felt that something was going to happen and I was apart of it.
I think this "Heart" is Kotor 2 being a much more "local" story. You are not trying to uncover some grand mystery that decides the fate of the galaxy. That is just icing on the cake. Kotor 2 is a personal story of your character and a battle with their past demons. You learn more about the Exile as he/she learns more about him/herself. Everything is a lot more quiet and that is the brilliant part of it. A quiet personal story that deals with the remnants of events long past, all trying to push their ends on a galaxy that no longer cares for them. And you are one of them.
I picked Kotor (and this game up) out of nostalgia and to see how my views change on the games I played years ago and see how I view them now.
Had I been asked which game was better several years ago I would have said Kotor 1 without a second thought. But after some time and returning I have to switch that feeling. Kotor 2 is better. Much better. The RCM makes it fantastic. And I can't stress it enough.
As a small note I suggest you play this game with the Restored Content Mod, as it is more of a patch and less of a mod. and is the closest thing we'll (likely) get to a finished game that Obsidian wanted.

Otherwise the buildings effectiveness doesn't provide enough resources you need in enough quantities with some exceptions depending on what resources you are using the most. In the end considering that this game is not an early access game but a full release you can't count on these issues being fixed so I can't recommend that anyone buy this game.

Simply put, I really did not like this game. Many of my complaints are mirrored by other reviewers. The narrator's voice is not very well acted, very repetitious, very trite, and just...constant. He shows up with zingers about finding your heart, how anger is dangerous, how it's important to feel sadness, and at times I found myself blinking in disbelief that the lines made it through to the final draft.
The gameplay is mediocre. It isn't outright bad, but it's just not very fun. You spend most of your time trying out different powers, which will give you the ability to: slide yourself and objects over ground, toast things (including you if you're not careful) with raging fires, make the ground 'bouncy' so everything springs off of it, create electricity to turn on circuits (and thus make puzzles 'run' their active elements), and a few others I'm probably forgetting. That's the thing - the abilities are really just forgettable. Platforming staples like 'bouncy bouncy' need a little twist to make them interesting. Otherwise you are just back to Mario and spring-boards again.
Personally, I found the story tedious and unoriginal. You play as a sliver of the void, inexplicably cast onto the earth, and running from the 'void' - an understandably featureless foe who chases you across the map on occasion, and summons minions to try and slay you in a few different ways. The rule in this game is Insta-Death, which would be fun and exciting if the monsters were not so often acting in entirely novel ways, reacting unpredictably to tiny mistakes on your behalf (e.g. missing a small spot on the floor with the 'paint-on' effects), or just being RIGHT THERE as you enter a new frame. They also tend to have (IMO) awkward hit-boxes, such that you think you are okay springing over them, only to mysteriously die when you get too close.
I finished the main game in a little over two hours. It's a decently priced game, and I don't have much to complain about here. There is a 'void' mode unlocked after beating the main game, but I found the game suddenly veered from stupidly easy, to stupidly hard when I reached this mode - I never found the game reached that 'sweet spot' for me, between the two poles. I found myself, ridiculously, stuck on the very first 'room' of Void mode, perfectly able to solve the 'puzzle' (jumping over a charging enemy by building a little altitude), and occasionally succeeding (only to die on the next room) but almost entirely unable to execute it.
Trading Cards are a nice perk, and I sold them for an effective $1 reduction in price.
Achievements are what you would expect. About half are for clearing levels and winning the game, or objectives you can't avoid completing. The other are fairly obscure, and I believe there is a handful of hidden ones. Nothing too staggering here, but par for the course.
Overall, I disliked this game, and would probably rate it something like 4/10. It wasn't pull-out-your-hair bad, but on reflection, I think it was not worth the money. A couple hours wasted, no harm done, but nothing I can give a 'thumb up' to with a good conscience.

Rush Bros Review - Raymond KT
Rush Bros. just isn't fun. The platforming is bland and uninspired, the multiplayer feels more like simultaneous single player, and the rhythm-based elements are almost an afterthought. Though the idea of a platformer that runs on custom soundtracks is a grand one, the execution here is extremely disappointing. Rush Bros has some good ideas behind it, but the execution leaves a lot to be desired; for a game that claims to be a blend of two genres, there’s surprisingly little content from either. Overall, this game is a mess, not a terrible mess, but it is not a great nor good game. If you get the game for free or something like that, play it for a while, then get bored, and as you can probably see from my playtime (15 minutes or so) I got bored REALLY quickly
Rush Bros. attempts something similar by taking a platformer, focusing it on racing, and sprinkling in some rhythm-based game elements to help spice things up. Unfortunately for this dish, the spice is sparse and the resulting experience is far too bland to be engaging.The tragedy of Rush Bros. is that in theory, it could have been a great game. Rhythm-based platforming has been done well in the past, and as an idea could be something really special if executed well. The big problem with Rush Bros. is that it purports a focus on music, but only includes music in the design in a superficial manner.

Think Fallout 3 meets Doom....
I bought Nether with mixed expectations, as I've never really gotten into MMO style games. But the brilliance and sheer beauty of the looks of the game finally swayed my opinion towards buying. I have not been disappointed. The game is a fine lined mix between PvP and PvE, with just the right elements of survival, RPG, and exploration.
Survival - The game is a PvE (Player vs. Environment) in the way that players have to maintain hunger. I find myself always on the loot for food supplies, as the bar drops at a rather alarming rate. I have not been able to confirm, but I also believe that the harder you push yourself in-game, (running, fighting, jumping) and the lower your stamina bar sits, the faster the hunger gauge drops. But again, I have not been able to confirm this.
The game also entails staying alive, and believe me, its quite saddening when you do finally bite the dust. But we'll get more into that later. Enemies in the game can be devastating to your survival. All the enemies have a teleport ability and once they  "blink" out, you never know where they will appear next (altho most likely directly behind or beside the player). Jumping and dashing out of the way of these creatures attacks is a must when doing melee combat with them, and even when a player has a gun, ammo is usually needed to be conserved, and may draw other unwanted attentions. If confrontation is not desired, this is possible too thanks to a decent and playable stealth mechanic.
The creatures in the game seemed to be a little ridiculously OP'd when I started playing Nether, but this has mostly been solved, and it doesn't seem like the 'nether' have as much of an advantage anymore. Whether this is only my perspective, or something the devs have 'fixed' in the game, I don't know... But it is certain that players are once again the biggest threat in the game.
RPG - Nether brought a brilliant idea to the MMO/RPG table in my opinion. It has a fairly simple and intuitive perks tree, and it's not relatively hard to gain levels. XP is awarded for kills, selling items (altho the money system is a bit unbalanced in my opinion), and for even just staying alive for lengths of time. Players recieve a perk point at every level, and i found that by level 30 or so, there weren't really any perks that I was left 'wanting' on.
This level system is also well balanced I think, by the fact that all inventory is dropped on death, so that strong players dont keep strong equipment, and all XP levels are lost as well. I was a bit upset when starting on this game, since I would gain a few levels and then die, having to start all over. But now I see that it would just be impossible if all the super leveled players just remained super leveled. Losing levels provides a very well balanced feel to the game.
Just as players will aquire levels, the devs also set the game to level accounts as well. This helps to give a better balance also, since players who have had more experience playing the game, will recieve extra bonuses on starting a new character. Some of these include, extra backpack room, extra health, and extra starting cash.
Something else I would like to comment on before going to the next section is the Tribes. The devs put several Tribes into the game, which are basicly built-in Clans. So even when just starting the game, you have a team that will look out for, and protect your back. I have had a few neat experiences teaming up with other Tribe members, helping them out, and being helped in return. STALKERS 4 LYFE!
Exploration - This game is simply just BEAUTIFUL! The environment looks extremely lush and vibrant, and almost feels like a living thing itself. The graphics and sound are totally immersive, and never fails to make me feel as if I'm really there in the game. One of my favorite things I have actually seen in the game, was dropping prone and crawling through the high grass... simply beautifully done.
Looting is made rather simple in this game, by not completely over-stocking the environment. Even with a server full of players, it hasn't been overly difficult to find items to loot. Lootable containers are also 'hi-lited' in game, so they are usually pretty hard to miss. Gas stations, and other similar buildings that contain loot, also have neon lights outside that will flash, so they aren't hard to miss either from a block or so away. This saves a lot on building crawling.
Almost every building is enterable in the game, altho only a percentile of them contain any loot, and only a fraction of those have any real furnishings. This still adds nice environmental touch to the game, and it's always handy to make a short cut through a building to get to the street I'm looking for. But always be aware, you never know what will be waiting around the next corner...
In closing, if your a fan of Survival or Post Apocalyptic style games, I would def recommend this game. The game play is simple to pick up, and it's a unique RPG with completely immersive effects. It IS still in Early Access, and the game does still have some glitches and bugs that need to be worked out. But this has only twice made the game not worth playing for me, when containers would become non-lootable, and I believe the devs have since fixed this problem. Rush bros is a speedrunning focused platformer. It plays like a budget super meat boy but with environmental hazards that move in time to your music. There is a lot to not like about this game, but I'd recommend it if heavily discounted despite the many flaws.
The bad
-Inbuilt music is very limited and what is there is just boring, bring your own.
-If you use very fast paced custom music, environmental hazards can move too quickly, making certain levels almost impossible to beat. Environmental hazards can also be difficult to predict
-Playable characters differ only in appearance
-Extremely barebone aesthetics
-Controls take a moment to get used to, but are otherwise decent.
-Not a lot of content compared to other games in the genre
The good
-Environmental hazards generally respond to the pace of your music as advertised
-Good variety in the somewhat limited number of levels (eg mostly straight track vs key/switch based puzzles)
-No bugs encountered after 6 hours of gameplay
-Large selection of online levels
-Levels load quickly and checkpoints within levels are frequent
Overall, I greatly enjoyed the title and would recommend if you are into speed running platformers and you see it on sale for a heavy discount. Don't be too concerned about the ocean of negative reviews that is probably surrounding this one. This product has been given away for free a few times, resulting in many reviews which appear to be from people who do like speedrunning in general, have not taken enough time to get used to how the characters move, or were expecting nothing less than the level of quality you see in games like super meat boy.

I can't imagine there's a huge market for speedrunning games, yet I see more and more of them every year. I mean, you don't HAVE to make a game about speedrunning, you can just make something like Super Meat Boy that supports and encourages speedrunning while having plenty more to keep people hooked. Otherwise you end up with something like Rush Bros, which sacrifices story and atmosphere and exploration and pretty much everything I like about platformers in favor of making you run through bland levels again and again. And no, the D-lister techno soundtrack is not going to save it.
Seriously, there's no story here. You play as a little neon DJ shuffling though visual cacophonies of black platforms and WinAmp visualizer backgrounds that pulse to the music. There are traps like spikes and... sharp things that move to the beat as well, so you'll need to run and jump and walljump around them. Most levels have doors locked with colored keys so they're not a straight shot through, as well as temporary powerups like double jumps and speed boosts to help you zoom through tricky spots.
That's it. We're done here. There's no care or artistry put into the levels, they're just platforms and doors to work your way through. None of them give a sense of speed or daring that you would get from Dustforce or Super Meat Boy or even Sonic. Your DJs aren't even very fast, and can't pull off anything more complicated than a limp wall jump. There's just no reason to work at speedrunning these levels because there's no mastery to achieve here. You're not going to find clever shortcuts or reflex tests, it's just following the same boring path over and over.
There's something like forty levels, and some extra game modes on top of that, but who cares? Rush Bros is incredibly effective at exactly one thing, and that's sucking every drop of possible enjoyment from speedrunning. The levels are twisty, plodding crap and the music is embarrassingly amateur-hour. Literally anything else would be more fun to speedrun, going all the way back to the original NES and beyond. Don't bother with this for any reason. Just don't.

RAM is faster than an SSD or hard drive.
RAM loses all memory when it loses power.
RAM is like pie, Windows O/S eats some, and your game/program eats some.
RAMDISK software takes a piece of RAM pie for its own. It then allows us to use it as just another hard drive, a FAST hard drive.
Traditionally, RAMDISK software is complicated, requires a lot of manual tweaking, and is built with server applications in mind.

Quick Summary:  BeamNG.drive was a surprise find for me.  It's an ambitious game that replicates realism and simulation on levels that other well known sim racers can't currently compete with.  It isn't without faults, of course, and there are areas where the immersion is broken.  However, I think a lot of this will eventually be addressed before the game actually releases.  There's a lot of fun to be had here, driving/racing enthusiasts should definitely give it a try.
In-Depth:  The game is best described, in my opinion, as a sandbox driving game.  I hesitate to directly compare this to sim racing titles as BeamNG.drive feels more ambitious than that--it has racing, sure, but its scope is much larger.  Before I start going into the game further, my experience is based on playing the game using the following set up:
Thrustmaster TX Servo w/ 458 wheel
Thrustmaster T3PA Pro Pedals w/ conical brake mod
Thrustmaster TH8A Shifter
RSeat Chassis
Predator X34 monitor
The game detected my equipment fine, but did not automatically set everything up correctly by default.  With that said, I absolutely love how you can assign absolutely everything in the game to any button on your wheel or if you have a button box.  It also allows multiple mappings, so you can have keyboard commands simultaneously.  The overall UI is clean and easy to understand--it has a couple quirks, but overall very nice for such an early game.
I have a pretty strong PC, and the game runs relatively well.  I'd expect for it to be even better optimized as it moves closer to actual launch, but its current state runs quite well.  I did have to run it in fullscreen or the game would barely run.  So if you are used to setting yours up as bordless windowed or anything like that, you may have to fiddle with some things to get it working properly.
The game looks incredible.  Most racing sims really focus on the cars visuals, which makes sense, but track side visuals usually pale in comparison.  BeamNG.drive is much more even--the cars, interiors, and environments are all equally beautiful, which I'm a big fan of.  There are plenty of graphical settings, however, I mostly had everything turned all the way up to max playing at 3440x1440 and it was great.  I'm kind of blown away with how nice and even the game looks for being still early in development.
On to the actual gameplay.  The game here is a bit split for me--at times (most of them), it felt like the most realistic driving experience I've ever had, but there were some times where the feeling was a bit off.  The few off times did seem to occur on paved surfaces, but it could also be the fault of my forcefeedback not accurately relaying to me what was happening with the car.  This is an area I think could use some improvement, the forcefeedback is present, but feels underdeveloped compared to the rest of the experience. (Assetto Corsa is my benchmark for forcefeedback)
Now a bit more on why I would not directly compare this to sim racing games.  This game is so much more ambitious than that.  I would call this a driving simulator, not a racing sim.  There's a lot of variety here, and while it does have some racing, I was more impressed with its environments off-road.  I hope this doesn't sound like a knock on the game--I think it could be a great sim racing game if they focused on that, but this game is so much more.
To the above point, there is a scenario mode which highlights all of the variety.  These scenarios are incredibly different from one another and provide a taste of what sort of possibilities there are for this game.  I won't go into them all, as there are quite a lot, but here's a couple:
Car Delivery - Here you are driving a flatbed and have a sports car on the back.  You're tasked with delivering the sports car to its new owner.  You are timed and are required to deliver it without damaging it too much.
Police Chase - Someone has robbed a bank and is making a getaway, you're tasked with stopping them.
Van Jumps - There are some crazy jumps in this game, but the set you'll need to tackle with a van are some of the most difficult.
This game has plenty more to offer including rally style driving, offroading, etc. There is also a mode that just lets you load up in a map and create your own fun.  You can spawn in multiple cars and objects, which allows you to set up some incredibly fun stuff.
Now onto the game's main feature, it's soft body physics/damage.  This is by far in a way the most impressive thing I've seen in a video game in the past few years.  It's without equal to my knowledge, and adds a layer of not only realism, but also fun to this game.  It seems everything can be damaged, starting with the obvious body panels, all the way to individual axles, driveshafts, and engine internals.
In closing, this game is very ambitious, beautiful, realistic, and fun.  There's a large variety of environements and driving surfaces.  This is a sandbox driving game at the moment and is amazing at what it does.  If you enjoy the chaos, destruction, and stunts of something like Burnout, or the make your own fun of any sandbox titles, you should definitely give this game a try.

Although this software is on Steam and generally geared towards Steam, it can be used for far more.  Housing temporary large files as well as speeding up applications that are not even games.   Best of all is that Tim is constantly discussing the application with users and taking suggestions that we give him.
Of course it also works awesome for what it is advertised for, loading games much much faster, but where it really beats out a lot of the competition is that it backs up your files before you load them into the RAM disk, so if something happens you do not lose what you have!  A lot of the other software does it using img drives that manage to destroy your files should something go wrong (I have had to reinstall games and apps so many times due to that happening in other RAM software.)
The best feature by far though is the ability to selectively load parts of an application.  The image and texture resources that really kill your speed in games, while leaving the parts that do not really matter like the executables.  A big helper with games that are just too large for a RAM drive (like World of Warcraft)
In all, well worth every penny!

If you love cars and all the physic's that go with them, then this game is for you. If' you're looking for the next racing game however, keep looking. BeamNG is the most realistic physic's simulatior I've ever played, is it perfect? Absolutly not. But it's very very good, among the best of the few games it compares to. It is so easy to turn on some music, or listen to book on tape and get lost for hours on end just driving around in your sandbox, racing, crashing, towing, testing or just exploring. Perhaps most importantly the dev's actually care about this game...One of the drawbacks to buying / playing early access game's is that it is often a gamble. A lot time's the devs become tired with their product and halt devolpment all together, leaving you with a hole in your wallet and a half finished product that'll never be more than that. That however, is not the case here. I owned this game for almost a year now, and throughout that year I have witnessed consistent improvements, patch's and added content. I cannot praise this game enough, I don't have the time to invest thousands of hours playing games like some people do. But I beleive this is my second most played game on steam...Only surpassed by Skyrim, and for the record BeamNG is closing fast on my Skyrim hours. The game has a decent arsenal of vehicles, ranging from your run of the mill work truck (which can modified to suit your taste) to Race cars, to Semi tractor trailers. And the fact, that this game is Steam Workshop compatible mean's that even more vehicle's and track's are just a click away!
I'm trying to think of some potential ''con's'' to weigh in with all the ''pro's'' that go with this game. Personally I would like to see even more customization implimented into the game, such as the ability to tune gear ratio's in the transmission and fine tune things like aero dynamics. It would also be nice to be able to add specific upgrade's to your vehicle's engine. As it stand's right now, most vehicle's have Stage 1 Stage 2 and Stage 3 engine tune's and/or intake's that give you three stage's of horsepower/torque. But that's really just cherry picking on my behalf. Let's see what else, For those of you who enjoy playing with others...This is not your game. To my knowledge it currently does not have any form of multiplayer. No internet race's, I heard one time that it has split screen playability, but it's not something I've ever tried to use. I've heard some complaint's that this game only run's good on bad♥♥♥♥♥desktops, which is not completely true, however their's some truth in that statement. My current desktop was top the of line...Eight years ago, which my graphic's turned down a bit I can run most of BeamNG just fine. Howver, until I get a new computer I cannot play on certian level's...Like Moab, it's just to much for my old machine. On the side of sound, it's currently fairly weak. All vehicle's sound the same, a turbo I4 sounds excatly the same as a modified big block V8 in this game, so there isn't a huge veriety in that area, but hopefully that'll be improved upon in future patch's...Personally I just play with the sound off and listen to Reddit horror stories on Youtube while playing.
With that said, It's time to tally up the Pro's and Con's.
(Pros)
AMAZING Physics.
Reliable Devs who invest in their product to make consistent improvements
Potential to get lost for hours playing.
Immense depth in level's, lot's of exploration to be done.
Decent veriety of vehicle's ranging from Pickups to Race cars to Semi's.
Supports Steam Workshop, meaning downloadedable vehicle's and tracks are just a click away.
(Cons)
Taxing to run at high resolution.
Needs a little more depth in vehicle tuning.
Lame sound effects.
In it's current state I give this game a solid (9/10)
It was worth every penny I spent on it.

pros:
- symbolic links allow it to load in games/saves very quicky
- very short startup times compared to other ramdisk software (which has to load/save the entire drive image)
- Speed of the drive is detailed elsewhere, but it is fast, very fast (if configured right!)
cons:
- very large steam libraries can take quite a while to populate (which it does in alphabetical order...)
- if you do not exit properly it (ie turn off the dimm drive and let it stop completely) it loses the settings
- does not seem to automatically add save files (if the save files are not in the steam directory) so saves and loads can be slow unless you add them manually)
suggestions:
- allow dimmdrive (with steam integration) to start automatically AND pickup steam settings (instead of a non steam user login)
-setting to allow dimmdrive to automatically start in the 'on' setting so it can begin loading in your game(s)
- automatically grab the save directory (ex in windows the documents\My Games\) to speed save/load up
- dragging a dropping multiple folders, only one folder is listed (meaning you have to drag and drop each one individually
tldr, this is a great piece of software that i hope gets even better, if you have the ram to support a ramdisk then you should consider this over others like AMD ramdisk or softperfect (both of which i have tried)

Well Lo Wang nailed it in his sentence.
Like always you will have to hack and slash demons into pieces or simply shoot them down.
You do expect nothing more than a nice and cool game that´s kind of different from other games where you will hunt demons down within a nice story.
I really loved the first Shadow Warrior game. A cool story, nice graphics, funny jokes everywhere and a really cool and sometimes challenging gameplay.
But this follower was a dissapointment for me.
Shadow Warrior 2 is very focused on multiplayer. You can almost do everything with your friend. You can play the main and also the side storys together. That´s a cool thing if you think about that, you get the same experience and the same weapon drops BUT you won´t have the same story progress if you´re joining a game.
That means if you go on with the main story and at the end of a mission it could be that a weapon is unlocked in a shop in the village, you can´t buy them because you aren´t that far with the main story. So you will have to play the main story to that point until you can buy the weapon you wanted.
It´s really annoying to not have the same progress and also if you want to play the story with a friend you will have to play it twice. Also you can´t really help your friend with the endboss. It happens to me that I was locked out of the area. I couldn´t really help him.
But still it was fun to play. The grapics are really good, you will enjoy to make Screenshots.
Also the jokes are almost as funny as they were in the first game. Lo Wangs jokes and also the ones on the fortune cookies, are unique and great. I really love them but in the end they just repeat themself it were to many wich were dropped.
Additionally the weapon drops are random and not as much as the cookie drops. But if there was a weapon drop, it doesn´t really made a difference. The weapons doesn´t look the same but have similar stats. Despite that it makes fun to arm your weapons with special gems. There so many and you need time to get used to it. For example there are gems for the elementary damage for your weapon. That means you can create a fire Katana for instance. There are four Elements, fire, ice, electricity and poison. Also the enemys have a vulnerability on some of the elements. For instance a fire demon is vulnerable through ice, so you can use a ice weapon to make more damage to him. That´s really nice and i really liked to have weapons with all of the elements equipped.
And also the gameplay is really cool despite that they changed some of the abilitys you have in the first Shadow Warrior. It´s still like hack and slay every demon you can see on the map.
The maps are more open in this game not that straigt forward as I´ve known that from the first game. That would have been really nice and cool if they would´ve creating more maps. For the side quests, there are like 4 different maps to play. Sometimes there are addet one more when you go on with the main story. It´s kind of annoying to see the same map again and again.
And also the side quests get very boring from time to time. There are 2 or 3 with a real story and the others are mostly like kill 5 of these demons to get these items from them and bring them to me or kill 40 special demons wich are spread everywhere on the map.
If you like nonsense running around the map and killing just for fun any demons in the same map with mostly the same kind of demons on it then it´s your kind of side quests if not then i would suggest to not make every side quest, to make just some wich have good rewards like a new weapon. If you still want to make all then it could get very boring in the end.
Also what I will have to see critical about the game is that the main story compared to all of the side quests is really short, it´s too short. You could rush the main story in about probably 4-5 hours but the side quests make that into a play time from about 30+ play time.
Another point is that you have skill points and you can spend them like you want to. It can fit perfectly to your own play style. And also you have some items or more gems for your character to make him better. To make him fit to your play style.
To put it into a nutshell it coul´ve been a better game the story is to short but ok, the side quests are really boring in the end, you just want to finish them as fast as it works. Then the gameplay is cool. the graphics are good and the most weapons make no progress in killing ´cause they almost have the same stats.
Despite all the first few hours are really fun to play and I really loved them but it gets annoying and boring after a while ´cause it´s always the same. I know that I repeat myself there but i had to highlight it.
I really loved to play the first game, it was great but if I compare the second game with the first one the second is really a dissapointment. I really would´ve loved to give this game a neutral or a good review but there are too many things that are not good or even bad and I want to add that this is a review about my own experience in Shadow Warrior 2.

I have quite a good machine for gaming, previous machines were always lacking on the video card which made gaming stuttery , jerky and generally not a good experience. This time I splashed out and spent a lot of money on a top end machine.
Realising how fast ram is over other components (both HDDs & SSDs), I bought a ramdrive which I could utilise my 32GB of ram to boost things up a bit, however, when using steam games I had to manipulate the system every time I wished to play my steam downloads. It wasn't until afterwards I saw Dimmdrive, which although I thought was a bit expensive compared to the other ramdrive (which was half the price) but took care of all the preparation and setting up of the ramdrive to avoid any errors which may have occurred as I was running the games from another SSD on my system which was not in my steam library directory. I now have freed up an SSD and store all my games on a conventional HDD which has lots of free space which Dimmdrive loads the games from. I now believe Dimmdrive is worth every cent and is a credit to the author who, as I have noticed, is right on the ball with any problems users have pointed out to him. I didn't buy a ramdrive to speed up loading times but to stop the texture loading stutters and jerkiness which a slow HDD will unavoidably cause and as I previously said I freed up an SSD which I can utilise elsewhere.
An excellent piece of software, well done.
