ผมว่า App นี้เหมาะสำหรับคนที่มี RAM บนเครื่องมากกว่า 24GB เพราะถ้าน้อยกว่านี้อาจจะใช้งานได้ค่อนข้างลำบาก
ตอนนี้ผมใช้ Seagate ST3000DM001 เป็นไดร์วเก็บ Steam อยู่เพราะว่ามันเร็วพอที่จะเล่นเกมแล้วไม่ค่อยสะดุดช่วง Loading/Streaming texture หรือ resource ของเกมใหม่
และหากว่าผมจะต้องเปลี่ยนไดร์วเก็บเกม Steam แต่ละทีนั้น ผมจะต้องหาข้อมูลพอสมควร เพราะการหาไดร์วที่เร็วกว่าเดิมและมีความจุมากนั้นค่อนข้างยากและแต่ละรุ่นก็ค่อนข้างแพง แต่ในตอนนี้ไม่จำเป็นอีกต่อไปแล้ว ผมสามารถใช้ app นี้ในการ cache เกมได้เลย แล้วใช้ harddisk ใหญ่ ๆ ถูก ๆ อะไรก็ได้ในการเก็บไฟล์เกม Steam เช่นไดร์วที่ช้า ๆ อย่างพวกรุ่น Green ต่าง ๆ เป็นต้น
วิธีใช้ก็ง่ายมาก:
- เปิด app
- เลือกเกมที่ต้องการจะ cache
- กดปุ่มเพื่อเปิดใช้งาน DIMMDrive แล้วรอมัน cache เกมลง RAM สักพักนึง
- เปิดเกมจาก App นี้แล้วก็เล่นได้เลย
ข้อดี:
- เร็วมาก
- ใช้งานง่าย
- ใช้ RAM ที่มีให้เป็นประโยชน์ (ถ้าไว้เล่นเกมอย่างเดียว ไม่ได้เปิดงานอื่นพร้อมไปด้วย)
ข้อเสีย:
- ต้อง disable DIMMDrive ทุกครั้งก่อนที่จะเพิ่ม/ลบ/เปลี่ยน เกมที่ต้องการจะ cache ซึ่งเป็นอะไรที่ค่อนข้างน่ารำคาญ
- Steam จะคืดว่าเรานั้นเล่น app นี้อยู่ตลอดเวลา ไม่ใช่เกมที่เราเล่นอยู่จริง ๆ (เห็นว่าทางผู้พัฒนากำลังแก้ไขอยู่)
-----
I recommended this app, if you have 24GB or more RAM in your system.
I have ST3000DM001 as a Steam storage, which is quite fast HDD for dealing with stuttering when resource/texture streaming occurs and for a low loading time.
I had to think hard before I buy a new Steam harddrive because large and fast HDD is quite expensive ... but now I can use any big drive (even slow Green-class drives) as a Steam drive and use this app for caching an (almost) entire game that I want to play into my PC's RAM.
And it also very easy to use you just:
- Launch the app
- Select the game you want to cache.
- Enable DIMMDrive and wait for it to caching your game to the RAM.
- Launch your cached game(s) from the app and enjoy!
The pros:
- Blistering Fast
- Easy to use
- It's a way to your RAM (for gaming purpose) efficiently.
The cons are:
- I need to disable the Drive everytime (reinitialize drive, wipe all data) before I can add/remove/change any game I want to cache which is a quite frustrating for me.
- Steam thinks I'm playing this app not the actual game. (this is a known issue, the dev is working on it.)

A supremely well crafted game which is both exciting and cautious to play at the same time, The game offers two ways of playing: Stealth based gameplay as a thief and top-down shooter fare as a guard. Both sides have equal strengths and  weaknesses, the guards posess the best weaponry but need a flashlight to navigate darkened rooms whilst thieves only posses one assault heavy class but have night vision goggles allowing them unparalleled navigation across maps. Game modes are pretty basic, TDM, bomb defusal/placing, capture the flag(Or precious objects rather) and a zombie rush and soccer mode (Both of which are quite fun to play and fell less tacked on and more tasty side dish, Zombie rush is quite popular among players so be warned if tht's not your cup of tea) . The maps are well designed and make the most of the games lighting and tight controls, though the lack of music and any sense of danger reduces the atmosphere to nought, but the gameplay is very fun and competitive and the two novelty modes are fun in their own right. I can recommend this game because of the easy to learn controls and its' very interesting concept, what makes it even better is that the current already fairly meaty experience is only the tip of the iceberg so if you feel the game is not worth buying despite the many recommendations and our need for many new players just wait a few updates and then reconsider.

So if you have enough RAM and you want improvement of overall gaming expierience - buy it. But do not expect that such program will make FPS in games fly up to the sky on a bad machine.

Sniper Elite V2 is pretty much great as sniping goes. It has good (but arcade-y) ballistics, good wind and the "snipe cam" effect doesn't get old as fast as you'd think it'd do. It gives decent to great satisfaction when you nail a long range shot. The scoring system is somewhat superflous personally, aside from friend bragging rights. You do have to adjust your scope for longest (<100 meter) shots, which doesn't make any frigging sense, but it's there for gameplay purposes to make it a little harder and more satisfying nailing that long range shot.
Sound and graphics are both competent, but nothing beyond that. There's nothing that stands out as amazing, and on occasion you can run into some fairly ugly textures. Enemies also keep "spamming" voicelines when they are searching for you, or in combat. Even with just one or two enemies, expect to hear taunts and "Keep looking!" every 3 or 4 seconds.
Weapon sounds are extremely weak aside from the signature sniper rifles. MP40's and other automatic rifles sound more like peashooters than actual weapons, and their accuracy is abysmal in everything but close combat.
As far as gameplay goes is where this game completely falls flat as an exciting sniping game, and I'd say that if you are after that, get any of the Hitman games instead. This game has a fatal flaw that completely ruins the experience you have. It's way too scripted. Enemies will not be present unless you've passed a specific trigger, making it impossible to "clear the way" for future areas by finding a good spot and taking out all enemies. Especially the "Blow up the bridge" mission was EXTREME for this, as the last part has no less than FOUR such trigger points very tightly together, forcing you into close combat with recently spawned enemies, and then three snipers that all spawn as you walk into their line of sight. You have 0 chance of spotting them before hand and take them out from range, instead you have to duck and cover and play "peekaboo" with them.
The mission before that had one gauntlet event spawn right behind you, even though you had perfectly stealthily gone through the previous area. Suddenly it's flooded with enemies that instantly know where you are, and you have no way of avoiding said event. Instead you have to fight your way out with hordes of enemies, leaving you feeling less like a sniper and more like Rambo, which is not what I was looking for when I got a game named "Sniper Elite".
I couldn't bring myself to finish the game due to those very "gamey" moments that kept pulling me out of the experience, and it does leave the game feeling lacklustre. Part of the stealth mechanics are also quite odd as you can barely ever take out an emey stealthily with your sniper rifle due to the lack of suppression or the "Loud Noise"-mechanic introduced in a few levels.
Do I recommend this game? Not if you are looking for a pure sniping experience where you have to survey the area, have a plan of attack and use a lot of stealth. If you are after a mediocre run and gun experience with occasional sniping elements then sure, get it. But otherwise I wouldn't bother unless it was on a deep sale. In addition, you should stay the HELL away from the DLC. It's mindboggingly boring.

Mount and Blade: With Fire and Sword is an interesting.. Sequel/Standalone whatever it is to Mount and Blade and Mount and Blade: Warband.
While it proudly boasts the classic Mount and Blade style game play, allowing you free roam to do whatever you please in the world, be it conquer it, hunt bandits, or even just run caravans, there are a few things that make it exceptionally notable from the original game and it's sequel.
The first, and most likely the most noticably, is the guns. Unlike the original and Warband, which were set in a medieval-esque setting, fit with Crossbows, Bows and Throwing weapons as the only ranged weapons, With Fire and sword is placed in the 17th century Polish-Lithuanian commonwealth, and, as such, the game features guns. Most people see this in the game, and are offput by it (Much like many were to Age of Empires III) figuring it to be game-ruining or cheap. Taleworlds are smarter than that though, and the method to which they added guns is quite interesting. Mount and blade is renowned for it's complex systems for calculating damage accuracy and speed, and the way they introduced guns fits perfectly into this. You see, the guns, like any weapon real life or (good) fantasy, have both pros and cons.
Starting off with the pros, guns are incredibly powerful. A good shot to a person can very easily kill them instantly, and someone without a shield (something the game encourages by making them a bit pricey) can't block the shot. That on it's own would be ridiculously powerful, but it is weighed against the incredibly long reload times, limited shots and incredible inaccuracy. The weapons are treated by the game to be a sort of glass cannon: Incredibly powerful, but on it's own? Useless. Anyone with a mind wouldn't ride on their horse with a gun and without a sword. This makes for some incredibly interesting strategy and thought to be combined with the weapon, as is usual with the series.
The second difference is in troop management. The player can only recruit so many troops from villages at the beginning, this means that they cannot stack up troops as they would in the other two games. Instead soldiers in the earlier game are comprised almost if not entirely of mercenaries. If this were how it were in Warband, the game would be absolutely unplayable. In With fire and sword, however, there are some major changes. Firstly, the mercenaries you build your armies out of can be hired as much as you like from a mercenary camp, and more interestingly, at a mercenary camp you can actually choose what gear your troops have (Much like with companions, although a bit less customizable)
This allows you to tailor your army however you like it, albeit at a cost.  This feature is incredibly fun and interesting, although I believe it should have been optional to have the village recruitments for the most part turned off in the beginning, to allow more freedom.
A downside to With Fire and Sword though is the lack of mods. This is of course not the fault of the developers, and much more the fanbase. The game didn't hit as much success as Warband did with the community, despite how well the game compares to it, and so the mod base, compared to Warband, is empty. This is a catastrophic shame, although even without mods the game on its own still has much merit.
The game also isn't quite as memorable as the other games were. While the other games had their own original nations, With Fire and Sword draws more from actual history, and so contains real nations exclusively. This means that, while they are different culturally and strategically, they aren't as exuberant and different as the ones in the original games. The original two had everything from the desert dwelling Sarranids to the steppe venturing Khergits and snow wandering Vaegirs. While you could see the cultures they were drawn from, it was still interesting to see them all interacting with one another, and they were distinctly different. Not as many people know the difference between Russian troops and Polish ones as people do Viking and Arabian ones. These features aren't inherently bad, though. They can appeal greatly to a history buff with a passion for the 17th century. It is simply that these features aren't as appealing to a wide audience.
Don't let me dissaude you though, With Fire and Sword is a wonderful game, even if you aren't as into history as some other people are. It holds up extremely well to it's counterparts and in some ways surpasses it. And, if you enjoyed either of the first two games, I highly reccomend you give this one a try, even if you don't like the game in the end, you won't regret any time spent in it.

Absolutely fantastic. Easily one of the best, most thrilling gaming experiences I've ever had. It really makes you think about our humanity and morality. Has some genuinely tense and frightening scenes, and the atmostphere builds up incredibly well throughout the game.
Gameplay is very similar to Amnesia and Alien: Isolation. You don't have any weapons, and must use the environment to your advantage. The physics and puzzles really work well together.
The environments are similiar to Bioshock, so fans of deep-sea areas will be in for a treat! Anyone afraid of the deep sea and the murky abyss will be terrified!
Audio design and foley are some of the best I've heard; definitely up to a similar standard set by Alien: Isolation, which was also incredibly detailed, rich and terrifying.
SOMA also makes use of a brilliant physics engine, where every object in the world can be picked up, rotated, examined, thrown, etc. This includes pulling your mouse to slide open drawers and doors, etc, which really adds to the immersive exploration.
Set aside an evening, turn off all the lights, put on your headphones and lose yourself at the bottom of the ocean.

Shadow Warrior 2's combat and movement sets it apart from other looter-shooters like Borderlands and The Division. Even though you are wittling down health bars in the same bullet-spongey way, your targets react to the damage you're dealing, such as falling over / getting knocked back / staggering, losing limbs and sporting giant holes in their torso all while they're still alive (similar to Ninja Gaiden 2). Movement abilities aren't on cooldowns and you can use your powers far more often than in other games like this. As a result, combat is much faster than other looter-shooters, since guns have little recoil you can fire and move fast simultaneously, removing the requirement to stay behind cover and shoot a static target like Destiny or The Division. As a result, killing things is fun and not a tedious chore like similar games.
Boss battles follow the same kind of approach as the original Painkiller: great big boss in a great big open arena where you dash and double-jump to avoid damage adequately.
No inventory limit and you can equip eight guns at once. Every gun has a unique model so no copy-paste gun models with slightly different stats, either. Some are based on real-life weapons, others are futuristic and others are demonic abominations and all look the part. Being able to carry such an arsenal keeps combat fresh since you can swap out your weapons at any time without having to go back to town to access a chest or locker to sort through weaponry.
Only criticism I have of the game is that the load times are longer than comfortable.
Neverless, this is the most fun I've had in an FPS since 2016's DOOM.

I would have been disappointed if I wasn't just so glad to finally finish the damn thing so I can delete my files and transfer it to my "Uninstall Hell" tab in my library.
IN TERMS OF GAMEPLAY: At the beginning of the second level, I realized that this game not only had a narrator constantly jibber jabbering almost SOLELY to "fill a void" as it were [heeheeheehee*snort*], but that the gameplay was going to be extremely formulaic. Namely: 1) FIND FLOWER 2) TRY OUT POWER [three: we just gotta, like...become one with nature, mee-unn] REAL3)BACK TRACK SHORT DISTANCE 4) LEARN 2 OR 3 THINGS POWER CAN DO 5) RUN [AKA walk] FROM VOID. There are five (if you don't count the void) levels and they are almost exactly the same except for the new power added each level and...I guess volcano had rising lava and darkness in it. Now that I think about it, the whole game felt almost like a tutorial of itself. They held my hand so firmly that it's all sweaty and gross now. Eeeugh. The ONLY reason I didn't permanently scrap this game after the first five minutes of the second level was because I still had cards to drop and by the time I got to volcano I figured I might as well see if the ending was any good since I'd gotten this far (It wasn't. See above.)
I have not played the after story puzzles, which based on accidentally clicking the first one I imagine may actually be challenging, but...I'm done. I'm done with this game. I beat the story. I put in my two hours and am thoroughly dissatisfied enough to never play again.
I'm not a pro gamer by any means, but story mode was easy. Very easy. And given how shallow the plot is I think if I were to recommend a target audience for this game I would suggest...middle skoolers. Or anyone who just wants to play a spooky shadow guy in a video game more than anything else. To anyone potentially interested I STRONGLY recommend maybe watching a stream or something before buying this to see if the narrator irks you as much as he did me or if the repetitive gameplay still looks fun enough that you'd still want to rinse and repeat for two hours.

I have lot to say about how poor the game was, but i'll keep it short - the fundamental gameplay of this game is simply not well designed, nor fun. Enemies (of which there are probably 8? 2 of which you'll fight a majority of the time over and over again) are gigantic bullet sponges, who - especially on half difficulty - will dish out a stupid amount of damage. Couple this with gunplay that is incredibly lacking in any form of feedback and you have an FPS that from the get go simply isnt fun to play. Guns arent satisfying to shoot, the sounds lack depth and animations are basic and the enemies reactions to getting hit are something like Goldeneye 64 with some mild flinching. - Boring level design - which essentially drops off about halfway through and the game starts to feel extreme filled with 'filler content' as you do the same thing over and over and levels seem uncessary long.

I get it, Duke is a relic of times passed and people will constantly defend this games poor writing and awful humor as being 'delightfully cheesy' but the issue is that this type of humor done better in other games (heck Bulletstorm released the same damn year and was ticked the same 'macho-man' theme whilst also having superior gameplay..). I am really satisfied with this product. It works well along with RPG Maker, and it speeds up my game making capacities :)
1. This program allows you to assemble various parts of characters (picked from a library, that contains many character parts from RPG Maker XP, VX and MV) into a custom one. The program provides a layer system: each character part that is added to your character is added as a layer.
Layers can be recolored, repositioned, resized, hidden, drawn over with pen/eraser/bucket, etc... This allows to post-edit each character part quickly.
2. The program also comes with a random character generator. With that, you can generate any amount of characters in one click. The characters that are generated look surprisingly good for the most part. Note that you can also tune each character generator with some parameters (gender, race, armor, etc) so you can generate only what you need.
It's a good purchase! It's a perfect mix with an easy-to-use art program like
and MV character generator!
Way better then dead by deadlight, some things have to be fixed but overall an enjoyable experience so far :)

If you like horror movies, if you like asymmetrical games, then you will love this game. For fans of the Friday the 13th movies, this is a must buy. But be warned, you will die very often, cause Jason is a killing machine.
#Graphics are great, nothing special, but the atmosphere of the game is excelent. And the level design is awesome, you really feel like you are in one of the movies. The motion capure looks great, but the character animations are a bit of.
#The sounds and music are also very good, the tunes ripped straight out of the movies really keep you on the edge of your seat,  while scaning your surroundings looking for Jason.
# Controlls. I have only played with mouse and keyboard, and there is no way to change them, the default settings work just fine, I had no reason to change any of the keybindings, but they should add the option to change keybindings.
# Gameplay, As jason kill everyone, as a counceler try to escape, you have multiple ways to escape, fix a car or a boat, call the cops, or even kill Jason. The overall gameplay is pretty straight forward, but it works, and it's more fun then repeating the same objectives everytime (looking at you DBD)
# Matchmaking, is working fine for me at the moment, I can find games fast, and I had no disconnects at my end.
# Replayability. Endless if you like the theme, if you have some friends to play this game you can have a hell of a good time, there are plenty of unlocks, different versions of Jason, and different counselers and costumes.

Gameplay:  The concept is a blast and its implementation works very well.  A game is generally fast paced and discourages mission-focused individuals from camping.  Despite some lag issues on a number of servers, the game runs smoothly with people flowing in and out rooms, vents and windows.  The mouse responsiveness needs to be improved so when busting into a room as a guard, you can quickly pie slice the room with your flashlight.
Sound:  Something I assume will be worked on in the future (i.e. Early Access).  There is no music and what sound effects there are tend to be minimal.
Overall:  I'm having a lot of fun with this so far and I'm excited to see how it develops in the future.

I've always thought that one of the problems with modern games is that they are a bit too obvious in thier attempt to make you feel good by - in essence - letting you win which is why the demanding difficulty of Offworld Trading Company is so very enjoyable.
As I pass the twenty five hour mark on Offworld I'm also playing The Witcher 3 which allows me to perform some very heroic slashes that seem far beyond the mashing of left mouse I am doing.  It is very pretty but it seems to remove me from the mix.  The Witcher 3 is great but sometimes I feel like I'm a distraction to it, rather than the other way around.
Offworld Trading Company is the opposite.  Go disengaged in a minute of playing Offworld and you lose.  Make bad decision in Offworld and you lose.  Play well but not as well as someone else (including the impressive AI) and you lose.  Every defeat one can imagine a cause for an consider how to fix it.  The moment I realised that not mining a resource because it could be bought dirty cheap was a viable strategy was a revelation made better because it was not hinted at, or revealed in a tutorial, or given to me in any way other than through experience.
The result is a game where one feels an authorship over victory (or defeat) that creates a more compelling narrative than many a game that sell themselves on their narratives.  An irony of sorts there.

This game is a blast, the best way I could describe it is Monaco mixed with Counter Strike and it's just as amazing as that sounds. If there was ever an early access game that deserved it's asking price, it's this one.
One thing that should be appreciated is this isn't an early access game where you'll find lots of bugs or glitches. In the many hours that I've played on all the gamemodes I have not encountered a single one, which has been pretty impressive. You will not clip into geometry, fall through the world or any other weird occurances. Everything works just as intended. The occassional lag will happen but that will occur due to the host. (Roll your mouse over the admin of the room to see their location.)
It's graphics and graphical options are very limited and it could probably run on a toaster but thats actually a great thing because that means more players will be able to play flawlessly. Personally I feel that artistic style>graphical fidelity anyday and OGAT has oodles of style. Not to mention it scales perfectly. I assume the engine is Unity, it's very well optimized.
The gameplay is fluid, responsive (if the server is decent), and well balanced. Some are quick to shout OP, but that wouldn't happen if everyone took the time to understand how to effectively use light. Light is a big part of most of the gamemodes in OGAT, it will be your friend and it will be your enemy.
The devs should truely be rewarded for their support of OGAT and the dedication to the community adding SO much to the game it's ridiculous!
Just take a look here
and scroll down to see all the gamemodes they are planning to add to the game! It's like they want to recreate all of the best gmod mods, and I'm all for it!
One thing that a few of my friends have made notice was that the game has no music in it what-so-ever. It really didn't occur to me at all that it would be an issue, but for some people apparently it might be. So if soley the sound of guns and grenades don't satisfy you, that might be a bit of a problem.

Before you get your panties in a bunch screaming "YOU DON'T LIKE ARMA?!?!?!" or "HAHHAHA I'M GONNA FIND THIS REVIEW FUNNY THAT'LL SHOW HIM!" Please just hear me out and fully read my review, please put aside your personal love for the game and put aside your biased opinion of the game. I'm not sitting here ripping on the game saying it's complete sh*t, this game has soooo much potential.
-Note this review is off base/core game.
I've been here since Arma 1, I have a lot of memories on this game.
I have about 3000 Clocked hours on Arma 3, so yes I've seen it and played it all.
Although that is true many players will admit to the truth that this game really is just a buggy unrealistic mess.
So I'm going to list the pro's and con's for you to get a better perspective.
If you want to comment and add to the list, by all means, do so!
(CONS)
- The AI, are the least intelligent system in the game. They're mental.
- The Command system is semi-in-depth but lacks responsiveness, (It sucks)
- Player movement is clunky STILL, it feels glitchy and not realistic
- Vehicle movement is clunky STILL, it feels glitchy and not realistic
- Hit detection is terrible, you think you killed him but then he pops out like a bush wookie.
- Online PVP is terrible, it's laggy and glitchy not enjoyable.
- Inventory was enhanced but still feels unfinished, don't quite feel right, lacks many things.
- There's no real "Classification" of the game, no one really knows what the game is meant for.
- DLC's are just another ridiculous way to steal your money for an unfinished game.
- Anti-cheat is close to nonexistent, I've had plenty of experiences with cheaters
- Map design isn't very unique (Arma 2 was better)
- Weapon play is clunky and needs fixing
- The damage system is way off.
- Audio sometimes sounds cheap
- Graphics are OK, in a lot of the textures you can literally see the pixels!
- Performance is low-grade, a lot of work can be done.
- Server browser is ancient, the same browser from Arma 2 no major updates to it.
- Server performance is terrible, pings are usually through the roof ( I have FIBER connection)
- Banning legit players, it's happened to me twice luckily I've been unbanned, but still happens.
- No to little character customization
- Unfinished and overpriced (Especially the DLC's)
- Destruction system is something that exists but isn't very in-depth.
- Community relies on mods for fixing issues such as AI
- DLC's are released although most mods have already been created, it's just an "Official Mod"
(PROS)
- 25% of the cons fixed with mods (Community relies on Modders though!)
- VOIP systems are good, audio is great.
- Flight systems are great, flying a plane/heli feels finished and clean.
- Modding, if modding didn't exist this game would've died a long time ago.
- Weapon handling feels realistic, recoil, aiming etc...
- Game modes, DayZ/Epoch etc.. bring a lot to the table.
- Large player base, servers are usually full.
- Re-playability, you'll more than likely not get bored, especially with friends.
- The new launcher is great especially for sorting out mods.
- Installing mods is much easier now
- The mission editor is great, especially better than Arma 2's
- Mission making is much more in-depth from Arma 2
- The only worthy DLC IMO is APEX, others may differ.
- Mass amount of players in one server
- Can sometimes be immersive, especially playing with mates.
- Huge maps
- The user interface looks much cleaner and modern.
- Customizing weapons now (Really good on the devs part!)
(Videos)
(Issues)
My biggest issues with this game is AI & Performance
The AI in Arma 3 is coded in such a certain way that they run in linear paths/set coordinates.
This system is old, it was ported from Arma 2 with minor improvements.
For example, calling the command to form a line takes about 30 seconds to a minute.
The AI will walk in a line behind one another until each AI finds its Cords/Pos in relation to the leader.
The same goes for when climbing into vehicles, load up a mission, put down a squad and one helicopter. Give the command to "Get Into", and you'll notice they get into this line causing the whole system to take forever. Not to mention sometimes they forget where they're supposed to be, or that one r*tarded AI who refuses to get in.
The AI needs to be more dynamic, simply just needs to be more intelligent instead of relying on hard code that makes them so robotic, instead of human-like
As for performance
this game lack any type of optimization, and the sad part is, it's not that graphically intense.
This is one of the two biggest issues of the game if you Google "Arma 3" I can guarantee the index is filled with "How to get better FPS" or "Why is it so laggy?"
This has been a problem since Arma 1 and Arma 2, the devs have barely touched the subject.
I don't blame them as much, seeing as it's really the engines fault, they're using a terrible engine (RV4 Engine)
If you have a low-end machine DON'T BUY, it will be unbearable especially in multi-player.
For Reference I run 2x Asus GTX 970 Strix - i7 4790k @ 3.60GHZ 32GB DDR3 Ram
512 GB SSD
I usually run on Ultra and get 60FPS in singleplayer with a decent amount of AI
My FPS Will bounce from 30-60FPS in multilayer depending on a lot of factors.
You'd ask yourself "Well that's really good!" Yeah, it is, if you want to spend a♥♥♥♥♥♥load of money just to play this game.
Back in the day I use to run an R9 280x with some AMD CPU I don't remember, on average I got 20 - 45FPS never capped 60FPS.
Be warned - This game is CPU intensive, you can have a GTX 1080 and it will still run like♥♥♥♥♥♥
(Score)
Overall I give the score of 6/10. This game has so much potential already seeing as it's the only game offering this type of playing field. If the devs would just fix half of this♥♥♥♥♥♥especially performance and AI I would totally recommend this to anyone!

Let me first point out, don't let my hours fool you. I discovered this game through a friend from school almost a year ago, and fell absolutely in love with it. We would play at school all the time, spending hours upon hours (time I should've spent towards work, but eh) playing this game whether at school, or in skype calls at home.
I don't commit to games well. Jade Dynasty, the Sly Cooper series, Runescape, and Of Guards and Thieves are some of the biggest titles of my life. Though I've owned 100s of games in my 17 years, there are no games I've invested more time into than these four. Of Guards and Thieves is a very simple concept. WASD to move, mouse to shoot, guards vs thieves (or guards vs zombies). But the strong community of great people, a connection to all of my friends, and the countless hours of fun have turned this simple game into a game I treasure. The staff at SubvertGames are amazing and always willing to help. I've talked to and played with a few in-game, which is a pretty cool experience. How many games have you played where you're playing with the developers? They're interesting people, they come up with great ideas, they listen to the community, and they're all around great.
A great thing about the development team is their ability to make a great game. I'll warn you now, this is no hack and slash, run around and kill everything type of game. This game requires strategy and skill. A thief that expects to rugby tackle and shank guards into the ground will get nowhere, and a guard that wanders aimlessly near corners and dark places almost deserves to be stabbed to death. If you treat this game like a 2D top-down shooter, you'll get nowhere. I put more thought and effort into my playing than I do playing Stratego.
For an early access game, this game is pretty glitch-free. There are a few bugs here and there, but there's not a lot I've ever run into in the past year I've spent with this game.
The game is constantly expanding. When I joined, there were 2 classes for each team, and one gamemode. It was a wonderful game, but my friends and I kept brainstorming new ideas as we got bored. Now the developers are talking about custom loadouts and a map editor? Can I get a hellyeah.
I love this game, and I would love to see your beautiful face in the community. This is a wonderful game, with wonderful developers, and it deserves your $15. If you have any questions, please feel free to PM me or find me in-game. I will do anything to sway people to join this growing community.

Mount and Blade: With Fire and Sword is an interesting.. Sequel/Standalone whatever it is to Mount and Blade and Mount and Blade: Warband.
While it proudly boasts the classic Mount and Blade style game play, allowing you free roam to do whatever you please in the world, be it conquer it, hunt bandits, or even just run caravans, there are a few things that make it exceptionally notable from the original game and it's sequel.
The first, and most likely the most noticably, is the guns. Unlike the original and Warband, which were set in a medieval-esque setting, fit with Crossbows, Bows and Throwing weapons as the only ranged weapons, With Fire and sword is placed in the 17th century Polish-Lithuanian commonwealth, and, as such, the game features guns. Most people see this in the game, and are offput by it (Much like many were to Age of Empires III) figuring it to be game-ruining or cheap. Taleworlds are smarter than that though, and the method to which they added guns is quite interesting. Mount and blade is renowned for it's complex systems for calculating damage accuracy and speed, and the way they introduced guns fits perfectly into this. You see, the guns, like any weapon real life or (good) fantasy, have both pros and cons.
Starting off with the pros, guns are incredibly powerful. A good shot to a person can very easily kill them instantly, and someone without a shield (something the game encourages by making them a bit pricey) can't block the shot. That on it's own would be ridiculously powerful, but it is weighed against the incredibly long reload times, limited shots and incredible inaccuracy. The weapons are treated by the game to be a sort of glass cannon: Incredibly powerful, but on it's own? Useless. Anyone with a mind wouldn't ride on their horse with a gun and without a sword. This makes for some incredibly interesting strategy and thought to be combined with the weapon, as is usual with the series.
The second difference is in troop management. The player can only recruit so many troops from villages at the beginning, this means that they cannot stack up troops as they would in the other two games. Instead soldiers in the earlier game are comprised almost if not entirely of mercenaries. If this were how it were in Warband, the game would be absolutely unplayable. In With fire and sword, however, there are some major changes. Firstly, the mercenaries you build your armies out of can be hired as much as you like from a mercenary camp, and more interestingly, at a mercenary camp you can actually choose what gear your troops have (Much like with companions, although a bit less customizable)
This allows you to tailor your army however you like it, albeit at a cost.  This feature is incredibly fun and interesting, although I believe it should have been optional to have the village recruitments for the most part turned off in the beginning, to allow more freedom.
A downside to With Fire and Sword though is the lack of mods. This is of course not the fault of the developers, and much more the fanbase. The game didn't hit as much success as Warband did with the community, despite how well the game compares to it, and so the mod base, compared to Warband, is empty. This is a catastrophic shame, although even without mods the game on its own still has much merit.
The game also isn't quite as memorable as the other games were. While the other games had their own original nations, With Fire and Sword draws more from actual history, and so contains real nations exclusively. This means that, while they are different culturally and strategically, they aren't as exuberant and different as the ones in the original games. The original two had everything from the desert dwelling Sarranids to the steppe venturing Khergits and snow wandering Vaegirs. While you could see the cultures they were drawn from, it was still interesting to see them all interacting with one another, and they were distinctly different. Not as many people know the difference between Russian troops and Polish ones as people do Viking and Arabian ones. These features aren't inherently bad, though. They can appeal greatly to a history buff with a passion for the 17th century. It is simply that these features aren't as appealing to a wide audience.
Don't let me dissaude you though, With Fire and Sword is a wonderful game, even if you aren't as into history as some other people are. It holds up extremely well to it's counterparts and in some ways surpasses it. And, if you enjoyed either of the first two games, I highly reccomend you give this one a try, even if you don't like the game in the end, you won't regret any time spent in it.

I've been using DImmdrive for almost a year now so I think I'm pretty educated on its functions and its uses.
It's VERY good. Plain and simple.
The way that the program works is that it takes your RAM and turns it into a virtual drive. Since RAM has high speeds whatever games you choose to put in this virtual drive gets a speed boost in terms of load times and such.
While this probably isn't the cheapest way to get top speeds for program loading and gaming load times it is extremely effective and the difference between an SSD and this is night and day. Some people will say that the amount of time is negligable but in reality if you continually replace and remove a program from an SSD you will be diminsihing the health of it. Dimmdrive doesn't have this problem. So you're getting speeds that are both a little faster (anywhere between half a second to a full 2 seconds in my experience) and you're also protecting your SSD. For us gamers this is a godsend in my eyes.
To use this program properly you'll need at least 24gb of RAM. Your ram speed doesn't really matter but heatsinks/good airflow is my personal suggestion, despite me not seeing any high temperatures, it's just a precaution.
If you happen to fall upon extra RAM from friends or family this DOES become a cheaper solution than SSD but you'd have to be lucky in that respect. I bought my ram from people selling on /r/hardwareswap and am now sitting on a nice 24gb of RAM. I spent maybe 65 bucks total. I got lucky.
Also if you are worried about huge games that are 50gb+ you need not worry! You can specify which parts of the game get loaded into Dimmdrive. This way you can save on space AND specifially choose what takes priority. For example lets say Crysis 3 contstantly accesses 4 files constantly which would be Textures, models, terrain, levels. You can choose what parts of those folders get loaded. In order to figure what gets used how often you need a program called Process Monitor (Procmon). You can also head to
where some people have already used Procmon to determine what games use what files the most (this saves you the time of doing all the work)
Lastly people are complaining about how long it takes to initially load the game into the dimmdrive itself. This can take up to 6 minutes for a 22gb game (I tested it) HOWEVER if you have a USB 3.0 around you can use it to fast track this initial load. If you don't use Turbo USB 3.0 (thats the name of the feature) you'll continuoulsy have to wait that 6 minutes for a 22 gb game, with the Turbo USB you wait 6 minutes the first time, after that you only wait for 1 minute (also tested). DO NOT USE AN EXTERNAL HARD DRIVE THAT IS USB 3.0 DIMMDRIVE DOESN'T RECOGNIZE IT AS  A USB!!! Just warning ya ;)
All in all I LOVE the program, and even after I get an SSD I'll still be using dimmdrive for games that I will be constantly uninstalling (You know since not everyone can try every game from their library)

It's a ramdisk. It does ramdisk things. Really, if you're familiar with the concept there's not too much to say.
GUI wise it's ok. Certainly a lot more convenient than most other solutions out there and I like the automatic discovery of software installed via stea, though there are some annoyances that I hope get ironed out. eg: The sorting mode selected does not stick whenever you enable dimmdrive for a particular game or application, forcing you to click again on your preferred sorting mode or have to scroll all the way to the top of the list to change the settings for that application further. Also, there does not appear to be a way to disable dimmdrive for an application without first stopping the entire service, which is very problematic if you're looking to keep certain applications on dimmdrive, but swap others out on an as needed basis, such as running a server and then playing various games on the side. The current implementation forces you to stop the server (booting any logged on users), change settings as needed for the other applications you really wanted to change and then start it back up again. Hopefully this is something that gets fixed soon.
There's also the issue of how Steam tracks your activity and therefore shows you "in-game" playing Dimmdrive at all times. Granted, this is a problem with Steam's behavior with regards to applications that launch through it due to its drm system and therefore occurs with all software you buy on steam, but it is nevertheless an issue that would be nice to have resolved/worked around somehow.
Overall, however, it works as advertised, but with the caveat that I think the listed system requirements should be changed. While technically you can run this on a system with 4GB ram is will be almost entirely useless for most users due to how small you would need to make the disks. Personally I would never recommend this for someone unless they have a minimum of 16GB system memory and only if they already have an SSD and would like to eke out slightly more speed. Ideally I'd say to only consider a ramdrive if you have a high end system with 32GB ram (or more), already have an SSD and you are aware of the diminishing returns from further speed increases as well as a good idea of which applications or games specifically that are being bottlenecked by your current disk I/O.
Does dimmdrive work? Yes it does. Do you need it? Most likely not. This, like all other ramdrives before it, is a very specialized tool for a very specific subset of users who already know they have a need or desire for something like it. The vast majority do not need this. If you do, however, then I'll say dimmdrive is a valid choice.

SOMA is an intense first-person sci-fi horror game by developer Frictional Games. To start off,
is a non-linear, Total War style rts with map based strategy and overhead control of soldiers. It is most similar to
, taking place in the same time period, 1700-1800. Being released in 2005 for pc and 2006 for mac, you would come to expect this game to be unapealing, especially with larger franchises that are so similar, but that is not the case. Here I am going to explain why.
Imperial Glory brings to the table many things that I have yet to see in a game of this style before such as population based recruiting, and missions that can give you many bonuses such as buildings being built instantly or elite units. The graphics and audio may not be the greatest, even for the time it came out, but we all have to remember that graphics and audio don't make a game.
The gameplay is where this game really shines in my eyes. Though once again similar to Empire: Total War in this aspect, it is very unique, in some ways even better than Total War. The map phase of the game, which is only in Europe, has far fewer provinces than Total War, this allows each game to be much faster and more action oriented while adding a less strategic depth making the game easier to grasp. All units are relatively small making the combat more strategy focused, though still not too difficult.
In the end this is just a cheap version of total war, but note,
. It's a good game to buy for a few hours of fun and is well worth $5 or less, but best to buy it on sale for best value.

Nihilumbra is, at its core, a puzzle game. You control the strange black shape (shown on majority of screenshots), and you can use 5 different colors to give surfaces certain properties (like "slippery", "sticky", "bouncy" etc.). These surfaces then affect you, enemies AND objects alike.
The good thing about Nihilumbra is that you always know where to go (always to the right), so if you see two paths to the rigth (upper and lower) and one of them turns out to be blocked, there's not any real backtracking or getting lost. The game progresses very nicely.
The puzzle challenges are quite good, sometimes there is some head-scratching involved until you figure out the solution. Each of the 5 worlds ends with a somewhat nerve-wrecking "boss level", where there is a time limit in the form of a big wall of destruction that is always progressing from left to right, so you will need to be able to perform the solution at reasonable speed. But the system of checkpoints is very well thought through and there is virtually no frustration - just tons of fun.
Took me 2 hours to finish, and I liked every minute of it.

Welcome to Offworld Trading Company, an economic strategy game developed by Mohawk Games. Your goal in OTC is simple, make more money than your competition and, eventually, buy them out completely. You’ll need to manage all of your resources, expand your company’s HQ and maybe there’ll be some corporate sabotage thrown in to the mix.
The core gameplay all revolves around harvesting resources and then using those resources to produce other resources (for example Silicon is used by the buildings that produce glass) and sell off anything you don’t need to boost your cash-flow. It sounds easy but you only have a certain number of tile claims. If you have five claims available that means you can only build five buildings. However, you can get more claims, mainly by upgrading your company’s HQ (up to the maximum level 5) but there are in-game auctions and you’ll sometimes be able to bid on extra claims or an actual tile as well as other things such as patents (technologies that provide a positive bonus to your business) and black market items (some of which are used for personal gain, others which are used to sabotage the competition).
As with all strategy games, OTC’s gameplay is split into early-game, mid-game and late-game. The early-game in OTC is all about securing the resources that are essential to your faction (one of four), without these you’ll find yourself in a lot of debt very quickly and you’ll be unable to expand your HQ. For example, Seneca Development is a human faction so they need food, water and oxygen to run their base but Yoshimi Robotics is run by robots so they don’t require these (though you may still want them in order to sell them). It’s also important to secure at least two of the three resources you need for upgrading your HQ in the early game so that you don’t have to spend too much money buying other resources. OTC’s mid-game is essentially about preparing for late-game. By the mid-game you should have secured all the resources you need to run and upgrade your HQ so now you’ll be thinking about increasing your HQ level and starting to look at producing resources which you’ll be able to make huge profits from in the late-game stage. If you have any resources to sell off, mid-game may also be when you start purchasing stocks in other players to prepare for buying them out. The late-game stage is when you’re going to be making most of your money. Prices will be at their highest now as the human colony you’re supporting will be very large now so this is the time to sell off resources you have large stockpiles of (in small amounts so you don’t push the price down too much) but it’s also when you want to be thinking about building two or three Offworld Markets. The Offworld Market building is a rocket which will launch 100 of whatever resource you choose to asteroid mines for insane amounts of money, several times more than simply selling your resources to the colony. Once you’ve sent up a couple of rockets you’ll have enough money to buy out the weakest competitor(s) and soon you’ll have enough to buy out even the strongest of the competition, as long as they’re still behind you.
The main way to limit your competition is by sabotaging them with black market items as I mentioned earlier. Some of the items which are for your benefit include bribing officials to give you an extra claim or using a M.U.L.E to collect 200 units of a resource. The sabotage items range from EMPs which will temporarily disable a few buildings to Mutiny which will give you any profits from a building for around a minute (particularly effective when used on Offworld Markets). Some of these items did feel unbalanced to me, for example an underground nuke reduces the number of resources you harvest from a tile, if an enemy uses this several times it can be incredibly damaging as you’ll then have to focus on getting more of that resource rather than making money. It also seems that AI are more likely to target human players than other AI players which is of course problematic if you’re playing single-player. While some of the individual items feel unbalanced, the black markets presence in the game is handled very well. Once you’ve purchased an item from the market you’ll have to wait one minute before you can purchase anything else and every time a player (human or AI) purchases an item its price increases for everyone so you can’t just spam a load of EMPs. Furthermore, there’s a pool of items and you only get a random selection of them for each game (the number of items also depends on the size of the map/number of players) which adds a little bit of variety to the game.
Although I’ve really enjoyed playing OTC (especially multiplayer skirmishes with friends) it does have two major issues: a lack of depth and a high price for what’s on offer. The former feeds into the latter so I’ll talk about it first. The problem I have is there’s not really any variation in gameplay or strategies. I’ve played quite a few matches in my ten hours with the game so far (they usually last between twenty to thirty minutes) and I’ve used the same strategy every time, winning all but two or three matches. Even when I played as a different faction I only had to make small tweaks to my strategy in order to win the game. Sure, if you play on the higher difficulties it’s more of a challenge but I still didn’t feel as though I needed to do anything differently to what I did in my previous games. Obviously I don’t expect it to be so varied that it feels like I’m playing a different game every time I play but I shouldn’t feel like I’m playing the same match when I play. It’s this lack of depth that makes the £30 asking price way too high, I feel that a price point of around £20 would be much better value.
A couple more things to tie up. OTC is a really good looking game, the style of the game fits it perfectly and, though it’s only a small feature, I enjoyed watching the little transport ships fly from my resource collection buildings back to the HQ. While Skirmish is probably playing most of the time, there is also a campaign mode. It’s well designed and offers slightly different gameplay to Skirmish mode, giving you seven days on a map to be the player who buys the most modules for the nearby colony. Personally I didn’t enjoy it anywhere near as much as skirmish/multiplayer but that’s not to say it’s bad. The tutorials are very good and explain everything very well though it is possible to screw up in the tutorials (for example if you build an extra building you won’t have enough claims to complete the tutorial) which means that you may have to restart the entire tutorial mission, a bit frustrating considering it’s not explained. Lastly, the game’s soundtrack is absolutely fantastic!
An enjoyable economic strategy game that’s good for a few hours of fun despite being overpriced and lacking depth. If you’re a fan of strategy games and you’re looking for something different I’d highly recommend picking it up on sale.

After quite a lot of issues regarding Windows Update, and a slight leap of faith, I have reviewed my previous review.
I think this is a great game. There are parts of it you should be aware of however. With the exception of what I'm about to describe, it's a very well designed, well executed, and well planned game.
口 It requires Windows 7 Service Pack 1 or higher.
口 Some of the destruction (soft-body physics) seems very strange; some crashes will cause stretchyness that seems impossible. It used to be much worse, but it can still be noticed rarely.
口 Things don't seem to collide very well; small objects or large, simple objects can pierce or swallow things. Some times, parts of a car can clip through other solid parts of the car, and so on.
口 There is not very much in the game yet. Simply enough, the game is a work in progress, and contains only a little bit of gameplay; scenarios (including timed races) and freeroam. The freeroam aspect is the best part of the game I think, but there it seems like you're the last person on Earth and happen to be a car detailer. There are no other cars lying around (because performance) or people (because that would be a massive feature to add). Just a map and a car. This has appeal to some, including myself, but might put some off.
口 There is not any real way to tell how fast you're travelling. Obviously in real life, there's a lot happening when you drive a car. You feel the road, you change gears and so on. Unfortunately the technology to make driving slow interesting just doesn't exist yet, so judging distance and speed, along with just enjoying driving around randomly, is something you only feel like doing occasionally. This game is a bit like Project Reality in that regard; getting into the mood for it is hard.
口 Because of limitations in the game engine, maps can only be so large, so they get old quite fast. If there were a map similar in size to Vice City's, the rate at which you would lose interest would be substantially less than with a 4km square.
口 None of the maps have urban or city areas. Some of the most interesting places to drive are in cities, and while the countryside is absolutely beautifully designed, it would be nice to drive around a city once in a while. Just a nit-pick.
口 It is extremely resource intensive and will likely be in development for years to come before several cars can be spawned without enabling slow motion.
口 The cars are unnaturally shiny. Not even factory-floor cars are that shiny.
Apart from that, it's a fantastic game, the art, level design, game mechanics are all great.

Before you get your panties in a bunch screaming "YOU DON'T LIKE ARMA?!?!?!" or "HAHHAHA I'M GONNA FIND THIS REVIEW FUNNY THAT'LL SHOW HIM!" Please just hear me out and fully read my review, please put aside your personal love for the game and put aside your biased opinion of the game. I'm not sitting here ripping on the game saying it's complete sh*t, this game has soooo much potential.
-Note this review is off base/core game.
I've been here since Arma 1, I have a lot of memories on this game.
I have about 3000 Clocked hours on Arma 3, so yes I've seen it and played it all.
Although that is true many players will admit to the truth that this game really is just a buggy unrealistic mess.
So I'm going to list the pro's and con's for you to get a better perspective.
If you want to comment and add to the list, by all means, do so!
(CONS)
- The AI, are the least intelligent system in the game. They're mental.
- The Command system is semi-in-depth but lacks responsiveness, (It sucks)
- Player movement is clunky STILL, it feels glitchy and not realistic
- Vehicle movement is clunky STILL, it feels glitchy and not realistic
- Hit detection is terrible, you think you killed him but then he pops out like a bush wookie.
- Online PVP is terrible, it's laggy and glitchy not enjoyable.
- Inventory was enhanced but still feels unfinished, don't quite feel right, lacks many things.
- There's no real "Classification" of the game, no one really knows what the game is meant for.
- DLC's are just another ridiculous way to steal your money for an unfinished game.
- Anti-cheat is close to nonexistent, I've had plenty of experiences with cheaters
- Map design isn't very unique (Arma 2 was better)
- Weapon play is clunky and needs fixing
- The damage system is way off.
- Audio sometimes sounds cheap
- Graphics are OK, in a lot of the textures you can literally see the pixels!
- Performance is low-grade, a lot of work can be done.
- Server browser is ancient, the same browser from Arma 2 no major updates to it.
- Server performance is terrible, pings are usually through the roof ( I have FIBER connection)
- Banning legit players, it's happened to me twice luckily I've been unbanned, but still happens.
- No to little character customization
- Unfinished and overpriced (Especially the DLC's)
- Destruction system is something that exists but isn't very in-depth.
- Community relies on mods for fixing issues such as AI
- DLC's are released although most mods have already been created, it's just an "Official Mod"
(PROS)
- 25% of the cons fixed with mods (Community relies on Modders though!)
- VOIP systems are good, audio is great.
- Flight systems are great, flying a plane/heli feels finished and clean.
- Modding, if modding didn't exist this game would've died a long time ago.
- Weapon handling feels realistic, recoil, aiming etc...
- Game modes, DayZ/Epoch etc.. bring a lot to the table.
- Large player base, servers are usually full.
- Re-playability, you'll more than likely not get bored, especially with friends.
- The new launcher is great especially for sorting out mods.
- Installing mods is much easier now
- The mission editor is great, especially better than Arma 2's
- Mission making is much more in-depth from Arma 2
- The only worthy DLC IMO is APEX, others may differ.
- Mass amount of players in one server
- Can sometimes be immersive, especially playing with mates.
- Huge maps
- The user interface looks much cleaner and modern.
- Customizing weapons now (Really good on the devs part!)
(Videos)
(Issues)
My biggest issues with this game is AI & Performance
The AI in Arma 3 is coded in such a certain way that they run in linear paths/set coordinates.
This system is old, it was ported from Arma 2 with minor improvements.
For example, calling the command to form a line takes about 30 seconds to a minute.
The AI will walk in a line behind one another until each AI finds its Cords/Pos in relation to the leader.
The same goes for when climbing into vehicles, load up a mission, put down a squad and one helicopter. Give the command to "Get Into", and you'll notice they get into this line causing the whole system to take forever. Not to mention sometimes they forget where they're supposed to be, or that one r*tarded AI who refuses to get in.
The AI needs to be more dynamic, simply just needs to be more intelligent instead of relying on hard code that makes them so robotic, instead of human-like
As for performance
this game lack any type of optimization, and the sad part is, it's not that graphically intense.
This is one of the two biggest issues of the game if you Google "Arma 3" I can guarantee the index is filled with "How to get better FPS" or "Why is it so laggy?"
This has been a problem since Arma 1 and Arma 2, the devs have barely touched the subject.
I don't blame them as much, seeing as it's really the engines fault, they're using a terrible engine (RV4 Engine)
If you have a low-end machine DON'T BUY, it will be unbearable especially in multi-player.
For Reference I run 2x Asus GTX 970 Strix - i7 4790k @ 3.60GHZ 32GB DDR3 Ram
512 GB SSD
I usually run on Ultra and get 60FPS in singleplayer with a decent amount of AI
My FPS Will bounce from 30-60FPS in multilayer depending on a lot of factors.
You'd ask yourself "Well that's really good!" Yeah, it is, if you want to spend a♥♥♥♥♥♥load of money just to play this game.
Back in the day I use to run an R9 280x with some AMD CPU I don't remember, on average I got 20 - 45FPS never capped 60FPS.
Be warned - This game is CPU intensive, you can have a GTX 1080 and it will still run like♥♥♥♥♥♥
(Score)
Overall I give the score of 6/10. This game has so much potential already seeing as it's the only game offering this type of playing field. If the devs would just fix half of this♥♥♥♥♥♥especially performance and AI I would totally recommend this to anyone!
(Discussion)
In reply to some people "If you logged 3000 Hours on it then how can't you recommend it?!"
As I've stated I love this game, but the simple fact is the mass amount of consumers who have never touched the Arma series will look at it like "What the flying F*CK?" **Extended review incoming.**
First of all I will address what I believe are the surface principal advantages and disadvantages of the game, for whoever's considering buying it.
- When you buy this you essentially get the following: the main game, the Justine expansion, a sum of short stories in PDF form, developer commentary and "super secrets", and any number of custom story mods that you can find and add to your game. All in all, even though Amnesia is not great for multiple playthroughs, the mods and expansions guarantee that you get to spend loads of time playing! I got this for £15, and I have to admit I can't say that it wasn't worth the price at all, since it provides you with loads of entertaining and interesting content that other equally priced games won't provide.
- Unless your computer is absolutely compatible with all of Amnesia's requirements, the game is bound to freeze more or less frequently. For me, whenever Amnesia froze, it froze largely while loading new levels, or when something needed to load while I was already in the level. However, at least in my case, it's nothing that closing and restarting the game from the savepoint won't fix. I do not believe that these occassional freezes will inhibit you from playing the game from beginning to end and getting the full experience. That said, everybody's computer is different.
Now on to some more specific commentary.
In my eyes, Amnesia: The Dark Descent is more or less a classic of modern-day horror games, an example of how horror should be!
Initially, I'd like to praise the amazing physics and interactions with objects in-game. All movement, from your character's strolls to the handling of a crate, is rather fluid. Being able to to hold, examine, rotate, throw, push etc pretty much any object in Amnesia feels rather natural and gives the player a feeling of freedom. It is with that same freedom that the player has to decide whether and where to hide every time a monster appears. In Amnesia, the player's actions and decisions in response to stimuli (such the appearance of a monster, or being locked in a cell, or saving a prisoner) are not really predestined; you can choose what to do and how to do it. The storyline is mainly linear, however the player can add variety to the way he goes about following it, and thus the story doesn't feel burdensome.
Just like in all games, there is a protagonist and an antagonist, as well as maybe a few other characters, crucial to the story. In Amnesia, the depth of those characters is indeed capitalised on. For example, a lot of emphasis is given on the protagonist's psychology at any given point in the story, with his actions reflecting how he feels. A lot of controversy stems from the fact that in the game it's not particularly easy to distinguish good from evil. That is, you as a player are not sure whether you should feel sympathy for the main character or the antagonist, or find both of them outright evil because of the ways they approach their goals.
Being predominantly an atmospheric psychological horror game, there aren't many jumpscares to be found, and when they do happen, they usually don't involve the sudden appearance of a monster, but rather, a sudden flashback or a sudden sound. Which means that yes, Amnesia is not going to make you scream out of nowhere in the middle of the night as your family is sound asleep. Instead, focus was put on making the game very immersive and hence the player has to crawl through claustrophobic narrow spaces, walk in pitch black dungeons, and helplessly hide, while listening to  the game's splendid ambience and screams, moans and knocks implying the presence of terrors.
To make the game less likely to actually discourage players from playing because of its high scare factor+high complexity, Amnesia also opts for generally easier gameplay. That is, the puzzles are not too complicated, and as a player you may never even need to look for a walkthrough. The developers made sure to give you plenty of room for you to use your imagination to solve a puzzle, and if that doesn't work, hints and visual-audio clues will help you even further. The monsters you encounter, although terrifying, will not be too hard to ward off as long as your hide tactics are on point despite the panic attack induced by their moans after, say, you opened that door.
TL;DR: To finish off this large review, the main points I'd like to make about the game are the following:
- The graphics and physics in the game are marvellous, which screams that Amnesia is a well-made game as a first impression.
- The game's storyline is very interesting and thought-provoking, and the player has lots of freedom of movement and action within it. The characters' psychology, decisions and actions are the primary focus.
- Amnesia is guaranteed not to give you a jumpscare-induced heart attack since it pretty much lacks jumpscares. Instead it relies on the story, the environment, and the soundtrack to give you the creeps.
- And finally, considering how scared it makes you feel already, it opts to make progressing through the story easier for the player by introducing relatively easy puzzles and manageable enemy monsters.

is a popular game in the making. Movement feels tight. Lighting is gorgeous. Sounds are immensely satisfying. Don't be fooled by the Early Access tag:
is already a blast, and it can only get better.
To start:
's strength lies in the fact that any game mode is possible. The mainstay, of course, is Guards and Thieves. Guards defend six objects, but only one is the Thieves' target. In a battle of misdirection, it's a tense standoff where sharp timing is key. Classic gametypes execute perfectly in
, but the game's core is so strong that the devs can (and do!) experiment.
As you'd expect, each class has strengths & weaknesses. Cobras are quick and strong with terrible HP. Juggernauts are strong with high HP but painfully slow. You'll have preferences based on your playstyle, but all classes are fun and effective. Many more classes are on the horizon: Sniper, Engineer, Hacker, etc. Also on the way are "Gadgets", a wide variety of tools to customize loadouts.
The game centers heavily on its lighting. For Thieves (and Zombies), their main advantage is night vision. For Guards, it's a constant struggle to keep the map well-lit. Bright red light switches line the walls. When switched off, Thieves can impose their advantage. A suddenly-dark room compels moments of risk / reward for Guards. Do I rush in, or consider the room "lost"? Darkness is dangerous territory. To counter, Guards have flashlights...but their beams are of little comfort.
When light is scarce – which it often is – you need to locate action with your ears. The rustling of a bush. A distant knife swing. A shattering window. Since the game's sounds are so useful, verbal communication (not incl. in-game) is a borderline disadvantage. It's a bizarre feeling at first, but it works very well. As an alternative to voice chat, holding Mouse 3 brings up a radial menu with commands like
and
. Text chat is always an option too, mostly used while dead on the floor.
's biggest stumble is currently a lack of dedicated servers. When you want to play, sometimes you can't find a server that works – let alone one on the same
. Dedicated servers are in-progress, but the simple fix is: more players! More players = more player-hosted servers. So, ultimately, a Steam release alone should go a long way to address its main issue.
In my opinion,
is a powder keg of potential. Even in its current form, it's an absolute ton of fun with friends and strangers alike. With a solid core and great features on the way, there's simply no reason to pass it by. Get in on the ground floor and let's go!

Let me begin by saying that I hardly take the time to write reviews. Not even on games that I adore heart and soul. This game, however, has forced me to give fair warning to anyone who may be interested, because it can be hard to find clear answers around both the love and hate this game has. I'm no authority, and this is no expert critique, but it is my opinion.
In truth...I liked this game quite a bit. As both a roleplayer, history buff, and all around nerd, the concept of this game instantly had allure. It also didn't help that me and my gaming group are all seasoned veterans of Warband's PW modification, so it was destiny that we would end up playing this game. My friend bought me a copy (#poor) so that I could join them on this game. At the time, I had been on the fence about getting it, as the reviews were mixed and I had heard many bad things. I was convinced because the friends who had been playing had already enjoyed it immensely.
So why can I not recommend this game if I liked it? Well, I have seen many complain about the time it takes to do something worthwhile, or about the combat system. My issue is with none of these, but insteads sits with the developers and overall state of the game itself. When I started playing, the game was a buggy mess, albeit a fun buggy mess. Over half a year later... it's STILL a buggy mess. Furthermore, the game lacked many requested features and felt a bit bare. It is still lacking a vast majority of these features and feels bare. Back when the first of my friends started playing, it might surprise you to learn that the game was actually a bare, buggy mess!
You get the point. The game has issues, but the problem is that so little of those issues are being actively resolved by the developers. To add insult to injury, they have decided to go ahead and release a new game. Clearly, we can see where their time and effort has gone the last year or so...and it wasn't towards this highly unfinished product. They have for a long time planned and talked and announced news towards an MMO, apparently the intended version of this game. Many are excited for this. However, I'm not sure how they can pull of a successful MMO when they have yet to get anywhere near finishing a game that still costs 40$. Now, there is talk (albeit rumors) that they have partnered up with a company that specializes in micro-transactions.
I could go into more detail, but the bottom line is that the progress and work put forth towards this relatively expensive beta (mind you the game is labeled 'fully released') has been nothing but disappointing, and I do not see it getting any better. As we get further and further on, it seems more or less like a cash-grab by the devs, or at the very least a passion that has died down. Really, this is just another case of a larger disease plagueing our recent gaming world, but it unfortunately claimed such a fantastic idea as it's victim.
Save your money: wait for Bannerlord or splurge on CKII DLC. You'll avoid the sadness of a great idea unfinished.
